review_text:
The newest restaurant from Jean Georges in the ABC empire is all vegetarian, but just as good as the others. It's one of those rare vegetarian restaurants that makes you not really miss that there's no meat in your meal.

They have pastries and a coffee bar up front, as well as a full service restaurant toward the back of the large, beautiful space. The croissants and other baked goods are vegan, and while you can definitely taste the absence of butter, they are still delicious when you get one freshly made.

The large menu has so much great stuff, lots of which you wouldn't expect to be so incredibly delicious. Standouts from the small dishes include the Wood Roasted Beets ($13) and the Market Carrots ($11), which are slathered in an amazing nut and seed butter. For the larger ones, definitely try the the Dosa ($14) and the Fresh Spinach Spaghetti ($18). I will definitely be back soon to try dinner and more of the great options at breakfast and lunch.

They ignore emails and are closed weekends, and despite no line it took 6 minutes from signing my receipt (which listed a 'Pain Au Chocolate') to receive a single pastry, and the $4.36 pain au chocolat (dairy version*) was so dense and un-flaky (albeit with a fair bit of good chocolate) I'm convinced it was the vegan one. It's a nice space with the healthy ABC bent that you can get behind.

*Seems they have no-meat/non-vegan and vegan items here, with vegan alternatives to all items where a non-vegan one exists.

First of all: complimentary bread.

Second of all: Pink Decor. 

Third of all: To all my vegan homies with omnivorous friends- this. Is . it. This is where you go to prove vegan food is just, and even more delicious than meat and dairy. My Michelin loving, burger eating boyfriend said this was the best food he's ever tasted in his entire life. Ever. 

Dinner:

Wood Roasted Beets (5/5)
This one impressed us both. We've both had so many beets in our lives and whatever they did to these badboys is out of this world. The mini pickles and the cream on top and bottom just added to the sweet beet flavor.

Wild Mushroom Burdock Noodles (5/5)
Strong, delicious, woody, earthy, mushroomy.

Whole Artichoke (5/5)
The herb dipping oil!!! If it wasn't for my boyfriend probably being embarrassed, I would have just drank it.

Fresh Spinach Spaghetti (5/5)
These came in a garlicky broccoli bread crumb sauce. Happiest I've ever been about garlic breath. FYI you can request the cheese on the side.

Soft Custardy Tofu (4/5)
I LOOooooVED this texture and there was none of that raw tofu flavor to it. However, there was one strong herb taste that overpowered the dish and our nostrils a bit. I'd still order it again ;)

Dessert:

Vegan Matcha Crème Brulee (5/5)
So delicate so cute so beautiful. I ate half before I remembered to take a picture. Also they wrote Happy Birthday in chocolate and lit a candle because it was my Birthday!

Vegan Chocolate Mousse (4/5)
The mint crumble at the bottom made it. But the white blob at the top, what I'm guessing might have been whipped cream, was sour and distracted from the delicious chocolate.

Cocktails:

Pear and Rose: this alcoholic juice complemented the lunch so nicely. And it was pink!
Cynar Negroni: NO. so bitter.
Root and Rye: kinda like a upscale root beer with good whiskey

 

TL;DR: Everything blew my mind here.

What a stark contrast to the old space when it was Pipa Tapas Bar. A bright interior and friendly staff welcomes you as you enter the what-seems-like a Town & Country set for breakfast or lunch (for now, no dinner service). The vegetarian menu seems to be peppered with Indian-inspired dishes. Tried the dosa with Swiss chard, fried egg and zaatar. This was light yet filling and satisfactory. Also tried the kitchari yogurt with mint, fermented carrot and turmeric. Unfortunately this dish was bland and could've used additional spices. The baked goods were really good. Tried the breakfast cookie, einkorn muffin which tasted like bran, matcha muffin with fresh blueberries (yum!!!) and the morning glory muffin which tasted like carrot cake (my favorite!). So fresh and moist! I would love to follow the baked goods menu and enjoy more of them!

What an amazing new spot. Absolutely love what thy have done with the decor! Clean and fresh. Went for breakfast and had the wonderful vanilla chia bowl and the matcha muffin. My friend had the sea buckthorn bowl which was a unique smoothie bowl. Overall absolutely amazing. Can't wait to go back to try everything else (especially the dosa; want to see how they put their spin on it)

Have been recently for takeout (veggie bowl and kale avocado cucumber sandwich) which was very delicious, and finally made it to the restaurant which was unbelievable:

Wood roasted beets -- incredibly tangy and tasty, loved everything about this. Wound up putting beets on/soaking up leftover dressing with the dosa.
Dosa -- my friend and I tried both the coconut yogurt (Anita's Yogurt is a favorite!) and cashew (house made) yogurt for toppings. The fermented lentil dosa pancake was absolute perfection.
Wild mushroom burdock root noodles  -- so hearty and flavorful, would have never thought to order this but am so glad we did. The tempeh was excellent.

Also a huge fan of their einkorn muffin at the takeout counter (which I took home to toast and slather with ghee), and they make a mean coconut milk matcha.

Love the overall aesthetic, plates and utensils are wonderfully curated, service was great.

Save room for dessert, we regretted being too full to order a treat. Next round...

Not a big fan of vegetarian restaurants, but this place was truly great.  The homemade hot sauce on the table goes great with everything, especially the amazing lettuce wraps and cauliflower.   Make sure to try the lentil soup, and don't forget to eat your carrots :)

5 for the food as I am huge fan and have been here at least a dozen times since they opened. Their dosa is amazing and more authentic than any Indian restaurant in new york!

However zero for the attitude of the management. Often times there are so many tables open and yet they seem to say they are reserved. I waited half an hour and saw no one claim them! There is some thing to serve a loyal customer especially when 50 percent of your tables are empty. I detest restaurants that have this attitude- where they are too good for you. So not approachable - you cannot even call anyone if you want to make a change
I am a vegetarian. Spectacular and original food. Great ambience. Good service. Good cocktails. If you go there try the dosa, beetroot, carrots and labne!

I have been to pretty much every vegan restaurant in NYC with the exception of a few in Brooklyn and I can confidently say that ABCV is the best vegan restaurant in New York City. I will always love Dirt Candy, Avant Garden, and the Candle spots but ABCV reigns supreme.

The aesthetic of the restaurant is modern and clean with lots of white which immediately create a tone that is much different than other vegan restaurants in the city...or America for that matter. The only place that is more visually appealing in terms of vegan restaurants if Full Bloom in Miami because you have a great view of the water...however, the food at Full Bloom does not compare to ABCV's.

The best part of ABCV was being able to taste the freshness and quality of all of the ingredients in each dish. Without putting an overwhelming amount of spices, oils, or frying, ABCV is able to use simple and flavorful ingredients to curate all of their delicious dishes. My biggest complaint in NYC (other than winter) has always been that I felt food was fresher in Los Angeles, well NOW I can't say I know a restaurant in LA with fresher tasting food than ABCV.

My favorite items on the menu include:
Fried wild rice
Pine nut and lemon dip
Spinach spaghetti
Lentil soup
Green chickpea hummus
Avocado lettuce cups
Beluga lentils
Roasted cauliflower
Coconut sticky rice
Spring vegetable dish on takeout menu

...I basically just named the entire menu. Everything's great and fresh!
Food was awesome! Definitely get the whole (or half) cauliflower with pistachios on top! Also the Rose flavored lemonade was awesome

Amazing!!! AMAZING! AAAAMMMMAAAZING! 

I wouldn't expect anything less from a restaurant by Jean Georges. The restaurant is very similar in style to ABC kitchen and has a clean simple decor. 

The food is fabulous with one dish better than the next. By far the favorite of the table was the roasted whole cauliflower and I would just order as many as there are people at your table because this is one dish you Do not want to share. The amazing sauce that's accompanied with this dish is a side dish all on its own. 

The carrots with seed butter was also another phenomenal taste which we could not get enough of. The seed butter was perfection and something I will dream about. 

The desserts were also nothing short of spectacular and the table favorite was the coconut custard which was creamy and delicious!

The theme of the night for a first time experience: overdoneness. While the ambiance and staff remains notoriously amazing as their ABC counterparts, the food left much to be desired. The Wild Mushroom Burdock noodles and the roasted cauliflower were both overcooked with none of the crispy texture one would expect with burdock or cauliflower. The chanterelle, chickpea hummus, and roasted beets starters were forgettable to say the least. I barely remembered that my party ordered those even though was less than 24 hours ago!

This review only represents my opinion of a dinner experience. Perhaps lunch would be more memorable. As it is still new, here is to hoping that ABCV irons out their kinks in the next few months. I still have faith.

A big thanks to the hostess that held our table for 30 minutes after the scheduled reservation time!

Ambience: 5/5
Food: 3.5/5
Service: 4/5

As with the other ABC restaurants, the ambience is fantastic. The minimalist white decor is a stunner, and a very pretty backdrop for the very pretty dishes. Perfect for a mid-upscale dinner date. I grabbed bar seats because there was a 30 min wait, but the bar is spacious and they were great at timing out plates to come out 1-2 at a time. 

I LOVED the dosa with yogurt, avocado and sprouts. The dosa is crisp on one side and slightly chewy on the other, a little sour from the fermentation, and is so good with the creamy avocado. I also highly recommend the fresh spinach spaghetti, which can probably trick the pickiest vegetable eaters. The green pasta has a great chewy texture, and the way the veggies work with a bite of lemon and a salty parmesan just makes them absolutely delicious. The chanterelles were disappointing, a little sad and uninspired - an expensive ingredient that looked tiny on the plate and could've been dressed up a little. The coconut sticky rice was spiced and a little funky, more flavorful and less sticky than one you'd get at an Asian restaurant, with a thin bruleed top. The roasted cauliflower is good but not as amazing as I'd hoped. I would've preferred a crisp texture on the outside. The sauce could've had more punch. Half a head was plenty for 2. 

I admire the creativity of the menu, making vegetables exciting with preparations/flavors inspired by all kinds of cuisines. It's pricey, but the quality of the ingredients is excellent and also it's a JG restaurant. If they make some tweaks so that all the dishes are on par with the dosa and spaghetti, abcV would be a restaurant worth visiting again and again.

The food deserved four stars, but our service was so offensively bad.

It took over 20 minutes for someone to come by for our drink order.  Our server was like, oh, it looks like you are ready to order everything, which yes, it took over 20 minutes before anyone came over so we had plenty of time to look at both menus.

Those drinks (a glass of wine and simple cocktail) didn't even come out til our final course.

Nor did the bread.  Though other tables got right away, and we had said yes when server asked, we didn't get any until we were finishing up our mains, when he must have heard us talking to each other quietly about how they didn't even do that.

Twenty minutes after they cleared plates, we hadn't been asked about dessert or offered menus, so we finally flagged our server for the check.

No apologies, and I still tipped 20% as always.  I know it is a new restaurant, but they weren't giving a still-getting-our-act-together discount.  I was totally embarrassed to have made a reservation to celebrate a birthday with a friend here.  Should have stuck with Dirt Candy.
Loved everything I had. Fried rice, lentil soup, protein smoothie and coconut custard. All were great. Cool vibe. Busy but friendly staff. I'll be back.

I was pleasantly surprised after how satiated I was after sharing 4 tapas here. (3 would have been just enough!)

Dosa with yogurt and avocado- admittedly I ordered this plate for the photo opp. An extra large crepe made of lentils is served in a cone shaped plated with lemon accented yogurt and avocado. The combination of all the flavors made this my favorite dish.

Shallot labneh This was my second favorite dish. Using the same yogurt but this time flavored with mint and an oregano-like spice and drizzled with olive oil was very good. Root chips and cucumbers were served to dip into the yogurt. 

The white asparagus was something I never had before and it was interesting with the vanilla bean flavor- you can actually taste it. However this dish was too salty in my opinion leaving me to not finish it.

Fresh steamed tofu-This tofu dish was not what I was expecting based on its name. Rather the tofu is extra silly served in a bowl with  ponzu sauce to drizzle over it. It was interesting and I didn't not like it, but I wouldn't get it again. 

We sat at the food prep bar as couldn't get a reservation even for an early 6 pm. Sitting here was fun though as get to watch them prep the delicate dishes. Service was good though adamant about keeping our dining area clear so many times attempted to remove dishes we were still eating from. 

Selection of elixirs and kombuchas Id like to come and try. Also I think their brunch menu would probably be delicious

We enjoyed a good meal, but didn't love every dish and were expecting better considering the hype and lengthy wait for a table.

The cauliflower was my favorite dish.  It was crispy on the edges and flavorful on its own, even without the delicious cheesy sauce.  The pomegranate and pistachios were also a nice touch.

The beets were simple but delicious as well. The chili aioli and pickles went well with the dish.

The burdock noodles were also very fragrant and flavorful.  Only thing we didn't like was the tempeh, which had a strange, mushy yet crumbly texture.

The whole artichoke was pretty good with the olive oil dip, but the dip alone was pretty salty.

The chickpea hummus and pine nut and lemon dips were okay, but not that memorable, except that there were very few pieces of pita and a lot of vegetable crudités.

I had high hopes for the spinach spaghetti, but found the flavor to be too tart.

The dosa also didn't taste too authentic.  It was ever so slightly on the thick side, which meant it was on the doughy/chewy side and not crispy enough.  We got it with the avocado and sprouts, which were fine, but they were served on the side and not wrapped inside the dosa, so it felt like a random pairing to me (why avocado and sprouts with dosa, other than everyone loves avocado?).

Anyway, overall nothing was bad, but I'm not sure this would be at the top of my list to try again.

came here last night for dinner and ordered a bunch of plates to share, but wasn't completely stuffed by the end of dinner.  most of the dishes were pretty good, but my faves were the labneh and beets.  thought the dosa with yogurt and avocado lacked flavor, although the presentation was nice.  the whole roasted cauliflower, lentils, and spinach spaghetti were pretty good.  overall, had a pleasant experience, but not somewhere i'm dying to go back to.

Boo... what a disappointment.  Am a fan of JG and all of his establishments.  AbcV fell flat.  Also, heads up: this is clearly a restaurant that caters to the cocktail/spritzer clientele and should not be a destination for those seeking wine.  The wine list did not seem well thought out and nothing seemed to pair well with the menu.  When we asked questions about several of the bottles on their list neither our waitress nor the 2 others (whom she dubbed "more well-versed" in wine) could help us.  If you're looking for a sommelier to help you find the most ideal pairing of beverage to food, it's not here.  And i am NOT a wine snob nor one who claims to remotely know anything about wine (that would be my dining companion) but it was painful to see everyone scrambling to find someone to talk to us about the wine list, which begs me to question who compiled the list in the first place.

The food was an even bigger letdown.  I always enjoy the ambiance and food at Abc Kitchen and Abc Cocina but aside from the green chickpea hummus w/crudite there was nothing else on their menu that was appealing to my palate (and I eat EVERYTHING).  The menu and descriptions of each dish and the beautifully illustrated insert did little to distract me from how unbalanced everything tasted.  The roasted cauliflower that everyone raved about was so over-blanched (or steamed) prior to its brief stint under the flame that although the exterior had a beautiful nice char, once you cut into the dish it fell apart and was complete mush (texture not unlike baby food).  The avocado lettuce cups, while pretty, were again, texturally a fail.  I am not sure why a huge chunk of roasted sweet potato was added to this dish.  While i love sweet potatoes, the addition of the soft tuber to the soft avocado in a soft butter lettuce leaf cup (which, in general, does not provide any crunch) made each bite a squishy mouthful of  flavors that i found did not work well.  The sweetness of the sweet potato overpowered the rest of the ingredients.  I am a huge fan of all things mushroom, and the 3 dishes we tried were all disappointing.  The shitake dish and the morel/crimini dish were swimming in so much vinegar that's all you could taste.  I appreciate the distinct flavors of the various types of mushrooms out there and when cooked and prepared properly, are extremely enjoyable to eat.  All I tasted was vinegar.  The morel wontons were unimpressive.  The filling was undercooked in my mind and chewy, while the broth again was laden with so much vinegar that i could not enjoy the star of the dish.  The fresh spinach spaghetti dish was being ordered left and right, so i thought it only appropriate to try it as well, seeing that the pasta seemed to be popular that evening.  Unfortunately there was no balance of flavors and the preserved lemon completely overpowered everything else in the dish.  Sad, because i love spinach pasta (couldn't taste the spinach), I love broccoli, love kale, love garlic, love cheese and love saffron.  Could not taste ANYTHING except preserved lemon.  I did order the dosa for "educational purposes" and thank God i did.  It helped cleanse my palate after every overdose of vinegar and preserved lemon that hit my tongue.  

Aside from the food and beverages, we had an awesome waitress who worked her ass off and was so sweet and helpful and kind.  My less-than-impressed experience at abcV was in no way her fault.  She was the best!  I just wish I could have left without the need to erase the memory of the distorted flavors off of my palate via chicken McNuggets.  (No joke.  I was seriously contemplating a quick swing by McDonald's).  

Needless to say unless something changes in the menu at abcV (both food and wine) I highly doubt I will ever step foot in here again.  My experience there in no way diminishes my appreciation and "like" for abc kitchen and abc Cocina.  

Pretty ain't pretty no more if it ain't delicious on the inside.
Lunch was spectacular!!! Mushroom and barley soup was best ever.!!! Hummus heavenly!!! Loved the ambiance and service was great! Look forward to returning!
Beautiful, Delicious and as Excellent as it gets - drinks to desserts and every moment in between.

I am not a big fan of veggie, so I possess a natural bias against vegetarian food. Not that I dislike the concept, but I just feel less satisfying after a meal without meat.

We came in a bit after 8, the earliest possible time we could secure a table. Menu was quite extensive, from light plates to warm dishes. We shared a couple, morel mushrooms, roasted cauliflower being my favorite.

The coconut sticky rice was ok yet not fantastic. Too bland. 

In general, I would prefer ABC Kitchen or Cocina, the two other down-to-earth type of places. Vegetarians, please come and try your luck on it!

I visited ABCV a few weeks ago to meet a girlfriend and I thought we were actually going to the original ABC kitchen (that I love and adore!)  but she's vegetarian and decided to choose ABCV. I was really nervous at first because I didn't think there would be anything on the menu that I liked... surprisingly from the moment I sat down I really enjoyed every minute there! 

Throughout the evening we enjoyed the spinach spaghetti (soo yummy!) the roasted cauliflower (I can't even describe all the seriously amazing flavors they came up with in this dish) and to top it off a few cute little appetizers that the chef sent out to us courtesy of the kitchen! Oh! We also ended our meal with an amazing chi latte.  

If you're not into vegetarian restaurants please give this one a chance !

You are what you eat, or so the saying goes. And luckily more restaurants are providing beautiful, nutritious offerings that us feeling refreshed and nourished. Such is the case with the latest concept by Jean Georges in NY. Healthy, plant based food reigns supreme here. Not every dish was perfect, but there were so many incredible sounding items and unlike most restaurants, you leave feeling good about what you've put in your body. 

We shared many things from the hummus to the dosa to the carrots and cauliflower. 

Highlights for me were the carrots, beautifully roasted and served with stone ground nut and seed butter, chilis and limes, this was excellent and I particularly loved the crunch from the nut and seed butter. 

The dosa was also yummy, but more than anything a gorgeous presentation with avocado, yogurt and sprouts (note the yogurt is not dairy free). 

Fried wild rice was colorful and full of healthy items such as mushrooms, carrots, asparagus and cilantro, but was not my favorite dish. 

Green chickpea hummus could have been a bit creamier but I loved the peas sprinkled throughout. 

Cauliflower is supposed to be one of the best dishes here, and yet I found the texture mushy and over cooked. 

Vegan coconut custard and sorbets were an excellent way to end the meal. 

Next time I'd try new things and order the carrots again since they were my favorite!
Went here after work, the place is beautiful, lot of space, service very attentive and most importantly great food!

I absolutely loved all of our dishes here. They were quaint, flavorful, and pleasantly served. The  pine nut and harissa with dried apricots was so refreshing. The avocado lettuce cups were a skip to me - I didn't find anything in there that made them unique enough to choose over another dish. The wontons and the tofu were delicious. We also got a mushroom dish but now I can'r remember what is was. So, we have a couple cocktails and 5 dishes to share. The portions were so small, and so expensive for what they were, that...while it was a palate pleasing experience, we asked ourselves, "So what should we have for dinner?" This is not a joke. When we left, we paid out $150 dollar bill and then picked up a sushi roll when we went grocery shopping

You just can't go wrong with any items that you choose on the menu! Very flavorful very healthy and creative, no mediocre in their dictionary. Dishes are to be shared, for two people order at least 8 dishes.

ABCV is everything I hoped to find at other similar vegetarian restaurants. Dishes here taste light, but are rich enough to be filling. Plates are small and are meant to be shared. 

We had the pine nut and lemon, beet salad, cremini and morel mushrooms, spinach spaghetti, and fried wild rice. We also tried the housemade rosewater and blackcurrant sodas and the grapefruit granite and coconut custard desserts. I loved that everything tasted extremely fresh, and that other flavors didn't overwhelm the taste of the vegetables. The cremini and morel mushrooms were the standout for me - the morel mushrooms were amazing soaked in the sherry vinegar. The fried wild rice is also fantastic.

Hands down the best vegetarian restaurant I've been to in NYC.

Reservations are difficult here, but we were able to walk in and get seats at the bar immediately.

Food is pretty good, but nothing that blows you away -- something about the quality of the ingredients just aren't to the level that leaves a lasting impression. 

-The labneh was really well done -- probably the only dish I will remember from this place. 
-Complimentary bread is good. 
-Cauliflower is an interesting mix of flavors that work well together. 
-Green spaghetti is more like a salad with a few strands of pasta, something felt like it was missing to make this dish really pop. 
-Seasonal dessert pavlova was HUGE and yummy. Strawberries were a little too sweet.

Cocktails are decent, but not really refined speakeasy quality. 

Service was very attentive and friendly. Ambiance is clean and that mix of shabby/mod that is typical of ABC restaurants -- very pretty.

In a brief nutshell - it does not compare to it's sister restaurant (within the same building) ABC Kitchen (which has amazing food and plenty of options for vegetarians). As foodies living in the city, this was a first and last experience. On a scale of 1-10 I'd give it a 7. Service was friendly, ambience was fine, food was light and fresh but rather bland. Not worth the price.

Cute decor and food is pretty good for vegan (two stars for that), but they are very shady and overcharged us significantly. If you go there, make sure you keep track and look at your check very closely. I'm never going back.

The short: I don't usually frequent vegetarian spots, because I like meat (lol), but this restaurant was incredible. 

The longer: I accidentally stumbled in here for a work meeting (we were supposed to go to Kitchen), but on a Friday we were able to wait 15 minutes and get a nice table. 

The restaurant is bright, open & beautifully decorated - as I've come to expect with ABC Home. We decided to do the "taste of spring" chefs selection of dishes. 

I don't say this lightly: every single dish was delicious. From the hummus, to the stems & sprouts (my fav), to the fresh spinach pasta, cauliflower, veggie soup, sorbets & avocado lettuce cups... all the dishes were beautifully presented & you got tons of yummy food. It was totally worth the $38/pp.

Our waitress was super sweet and service was impeccable. Glad we stumbled in here and excited to recommend this spot to my friends!

On a whim, we booked a reservation for 10:30pm on a weeknight. I was excited to try this veggie-centric Jean Georges restaurant -- especially because the chef de cuisine hails from the sadly-closed but incredible-while-it-lasted Pure Food and Wine. 

I was ambitious with thinking I could make it to 10:30pm without eating, and I was definitely hangry. Apologies to the incredible company I had for the meal. Fortunately, the decor was beautiful. Airy and well-lit, the interior makes for a cheery atmosphere. 

Our waiter took a while to come around to check on us, and I feel like it took a long time for us to finally get someone to take our order. Other than that, I enjoyed the meal immensely. 

The menu was incredible, and as someone who hunts down good plant-based food, I was in heaven. We decided to do the chef's tasting plus the unmissable coconut sticky rice (which I highly recommend). Among our favorites: avocado lettuce wraps, warm crimini and morel mushrooms, and the whole roasted cauliflower. We all ordered various cocktails and juices, and they were delicious. 

Since I'm a dessert girl, I gotta mention the strawberry rhubarb pavlova. I love anything meringue, and this pavlova was light, crunchy, and delicious. Such a treat. 

I can't wait to come back!

Since the restaurant opened not too long ago, I have already been a few times and it gets better and better! I am not a vegetarian/vegan but I appreciate fresh and creative vegetable dishes which is exactly what abcv is about. 

The restaurant itself is inviting, fresh, bright and beautiful. There is a big dining room that makes you feel homey with a trendy vibe. 

Every dish I had was delightful and refreshing. I highly recommend the cauliflower, spinach spaghetti, green hummus, wild fried rice, carrots, beets, and shiitake mushrooms. The staff are friendly, upbeat and informative! Everything from start to finish was excellent and I can't wait to go back.

Had a great experience here! Came for breakfast on a weekday as it's impossible to get a reservation for weekend brunch. Loved the atmosphere, the food and the service!

FOOD: We ordered three dishes to share for two people: the sea buckthorn and mango bowl, einkorn pancakes, and wild mushrooms with poached eggs. All were fantastic! Tasted very light and fresh, but we were full. The bowl was so interesting, a little more out there but worth it if you like acai bowls. The pancakes were my favorite and were accompanied with a perfectly light coconut cream and compote. Mushrooms were delicious, though is a more common dish. 

DRINKS: We ordered the green juice and a kombucha. Wouldn't necessarily recommend, their juices are pretty overpriced and typical of what you'd get elsewhere. Would be interested in trying their elixirs though. 

SERVICE AND ATMOSPHERE: The place is simply adorable! Full of light and simply decorated. Everyone was very kind as well. We arrived late for our reservation and were still seated very promptly. Our server was very attentive and let us know when the kitchen was closing so we could place our order asap, and all the food came out very quickly (probably a function of the kitchen closing!). 

Overall, would definitely recommend and would definitely return!

KenScale: 8.0/10

When the crudité came out with green chickpea hummus, I was surprised at my wife Jun's gasp. She was looking incredulously at one of the turnips with dirt still not fully removed. "Is that what I think it is?" She protested to the server who then brought a new bowl of crudité, but it was clear that the damage was already done and Jun was rolling her eyes in disbelief the entire time. I mean, if a vegetarian restaurant, especially from the acclaimed chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten, doesn't even properly take care of the vegetables it serves, what good is it? I get how ABCV would probably be the hottest place to be right now given all the obsession of yoga pants wearing New Yorkers with vegetable dishes, but that doesn't give you license to be sloppy or even arrogant, right? My gripe with the restaurant actually started even earlier, when we showed up at 5:30 p.m. because the online reservation system didn't have prime times available, even one month out. We clearly saw the restaurant half-empty at that point, but somehow the maître d decided to seat Jun and I at one of the communal tables. "What the hell?" I thought to myself. I politely asked that we be seated at one of the regular tables, and they still offered the other side of the communal table they initially try to seat us. I finally had it enough and yelled at the staff leading us, "Who in the world gets to decide some people sit at a regular table and others sit at a communal table when clearly there are empty tables everywhere?" Only after that outburst were we seated at one of the regular tables overlooking the kitchen. With all these unpleasant experiences, was ABCV still worth it? I have always tried to make sure in my restaurant reviews that KenScale is based on food only, therefore leaving out extraneous factors such as services out of the equation. With that principle in mind, I would give a reluctant 8.0 to ABCV.

The menu at ABCV consists mostly of shareable vegetarian dishes. Give credit where credit is due; despite the disaster with crudité, Jun and I were both very pleased with the green chickpea hummus that had a mildly spicy kick to it. I regretted ordering the fresh sauerkraut with horseradish and dill (after all, it works best in a hot dog, not as a standalone dish!) for being overly citrusy, but had no complaint whatsoever about roasted cauliflower that displayed great texture and worked harmoniously with turmeric-tahini sauce on the side. I could definitely see myself coming back to the restaurant just for this dish. Other times, the results were a bit more mixed. We both thought crimini and morel mushrooms could've toned down on seasoning, but did like the wild mushroom burdock noodle for its balance on flavor with smoky feel to it (although Jun was utterly confused why they had to add pieces of soy-based tempeh on top). I didn't understand what they were trying to do with the spinach spaghetti with broccoli, kale and preserved lemon as the flavor was a bit too overpowering for me, and the texture was somewhat off, but Jun did appreciate the creativity behind the dish. I have to admit, though, that the desserts that we ordered were fantastic. The pavlova with strawberry and rhubarb at ABCV was quite outstanding and I would gladly call it one of the best dessert dishes I've had this year. The refreshing sensation from the dish and the textural effect from the combination of different ingredients was quite memorable. Vegan coconut custard with berries was another standout dish that I liked even more for not being overly sweet. The server also handed out chocolate mousse with mint chocolate crumble on the house to apologize for the crudité fiasco, but it was by far the weakest dessert among the three. 

Not surprisingly, getting a table at ABCV through the online reservation can be exceptionally challenging. If you're amenable to eating at 5:00 p.m., I suggest you just show up and try your luck at the bar area. The bright dining space looks like its chief mission is to appeal to all the New Yorker girls who want to look at only cute stuffs in the world. There is full bar with cocktails incorporating some elements of vegetable; not surprisingly, the wine list is heavily geared toward organic and natural varieties (another huge turn-off for us). On our way out, Jun succinctly put her experience (and I wholeheartedly agree) this way: "For food alone, this is borderline 8.0. In terms of overall dining experience, I think even 7.5 is a generous score." Let's see if these miscues can be fixed over time. Until then, ABCV is just another overhyped dream story for self-righteous locavores out there.

Oh, this place us just heavenly!!  We're not even vegetarians, and this was still one our best New York dining experiences in recent memory.  Everything is beautiful here--the food, the drinks, the decor, and the staff. Food standouts were the dosa, the shallot labneh, and the spinach spaghetti, DEFINITELY the market carrots with nut and seed butter, chiles, and lime.  I don't usually find myself singing praises of carrots, but this is a flavor mix worth tasting!  Cocktails--we sipped a cynar negroni and a matcha colada; delicious.

Had the pleasure of dining here twice lately. 
Made reservations for breakfast with friends, which was so good, I went again with my husband on the very same week. 
The decor of abcv is absolutely gorgeous. The photos don't do it justice. 
Everybody was so attentive and knowledgeable about the menu and the different ingredients (thanks, Akil!) and the food is everything a person with health and aesthetic consciousness could ask for (let alone a vegan). 
Absolutely beautiful dishes, one tastier than the other, full of flavor, and you can literally feel the vitamins going through your veins :)
Had almost everything on the breakfast menu. Particularly loved the wild blueberry bowl, the vanilla chia bowl, the kitchari and the congee. Almost every dish can be made vegan. 
Go go go.

Visited yesterday for a ladies lunch. Some of the food was delicious, particularly loved the avocado tacos and dosa. The vegetable salad w egg also solid but nothing revolutionary. You can also take out food from the front of the restaurant. The vegetable spaghetti was a miss.

I've been dying to check this place out since it opened a couple of months ago. I think all of the ABC restaurants are connected so you can stop by for some light shopping at ABC Home and Kitchen and then come here for dinner. Disclaimer I do love vegetables and they basically make up 80% of my diet so I'm kind of biased. 

I would recommend making reservations in advance although they do reserve some seats for walk in guests as well. I tried my luck and opted for walk in and was told that I could only get a seat at the bar. It's interesting that they don't reserve bar seats for you; the hostess actually told me I had to wait by a previous guests bar seat to claim it. IMO that's kinda terrible service cause regardless of the price point this is still a Jean George's restaurant. And as a customer, I don't feel comfortable standing by another guests seat bc they might feel pressured to leave. 

Aside from that shitty experience, there's a great menu with dishes all under $20. The bartenders are all super sweet and make great recommendations. I highly recommend the dosa - the quality is seriously on par with Indian restaurants if not better. The celery root is also cooked amazingly well and had such good flavors. The shallot labneh and spinach spaghetti were kind of mediocre. The flavors were a little one dimensional. The portions are pretty decent although if you're used to eating large amounts of meat/portions, you'll most likely need to order more dishes. 

The interior is also so cute! It's all white
- literally the floors walls and the chairs and tables are all white, but the lighting is really cute and it feels very homey. It's a nice mix between upscale food and casual dining. 

This is now one of my new favorite restaurants. Can't wait to try more dishes!

We did the tasting menu and it was an awesome value. Everything was ultra creative and delicious. I have a big appetite and left feeling very full but not uncomfortable ;) Having eaten at all of the top NYC vegetarian spots, I can say this is a welcome addition at the very top of my list. Also appreciated the vibe. Casual yet still very upscale in terms of service and atmosphere. Can't wait to go back. Only thing they could lose is the host's attitude

ABCV is an excellent addition to the now three-strong ABC series.  After Pure Food & Wine flaked out, there has been a paucity of high-quality vegan-vegetarian fare in the Gramercy area, and Jean-Georges clearly saw that unmet need in opening this restaurant.

The restaurant is well-lit with white walls and contemporary fittings, not to mention the small Ganesha idol perched on a stand, but hard to spot from a distance.  It is a fairly large space, with multiple formats of seating, including communal tables.  Quite the contrast from the rustic setting of the other ABC restaurants.

The bar offers an excellent selection of restorative tonics, organic juices and even kombuchas.  I tried the beta glow with carrot, lemon, orange and ginger and the lemon-ginger-cayenne-turmeric kombucha -- both excellent.  The food menu has an impressive variety of 30+ choices spanning hot dishes, noodles and rice, legumes and even dosa.  The complimentary bread was light enough to not vitiate the selections that followed.  I loved the white asparagus with hearts of palm, excellently presented with short sections of the asparagus bunched together.  The lentils with potatoes and broccoli stems was fairly good, but I could have done without the excess of chili oil and vinegar.  And the chocolate mousse was a worthy finish.  All said, the food would justify a four-star rating.

The one distasteful aspect of ABCV is the reservations.  Granted, I was a walk-in.  But the hostess estimated 20 minutes for a communal table and an hour for a regular table.  And I had waited for an hour and 30 minutes without being called for a table.  The hostess was all smiles (I find that extremely annoying) with no appreciation for what I was feeling.  I counted between five and ten unoccupied tables for the entire duration of my wait.  Why would they mindlessly wait for guests who made reservations to arrive when they could have offered me one of the tables, especially since I was told that I was the "only one waiting to be seated"?  I alerted the manager who magically found a cancellation that cleared a table for me.  Were it not for a significant escalation of commitment at that point (100 minutes for a table when you can clearly see plenty of open tables?!!!!), I would have left without dining.  I really think Jean-Georges and the management team would do well to find receptionists and front-office staff with a modicum of common sense and empathy.  Very disappointed.

The place is full of light and beautifully decorated. We had the shallot labneh and burdock noodles all delicious. Nice selection of organic juices.
It's the perfect place if you are a fan of ABC kitchen, but you have vegan friends.
Vegetarians will love it. A nice lunch place with a great variety of healthy options to choose from. Love their fresh juice specials!

I'm a bit skeptical about the ABC restaurants since I found Kitchen to be overrated and Cocina to be too salty/overpriced.  If their newest addition abcV wasn't revolved around couture vegetables, I probably wouldn't have considered going.  But, I love vegetables and am curious to see what trendy kitchens can do with them.  

I recommend going with a few people so you can share everything.  I have to say we ordered the perfect amount (about 8-9 dishes to share between 4 people) and it left us feeling full & satisfied with no room for dessert.  

The dishes at abcV were well-executed and we enjoyed all of them (maybe some more than others).  I don't need to go back for seconds but I do recommend all you veggie lovers out there give it a try!

Had a nice lunch at ABCv last week...

Ambiance is beautiful (all ABC restaurants are quite beautiful actually). The restaurant was freezing cold though, so I wish they could do something about the A/C.

Service was excellent and friendly. Food comes out as it's ready which is nice.

Food was overall quite tasty:

-- Dosa was delicious and fairly authentic, although it definitely needed the customary potato filling. It was expensive at $14.

-- Shallot labne received good reviews from my colleagues (I am lactose-intolerant so I didn't try this).

-- Fresh spinach spaghetti was good but the lemon flavor was a bit too prominent for my tastes. I wouldn't order this again.

-- Beluga lentils were delicious, I definitely recommend this dish.

Overall we had a great dining experience and although quantities are small, prices are fairly decent. I'll definitely return.
So far the best place I've ever been. Interior, service, kitchen.. EXCELLENT! 5+ stars ! Thank you Molly, you are very helpful and positive person , thank you for your vibes !

Better food could be bought in the cold food isle of Fairway for 1/20th of the price.   An added advantage of going to Fairway is you wouldn't have to put up with the rude waiters and waitresses who basically throw the food onto the table and run away.  Explanations as to what you are eating in the tasting menu are non existent.   The only reason the restaurant may survive is the hype and big name chef behind it.  Even the idea that you are eating healthy food that will make you feel better and healthier is a myth.  I can guarantee you will not feel bloated when you leave the restaurant because you probably will leave most of the food on the plate.

This restaurant can be described with one word: meh. We got five dishes total for a party of 2. The items that were tasty were the ganoosh and the morel mushroom warm appetizer, but certainly not worth more than 15 dollars each. If you get the ganoosh, beware it comes with 4 tiny pieces of pita, and they charged us 4 dollars more when we asked for some more to eat with the remaining ganoosh.  The other three items we ordered was the mushroom wonton, coconut rice, and spinach spaghetti. Starting with the mushroom wonton, there were only four pieces. In three of the four pieces, there was a weird hard piece - chef said it was part of the spring onion (cool, but why was it in my dish if it's not supposed to?). Coconut rice was so bland, tasted like mushy rice. Finally, our last dish was the spinach spaghetti. This dish was horrible - it was so salty, lemony, and tasted like something was just caught from the ocean. This place really isn't worth the money or time. There are so many better vegetarian places than this.

Even as omnivores, we really enjoyed the food on offer at ABCv.  Not that one would expect any less from an outlet in the Jean-Georges empire.  Food was full of flavor and executed so well, that at no point did we miss meat.  Would love to give this place a higher rating, but honestly the service fell flat and disorganized.  It took a particularly long time to get water, drinks, bill incorrect, etc.  Hopefully this can improve as the restaurant gets more experience.

Atmosphere
- Clean and modern minimalist design.
- Can get a bit noisy given all the hard surfaces.
- Lack of a real bar area upfront for early arrivals/waiting for others in party.  Issue is that the bar is full of diners packed tightly, and bar tenders were constantly busy.  Waited to get menu, ordered drinks, never came, gave up and went to table (20 mins).  They should ideally put diners at high tops behind the bar (two long tables went almost wholly unused!)

Food
Very good overall.  We began with the Pine Nut and Lemon Dip ($14) which had deep layers of flavor and deft use of spice from the harissa, very unique and great with cocktails - really enjoyed.  The Stone Fruit Salad ($16) was light and refreshing.  Beluga Lentils and Broccoli ($13) had just the right amount of heft.  Half Roasted Cauliflower ($14) arrived with an interesting turmeric tahini sauce served in a beaker, combined with the crisp cauliflower and pomegranate and pistachios made an interesting combination, would have loved a bit more pomegranate and tad more salt.  The Fresh Spinach Spaghetti ($18), which appears to be quite popular, had good bite but flavor profile is rather generic.  Even to a non-mushroom aficionado, the Wood Grilled Donko Shiitake ($19) had a captivating savoriness with caramelized fennel and yuzukosho green goddess.  To conclude, the Vegan Coconut Custard ($13) was good though unremarkable.  Overall, we were satiated though not too full with 3 dishes per person.

Beverage
In terms of cocktails, the Watermelon Blanco ($16) and Yuzu Gin & Tonic ($16) were both very refreshing and well balanced.  Others looked quite enticing as well.  With the meal, we enjoyed a bottle of 2014 Anthony Thevenet 'Morgan' Gamay ($52) which was of good value and reasonably priced.  Served a bit too warm, think it had been sitting out.  Wine list is well conceived with many offerings under $75, including a fair amount of solid options in the $40-50 range.  Just need to step up the service/storage.

Service
- Server(s) were polite and nice, they seemed simply overstretched, covering large sections.
- Took a long time to be acknowledged/get water, receive drinks, bill was incorrect and took time to fix, etc.
- Staff didn't seem to have much knowledge of what was in dishes.

I was treated shabbily by staff, seated away from others, ignored, had to demand a glass of water.  The dish I chose came on a butter dish.  I had to stop for food on the way home.  They also made me stand and wait when I arrived 10 minutes early.  I'm a senior by the way.

I eat a lot of veggies - my hubby - not so much. When a place can make my husband happy and satisfied without serving meat...WIN. Loved the room, the presentation, the plates, the service. We did have a reservation and came in early - 6pm. ABCv is now one of my favorite go to spots in the city.
food was amazing and i loved the ambiance. Got the tasting selection and split it with two other people.

I wish half stars were used on Yelp, because 3.5 would be more accurate, and 4 if our beginning experience wasn't so unwelcoming. I can't believe I'm rating a Jean Georges resto this, but sadly, we were unenthralled by numerous aspects of our dinner here on July the 4th, starting from our unfriendly host who sat us. 
Jean-Georges is my favourite celebrity chef and restauranteur. I've been to his restaurants in Miami, Vancouver and New York, and was so excited to try ABCV, being a huge fan of vegetarian cuisine. Upon entering the beautifully designed restaurant, the host sat us in a corner table right next to a table of four people very close to us, but the rest of the room was essentially EMPTY. It was 930pm on July 4th, so I knew we were likely the last seating, and as the night progressed, I was right. We asked to be re-sat to the other side where there was more privacy and literally so much empty space, and the host was visibly annoyed and flippant, and that was a very unwelcoming beginning to ABCV. I don't think our request deserved that response.
Moving on, our server was attentive enough, friendly and casual, and the support staff were all great, helpful and pleasant! 
The food - some plates were absolutely heavenly, and some were unfortunately, very average. We ordered the roasted cauliflower, and a stone fruit and soft cheese dish to start, and those were the best dishes by far. Many delicious flavours all complementing each other, absolutely JG styles! We then had the beluga lentils, spinach spaghetti and dosa with yogurt, avocado and sprouts, and those three were sadly nothing special. 
Dessert was also disappointing. We ordered the chocolate mousse, and I've had better vegan mousses at Whole Foods. Our cocktails were also grainy and a bit unbalanced in flavours - I didn't even finish mine, sadly.
Ugh, I love you so much, Jean Georges, but on that night, ABCV didn't deliver like you normally do!!
We had the best veggie meal last night! Great atmosphere, really delicious food - surprisingly good. We couldn't stop ordering different dishes to try. Will be going back again and again!

Used to LOVE this place for takeout from lunch. A delicious bowl of fresh veggies for $12 + tax (and I usually leave a dollar for tip) - on the high-end of what I like to spend for takeout, but produce quality, service and packaging were worth it.

On a recent trip back I discovered they have raised prices for the veggie bowl from $12 to $14, and for the soba noodle bowl from $12 to $16. That is a 25% increase! $20 for a takeout, vegetarian lunch is just too much. Back to Sweetgreen for me. ABCV, I will miss you :(

They are doing amazing things here with vegetables. The restaurant is sleek and stylish. Ate at the bar and had fantastic service. Enjoyed the carrots and dosa. The tonics are light and refreshing. A perfect summer meal

Quick review:

Hen of Woods (dinner special) - amazing
Carrots - amazing (trust me)
Spinach spaghetti - very good
Harisa - very good
Sweet corn with truffles - good but pricey
Roasted cauliflower - good 
Eight ball squash - good not great
Sticky rice - good not great - very sweet
Lettuce cups - pass
Market peas - pass (salad with a few peas)

Pros:

An inspired vegan place in NYC - a must, not everything was mind blowing, but loved plant/raw based focus over tofu, definitely try the lettuce wraps, other dishes lacked in flavor (but never in presentation)

Excellent service (we had the wonderful waiter, the one that just moved from CA, pardon me for forgetting the name)

Flowers on food, flowers on tables - perfection

Nod-worthy cocktails / wine

It's Jean-George 

Pros:

Hard to reserve - I feel like their tables are disappearing into Resy or something 

Extremely uncomfortable chairs at the bar and outside, if you are over size 4 don't even dare to sit at the bar - the butt fat you were not aware of possessing will hang over the seat edges to your discomfort and horror 

A part of the bar faces a very underwhelming area of a kitchen that looks like the back of a cafeteria and has busy grumpies running back and forth, we sat at the bar for a while before we realized no one was ever coming to wait on us so we relocated outside to experience a significant improvement in the level of service

The hostess did not provide menus - if you are casual enough to sit guests on evil bare wire chairs that beg for cushions, you are casual enough to give menus right at the sitting
This place is insane! I'm my newest favourite! Very fresh delish veggies with a imaginable twist!

It's alright. It's a must try place for vegans/vegetarian and it's always fully booked. The decor is simple and cute. But as a fancish place, sharing a table is kinda of weird. So basically it's a huge table and it cuts into three (2 people) with one seat empty in between. 

Okay back to the food and drinks. My friend doesn't like her matcha cocktail (given her love for matcha) it's a bad sign. My kombucha is like 1/3 filled for a wine glass (probably only 1 fl oz!!! given $12 price tag) I feel like I should just go buy one at Whole Foods or any other places for $4 with at least 12 fl oz. I don't know if the waitress is being lazy or what. It's very disappointing. The service is also lacking for my table ( other tables later than us for bread blahhhh and we have to ask). 


The food is alright small portion, very similar to Nix. It's divided into light and hot food. The cauliflower is the best dish out there. ( please order this) combined with tahini sauce, it's a bit crispy while soft. Other dishes: lentil ( nothing special) mushroom (like the plating). Zucchini hummus (2nd best here but not the best hummus I've had) picked cabbages with fancy name called s....sth (nah)z. I forget other things I order. But overall speaking, thanks for the nice design, it's a bit disappointing for $70 + per person and don't think I'll want to be back again.(there are way better plant based restaurants to go).

And if you come here, cauliflower!!

Wonderful birthday dinner with my husband at abcV. We had a Saturday night reservation for 9:30pm. The restaurant was filled but not overly crowded, soft enough so we could have a nice conversation. 

We decided to go with "a taste of early summer", their tasting menu. Everything was superb!

AVOCADO LETTUCE WRAPS:
- I felt badly that I forgot to inform the waitress when ordering that I don't like avocado or cilantro. When she brought out the avo lettuce wraps I coyly mentioned my dislike of the creamy green fruit. She didn't skip a beat, offered to replace the dish with something else, and left the dish for my husband, who thoroughly enjoyed the dish. 

CHARRED ZUCCHINI BABA GHANOUSH:
- Smokey, creamy and delicious! A nice take on the classic eggplant baba ganoush. The fresh pita (4 small quarters) was light and airy, with a purple tint. 

HEIRLOOM TOMATO SALAD
- This off-menu dish was the replacement to the original Avocado wrap. The tomatoes were extremely fresh, and complimented with hearts of palm and an unrecognized but very flavorful herb. The dish was probably the least-memorable, though still enjoyable. 

SLOW ROASTED BEETS
- Easily the most beautiful dish of the night. Magenta beet slices topped with an avocado aiole for a striking color contrast. Tiny pickle slices and capers accompanied the beets by adding bursts of salty crunch. 

CHILLED BEEFSTEAK TOMATO SOUP
- This soup was one of the more interesting dishes, complex in flavor; acidic from the tomatoes, with a good amount of heat, light and summary, with a nice crunch from the micro croutons. 

ROASTED CAULIFLOWER
- Crispy on the outside, soft on the inside. There were +15 easily identified ingredients used to create this dish. Personal favorite accompaniment was the pistachio nuts, however the waitress said it's best with pomegranate seeds (none that night). The turmeric tahini sauce added a nice nutty and creamy flavor. Highly recommend. 

RAMEN WITH TEMPEH AND MUSHROOMS
- I'm not a big tempeh person, definitely my least favorite meat-free protein, however I must say that this tempeh was out of this world!!! Fried and salty, you just can't go wrong. The charred noodles and green beans gave the dish a distinctive lasting taste. 

VEGAN MATCHA CREME BRÛLÉE (birthday dessert)
- Excellent! Strong taste of matcha with the traditional texture of creme brûlée. 

VEGAN COCONUT CUSTARD
- The sweetness of the coconut and the light airiness of the custard brought me back to my childhood dreams of being a fairy princess. Nicely complemented with fresh berries and what tasted like dehydrated strawberry dust. Also excellent!

STRAWBERRY RHUBARB PAVLOVA 
- Pavlova was delicious; airy yet crispy. However, compared to the other two desserts, this one  comes in 3rd. 

Overall excellent experience at abcV. Would recommend the tasting menu, as it takes the heartache out of deciding what on the menu to order. abcV definitely ranks on par, if not higher, than NIX and Dirt Candy in terms of experience and menu creativeness. We will be back.

Let me start off by saying I'm an omnivore, though I guess I lean more to the carnivorous side - I'm not a huge vegetable person. Still, the dinner here left me full and satisfied. I never felt like I was missing meat. 

I came in with two other people on a Saturday night and we opted to sit at the bar since we just walked in without a reservation. Our bartender Sal was awesome! He was friendly, funny, and gave us great recommendations: 
- Pine Nuts with Lemon, Harissa, dried apricots and pita: this was so addicting! It feels like a dip, and I almost drowned my pita in all of that deliciousness 
- Avocado lettuce wraps: a solid choice. As the menu describes, it is very light and fresh. 
- Roasted Cauliflower: the whole cauliflower was a good portion for the 3 of us. It also came with this great turmeric sauce on the side! 
- fresh spinach spaghetti: interesting. It looks like spaghetti but kinds tastes like salad! I definitely enjoyed it 
- strawberry rhubarb pavolva: one of my favorite dishes! I loved the sorbet, and the rhubarb/strawberries kept everything sweet (but also tart), and refreshing. Perfect way to end the meal

GO HERE! I was so reluctant to spend money here since I saw so many negative and 'eh' reviews for abcv and honestly - that is mind boggling to me! Being a vegan, I'm a little biased because I love veg food (but... abcv IS a vegetarian restaurant so if you come here as a big meat eater, don't decide right away that no matter what, you're not gonna be that into it since you didn't get a piece of meat in your meal; you knew what you were getting yourself into). 

I truthfully have tried a great majority of popular vegan/vegetarian restaurants in NYC and right now, abcv is the BEST that I've tried. Their use and combination of flavors, textures, and especially herbs and spices is unreal. The atmosphere is so artsy and well decorated, and the flowers and homemade hot sauce (!) containers--which are little vintage style teacups--on the tables are adorable. Our waitress was also so cute and nice, and the meals took virtually no time to reach our table. I wasn't expecting it to be this good due to the mixed reviews, but seriously.....

My mother and I had the 'taste of summer' lunch tasting for 2, which was $48 a person. We got a really decent amount of food for this price, so I was definitely pleased. I'm gonna be *that* person and list everything that was included in the tasting because I'm that obsessed with their food, but keep in mind - I requested that the tasting be vegan (they use dairy and eggs in some dishes) and also, abcv picks the dishes in your tasting, so yours may be different than mine. 

*Appetizers*

1.  Wood Roasted Beets - these were my mom's favorite. She loves beets. I hate them...but these were actually amazing. They didn't taste like dirt or have that weird iron-y scent; they were sweet and delicious. There were also tiny pickles on top - I also HATE pickles but enjoyed the taste of these!

2. Green Chickpea Hummus w/ Veg Crudite and Pita - this hummus was the freshest I've ever tried! It had edamame and Thai basil on top, and even some mint I believe. The pita was the best I've ever had - very hot and straight from the oven; so fluffy. The crudite was a mixture of fresh hand-picked veggies like radishes, beans, and lettuces. 

3. Beefsteak Tomato Gazpacho - this was a cold tomato soup, sooo refreshing. It was filled with baby tomatoes, chunks of fresh avocado, corn, dill (which I--again--usually hate but it was so fresh and tasty) and other spices. 

4. Market Carrots - roasted carrots on top of a homemade ground nut butter. The combination of savory carrot and sweet nut butter was incredible, and the addition of a few tiny chili slices and a slice of lime added great spice. 

*Entrees*

5. Half-Roasted Cauliflower - so yummy, as per the general consensus. The cauliflower was crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and even tasted cheesy despite it being vegan. Turmeric-tahini dressing was great, and I loved how the dish came with fun, flavorful additions like pistachios and pomegranate seeds. 

6. Wild Mushroom Burdock Noodles w/ Tempeh - Tempeh is foreign to a lot of people, but it is essentially just compacted soybeans that can be grilled, fried, sauteed, etc. and taste sort of like chicken or even bacon when cooked/seasoned correctly. But having cooked with tempeh so many times, I was so astounded how they managed to get the tempeh so thoroughly crispy and eliminate any bitterness. As for the burdock noodles, I've never had burdock before but the noodles were really good! Like long slices of a very thin, firm potato. And the mushrooms were so fresh and juicy, especially in the delicious brown sauce that everything was tossed in. 

*Dessert*

7. Chocolate Mousse - ultra-thick and creamy. Loved the mint crumbles as well as the coconut cream on top (which was slightly and perfectly sour to play off the richness of the chocolate). Came with a few gluten free sugar cookies which were surprisingly so soft and moist despite being gluten-free. 

8. Matcha Creme Brulee - 11/10. Just amazing. Probably my favorite thing I'd eaten at abcv. Just order it.

Beautiful space with an unexpectedly Indian slant to vegetarian fare. 

We walked in on an early Wednesday evening and learned quickly this isn't a drop in spot - front host was a bit abrasive and told us to watch the bar for a spot because "AbcV is booked to capacity for many days". Okay, not that I asked long term.

After about 80 minutes (we went to Abcocina for drinks to occupy our minds for some of this) we grabbed two spots at the bar and moved onto the food. We ordered Dosa with Avocado, Spinach Spaghetti and rose water lemonades.

Waitstaff are attentive, plating is solid but the cooking is the star here. Vegetables have that perfect crunch to each bite, flavors have good range to them and the seasoning is balanced but thoughtful.

Despite the unwelcoming vibe initially, the food and fun, helpful waitstaff were worth the bits of discomfort.

ABCv was on my list long before its opening. I'm always on the lookout for vegan/vegetarian/gluten-free options when I dine out, and anything with the ABC name in NYC tends to get high marks. As it turns out, the hype was totally warranted. If it weren't for the comically bad service here, this would have easily been a five-star experience. Fantastic variety, flavors, execution, ingredients, thoughtfulness. There's a serious emphasis here on health and wellness, which is my top priority these days. Though we were pretty full by the end of the meal, we felt uplifted as opposed to uncomfortable. That's rare, even at great restaurants. If you're open to dining sans-meat, head on over here. My hope is that the service is an early kink and will not stay this egregious. 

My mom is a Jean-Georges fanatic, so when my parents came to town, his newer ventures were of interest to her. She's not vegan but maintained that JGV would no question master veggies like he masters everything else. Plus, we knew we'd love the decor given the whole ABC carpet connection. There's definitely a spiritual vibe going on here and that came across on the menu as well. Definitely affected the experience in a nice way for me.

I've been staying away from alcohol lately due to health reasons, so it was exciting to see that ABCv offers a nice list of "restorative tonics", which are uber-healthy, non-alcoholic elixirs. Anything you see, they'll pair with sparkling water for a nice, refreshing drinks. I ordered two: the "Brain" (brahmi, gotu, kola, kale, spinach, ginger, lime) and the "Grounding" (ashwagandha, brazilian ginseng, horsetail, pau d'arco, bartlett pear, green apple, agave). Both yummy, but the Brain was the real star. Earthy, slightly sweet and invigorating. Weird to not drink alcohol, but hey, maybe I was spiritually inebriated? 

Food-wise, the ABCv menu is geared towards sharing. Even the plates that are relatively larger are still on the small side. And though it might entail spending a good chunk of change, trying a nice variety of plates is pretty easy regardless of hunger level because you're just eating vegetables. The menu is broken up into cold apps, hot apps as well as some grain-focused plates. We mainly focused on the first two categories. I'm gluten-free, and ABCv makes sure to be thorough about making adjustments or explaining which dishes one in this position should stay away from. Even with the gluten allergy, I was able to take part in almost everything we ordered. Everything here is healthy, light and tasty. Eats, below:  

Green chickpea hummus, thai basil, fresh pita/crudité: A++
Monster starter. The rave reviews amongst the food bloggers/critics are accurate. Some of the best hummus I've ever had, and they bring crudite for those who can't eat pita. Incredibly texture and flavor. 

Strawberries, radicchio, saffron vinegar, celery: A-
Light/delicate and slightly sweet. Not a standout but still solid. Thoughtful ingredient pairings.

Avocado lettuce cups, toasted cumin, serrano and lime, pepitas: A+
Seriously delicious. Powerful flavors despite how light the plate was. Pepitas to add some extra crunch as well as the earthiness from the yam made for a wholly satisfying bite.

Fresh sauerkraut, horseradish, dill, EVOO: A
I love sauerkraut. Made a case for eating kraut straight. Could've had three plates of this. 

Market carrots, stone ground nut and seed butter, chilies, lime: A/A+
The carrots were yummy but that nut/seed butter was a game-changer. I need to know all of the ingredients. 

Seared baby artichokes, Sicilian olive oil, green olives, mint: A
Well-cooked artichokes, flavorful but still light. Nice, Mediterranean preparation. 

Slow-roasted eight ball squash, coconut, cashews, flowers, warming spices: A-
I'm hot and cold when it comes to squash. The flavors here were fantastic, but I wasn't a huge fan of the squash itself. Loved the thai/earthy reference here. Definitely warming, as the description states. One of the heartier dishes we tried. 

Half cauliflower w/ turmeric-tahini and pistachios: A+
One of the best cauliflower preparations I've had. Lightly charred, served with tumeric-tahini dressing on the side. Fantastic pairing with the pistachios. The dressing tasted like a healthy ginger snap. Another warming dish. 

Steamed broccoli, farmer's cheese, cardamom crumbs: A-/A
I couldn't eat the crumbs, but the cheese/broccoli was certainly yummy. Can't fully report because I couldn't eat this in its entirety. 

Fresh spinach spaghetti (sub quinoa pasta), broccoli, kale, preserved lemon, garlic, parmigiano, saffron crumbs: A-
Lightest pasta dish I've had in a while. Delicate flavors so not as powerful as some of the earlier dishes, but still solid. Likely better when prepared as is stated on the menu. 

Four stars instead of five because our waitress was pretty much AWOL the whole night. Food came quickly, she did not. The four of us all got fewer drinks than we wanted due to her absence. Sigh.

Exceptionally overpriced and not good. Jean George's regular restaurants have much better vegetarian food, particularly Jean George in Trump tower. It's about the same price if you go for lunch and much better. I'm pretty forgiving when it comes to veggie food, and this was truly underwhelming and we left hungry and also with $60 each down the drain.

abc V serves up seriously delicious food that's a refreshing take on vegan / vegetarian. we shared zucchini baba ganoush and pine nut harissa as appetizers. both were served with crudite and mini pitas. I highly recommend ordering both, as well as the seared artichokes with green olives. we then shared fried wild rice followed by beluga lentils. their fried rice is a fabulous take on the dish, not too greasy or heavy. for dessert we indulged in their strawberry rhubarb pavlova which is light, meringue-based dessert. do keep in mind the portions are small so I suggest splitting several dishes. don't miss abc V it's a true five star experience.

Great restaurant, although the prices don't match the food. Came here for a very early dinner on Thursday and got seated at the bar. Plus was that Tilda Swinton walked in while we were there.

For drinks, we ordered the watermelon tequila beverage which was very delicious and refreshing and not too sweet!

For food, we ordered the lentils, pine nuts and lemon, cauliflower and eight ball squash. We also ordered the mint chocolate mousse for dessert. The pine nuts dish was delicious, like a better, light version of hummus. The lentils were also quite tasty!

The cauliflower, as someone had told me before, was fairly tasteless, but they do give you a turmeric dressing to add on at your discretion. I highly recommend dousing the cauliflower in this. Also, the pistachios and garnishes had little flavor. The eight ball with curry was my favorite by far!

The mint chocolate mousse was good, but not to die for. Overall, for two people we spent about $140 including tip, so it's fairly pricey for just veggies. But, I was expecting this.

I have mix feelings of this place. Simple/cute interior like ABC Kitchen, friendly staffs, interesting menu, not very good cocktails.

Crispy Tofu- simple while the mix of tofu and crispy yuba makes it interesting. Try~

Beet- fresh and delicious.

Green Pea Hummus- probably my favorite, its flavor is light and refreshing, verrrrrrry yummy.

Roasted Cauliflower- actually quite boring for me, I was expecting for unique flavor or seasoning. It's just plain cauliflower and you pour with curry sauce.

Spinach Spaghetti- it's alright, not much memory of it.

Burdock Noodle- Heavier taste, more of Asian flavor? I like it a lot.

Dosa- it's good but $16? Seriously?

Matcha Creme Brûlée- very matchaee

Grapefruit Gelatin- my type of summer dessert, on the sour side but very good.

Cocktail basically just mocktail, can pass. And the one with buckthorn- Extremely sour and acidity, tasted worse than cleanse juice........

I really like the atmosphere and the interior here. It's so nice and beautiful inside. They give complimentary sparkling water and bread which tastes amazing. The dishes were ok, a bit expensive for what it is. The star of this place is the dessert, I'm obsessed with the coconut custard!

Amazing, Amazing, and Amazing.
Enjoyed every dish as they have interesting seasoning to make vegitables so flavorful.
For 2 people, I was recommended to order two dishes per person to share, but ended up ordering two each plus one more dish and desert for each. It was absolutely filling and felt that we ordered too much.
They have quite a extensive menus unlike my other favorite vegetarian/vegan restaurant like Vedge in Philly. Out of many options, I loved Cauliflower, Shiitake,and Spinatcn pasta.
Desert was solid and gorgeous just like you expected as his other restaurants.

4 stars for cocktails. 3 for food. 2 for price of food. Lots of use of acid - too much really. The warm and cold dishes we had tasted like salad. We shared 3 plates - all veggies / no starches and I left very hungry. I am not vegetarian but go out to eat vegetarian food a lot - honestly you can make this at home if you are a decent cook. Fun atmosphere and if you're watching your calories but not your wallet then this is a good place.

I tell everyone I know (vegan and non vegan) to go here and try the tasting menu! The chef is SUPER creative. The presentation and taste of the dishes are great! It was a while ago that we ate there so it's tough to remember specifically all the plates we ordered but we definitely loved the cauliflower, the soup, the dessert, and the drinks! The ambience is cool but dim, and it's better if you're seated at a table (we were seated at the bar - it is extremely difficult to get a table here on any night of the week).

Best veggies I've had hands down (if only they weren't so damn expensive). I got a reservation here about three weeks in advance (everything on their online system seemed to fill up really fast but the actual restaurant wasn't that packed when we went.) My boyfriend and I started with the green chickpea hummus which was good but nothing to blow you away. The carrots however, were simply delicious and we finished them off quickly. We also opted to share the wild rice and the ramen noodles, both of which were seasoned perfectly and really delicious. Overall, the meal was really delicious but a bit too expensive for the food we received. Great place for a special occasion though or maybe coming with parents when they're paying.

Similar to Nix, an all vegetarian restaurant where most things can be made vegan/gluten-free as well. Super awesome for those who have dietary restrictions to have a nice evening out without having to worry about their diet. They have cute and unique drinks here and a pretty bar area in the front that you can chill at while waiting to get seated. All white interiors with mood lighting and a surprisingly large amount of seating, we got seated at 6 pm on a weekend with no problem but try to make a reservation otherwise. 

My friend and I got to try a bunch of dishes together. Standouts were the dosa, the beluga lentils, the zucchini babaganoush and the fried wild rice. Yes it is expensive but you're paying for ingredient quality and ambiance -- worth visiting once to try a nice dinner, especially if you're trying to convince meat eaters how tasty vegetables can be!

One of the best meals I've had in NYC in a long time. The only reason I did not give 5 stars is because I was not crazy about our waitress. As soon as we were seated, she informed us that we would need to be somewhat quick because they were fully booked. We ordered a bottle of wine and she didn't give us a taste - just poured us both glasses. And then was slow to refill our glasses when they were empty. I don't like it when waitstaff hover around your table and check-in too frequently, but there were definitely moments during dinner when we were wondering what happened to our waitress. Which seemed odd since she told us we would need to be quick. Lastly, when our plates were cleared and when we were given new utensils, the way they were placed was a bit haphazard. Usually I don't even notice things like this, but it was done in a way that both my friend and I noticed.

Outside of our particular server though, everything else was really beautiful and delicious. The restaurant itself is beautifully designed, down to the ceramic plates, flowers and salt on the table, the hot sauce on the table (which I appreciated!), and the menu. We ordered the following:

Charred zucchini baba ghanoush: Wonderfully flavored - some of the best baba ghanoush I've had and the pita was fresh, perfect chewy-ness, and slightly sour which I liked. Not your traditional baba ghanoush or pita.

Fresh sauerkraut: Good crunch, not overly vinegar-y. A nice, fresh flavor. Not sure though if I would order again though, even though I enjoyed it. Baba ghanoush I would order again because it was so good; sauerkraut I would pass on so that I can try something new.

Half roasted cauliflower: Delicious, and I've had a lot of roasted cauliflower. I enjoyed the side of tumeric-tahini to drizzle on top according to your taste, as well as the seasonings. Well done, would order again.

Chilled angel hair soba: This was my least favorite dish. I've been craving soba noodles and granted this was probably not the place to go for that, I was still hopeful given that everything on the menu sounds so tasty. I found the noodles overcooked and too thin for soba, and the tomato miso broth a bit bland. The veggies had a nice crunch, but didn't really do anything for the dish. I would not recommend ordering this, especially since so many other items on the menu either are or sound so delicious.

Fresh spinach spaghetti: SO GOOD. I already made reservations here so that I can have my friends try this dish. The spaghetti was the perfect thickness and cooked perfectly. The way the broccoli was cut - just everything - it was perfection. I would definitely order this again (and again and again and again).

Chocolate mousse: This was just okay until we realized that the mint chocolate crumble was all the way at the bottom. The crumble was a game changer and we wish there was more of it in the mousse. If you order, make sure to dig down with every bite to get some of the crumble. I wuold be open to ordering this again, but not tied to it.

Red currant macaron with basil ice cream and stone fruit: Oh my goodness, one of the best desserts I've had in a long time. I would go back just to eat this, but think it's likely seasonal, which makes me sad. The combination of flavors is amazing. I think I had a bite of basil ice cream, macaron, cherry, and peach and the insides of my mouth were going crazy with all the flavors. It's been a while since that has happened. I highly highly highly recommend this if they have it on the menu and am praying like crazy that they have it on the menu when I take my friends.

As a vegetarian and foodie, I've been wanting to try this restaurant for a while. I finally made it this past Friday night. The concept is small plates with the waiter suggesting my friend and I order 2-3 plates each (which would also equate to a pretty pricey dinner). Because it was late and my friend and I were not that hungry, we opted to split the half roasted cauliflower and each order a second dish. For that, I ordered the fresh spinach spaghetti and my friend ordered the avocado lettuce cups. 

The cauliflower--large like a whole artichoke served in Italy and lightly charred with a tahini dressing--was warm and delicious. 

The spinach spaghetti was light and delicate with a great mix of lemon, garlic, and saffron crumbs--a yummy and unique tasting pasta.

My friend also liked her avocado lettuce cups.
