Overall, a great but slightly expensive place for uniquely flavored and creative veggie dishes, and vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free eaters in a sleek setting.
Love the simple but very tasteful decor. The staff is amazing. Delicious food, expensive and very small portions.

Brought the boyfriend here for a chill birthday lunch and we both enjoyed it! Dishes we chose were all pretty flavorful so we didn't feel lacking despite us both being meat eaters. The avocado lettuce cups were simple but delicious (really flavorful with the toasted cumin/lime/pepitas on top of the avocado) - think they were the bf's favorite of the three dishes we ordered. I liked the kitchari a lot - it's a warm lentil/rice dish topped with yogurt/mint (we also mixed in the fermented carrot which is served on the side). We also tried the dosa with sambal, cheddar, egg and mint (solid dish - but I needed the hot sauce on the table for a little more kick/flavor). If you're familiar with dan bin (common chinese/taiwanese breakfast item), it kind of reminded me of that, but w/ dosa vs tortilla. We felt comfortably full/satisfied with the 3 dishes,
but we aren't big eaters (and honestly, if he were down I could have easily eaten at least another dish). 

Good service generally, albeit a little formal/lacking in energy. Will say that when I made the resi I had noted it was for a birthday, and they remembered (brought out a complimentary vegan matcha creme brulee with a small candle / happy birthday written in chocolate on the plate).

I came here during my 22 day vegan challenge for dinner. Besides the very rude and unpleasant host, my dining experience went great. Jamie and Masad helped alleviate my mood. 

We sat in the "chef's counter" which is just a fancy word to see the cooks prepare cold dishes and coffee, apparently the dining room was all booked up for the evening and they were not able to give us a table. After working many years in the service industry it was disappointing to see that the host did absolutely nothing to accommodate us.  40 minutes in and there were still plenty of vacant tables.
 
The food was delicious we had avocado cups, the cauliflower, the 8ball squash and spinach spaghetti. 

For dessert I tried the coconut tart, I was not pleased with the consistency of the tart, it felt really slimy, so I switched my dessert to the chocolate mousse (vegan) and that was yummy and it comes with vanilla cookies. 

The cocktails were refreshing and you can taste the freshness of the ingredients they use. I had a few pomegranate martinis, my friend opted for the nonalcoholic rose or lavender lemonade can't remember but she enjoyed it  

 The interior and décor of the restaurant is also a plus, loved the lighting fixtures and sink in the bathroom

I took a friend there for her birthday.  First of all, they wouldn't give us a reservation until 10 pm.  When we arrived at 9:30pm, the place was not crowded.  They wanted to stick us at a communal table when our time came up.  We had to fight to get a decent table.  The waiters were snobby and uninterested in serving us.  They were more concerned with their own convenience.  The food was excellent but skimpy.  I've been a vegetarian all my life so I know they were doing something very special with the veggies.  It wasn't worth the price though with the bitchy staff.

was really disappointed in this place. Service were really poor communicators since I ordered what i thought was a tasting menu (said the words tasting menu) but instead was brought 4 a la carte plates whose combined price was cheaper than the tasting menu price. Rather than telling me a tasting menu doesn't exist (at least for a solo diner), they basically charged me extra to not be able to pick what to order.

As for the food, the wok fried ramen was boring and hum drum, don't order that. The market carrots' texture was too soft and the taste was bland though the nut butter or whatever it was, was great. The green chickpea hummus was the highlight but it's not like i'm clamoring to go back for it. Just really disappointed overall and won't be back. Still can't believe they didnt just tell me to go a la carte instead of pay extra for a fake tasting menu.

Last night, we went to the restaurant with 7 people to celebrate a birthday. We eat out a lot. So, we know what is good.
The waitress recommended ordering 2-3 dishes per person. Consequently, we got to sample roughly 18 different dishes, as we doubled up on some. This excluded the desserts at the end.
Overall, we were disappointed!!  A few of the dishes were tasty, but most were mediocre. One noodle dish was extremely salty, too salty. We mentioned this to the waitress but got no feedback.
The biggest gripe was that the dishes were exceedingly SMALL, with the exception of the cauliflower. We looked at each other in amazement when the dishes were brought out. Where is the food? 
Dishes were much smaller than typical tapas dishes and half were entrees.
For roughly $60 per person, (EXCLUDING the drinks, tip and taxes), we finished the meal still being hungry.
Can't see how this restaurant will survive unless it keeps attracting people with its celebrity connection, Jean-Georges V.
This shows that you can't always believe in the restaurant reviews. Assume they don't care about getting up hungry as they don't have to pay for their meals.
I was really looking forward to trying this place but the food was average.  Nothing to write home about.

Vegan food of my dreams. Truly delicious, even a meat eater wouldn't miss steak while dining here. Beautifully presented, elevated flavors. I have eaten at several vegan places around the USA, ABCV outshines them all. Book your table well in advance.

Beautiful room and excellent food. Interesting and flavorful vegan/veg fare that was just right amount. Everyone enjoyed what they ordered except for the chopped salad with sticky rice - friend who ordered that did not care for it. Nice staff but we're a bit disorganized when we arrived with a reservation. We ended up seating ourselves finally. Bit of a disappointment to not get a better welcome at this restaurant.

On a recent trip to NYC, I selected ABCV as the perfect brunch restaurant to celebrate my husband's birthday. We were not sure what to expect, other than being impressed by the yelp reviews and the menus posted online. As soon as we walked in, we knew this was going to be a fantastic meal! The decor included fun lighting, lots of whites, and an upbeat ambiance. At 11:30am on a Saturday, the place was bustling, and even had a wait when we finished our meal an hour later. 

Both the service and food were fantastic! I'm only docking a star because the prices were a tad expensive for brunch (our meal was over $100, sans alcohol). Some of the highlights of our meal included: the hot sauce that is complimentary on every table (SOOO GOOD!), the fresh juices, the dosas, and the hummus. All in all, it was a memorable experience and we hope to come again to try their dinner sometime soon.

One of the BEST vegan restaurants, or restaurants in general, I have ever been.  The cuisine here is an experience!  Everything from the drinks, appetizers, main course and deserts were heavenly!!!!  Highly recommend it.  
The atmosphere is lovely, bright and comfortable.  Keep in mind that it is a bit loud and they don't accept reservations so you may have to wait to be seated.

The food here is unbelievably delicious. I find myself craving it all the time. Bravo on creating a restaurant with insanely yummy food, great fresh ingredients that's actually really healthy!! We've been coming once or twice a week and not going to slow down!!

Came here for a girls night and for three meat eaters, we were all super impressed and loved all of the food we had. The fried hen of the woods mushroom reminded us of fried chicken, it was pretty crazy how similar it was. The fresh spinach spaghetti was delicious and a favorite of all of ours. We also had green chickpea hummus, slow roasted beets, and seared baby artichokes, all of which we enjoyed. The only dish that none of us liked was the fresh steamed tofu. As a tofu fanatic myself, I was really disappointed with this dish. The flavor of the sauce that it was served with was not good. I think it was some type of soy/ Asian style sauce (it was not the truffle one that is currently shown on the online menu, which may be better).
Great vegetarian restaurant. Every dish is unique and flavorful in its own way. Highly recommended

I have been to ABC cocina many times and have been dying to try it's sister restaurant abcv. Abcv definitely did not disappoint! 

I dined with one friend and between the two of us we had a few good allergies. Our waiter was incredibly patient with us. He was so knowledgeable about the menu and gave us great recommendations. 

We ordered the avocado lettuce cups, roasted cauliflower, gluten free green spaghetti and baluga lentils. The lentils and the spaghetti were our favorite dishes because both had SO much flavor. The cauliflower came with a delicious turmeric sauce that was fun and tasty, but I personally prefer my roasted veggies to be super roasted (hovering on burnt ). This cauliflower was more of a light roast.

I love that the drink and food menus hit very different taste buds than the cocina menu, but the quality, service and experience are still superb. I will definitely be dining here more often.

Great vegetarian! Came here not because I eat vegan but because date did, and I think I might give some vegetarian only restaurants a chance. I finished the meal without feeling tired, and we ate a lot! Great non-alcoholic drinks! Really tonic line and refreshing. Almost everything we ate was great. The beats & avocado was good. Lettuce wraps. They have this fake chicken & honey dish which takes like real chicken and was delicious. Hummus was really good. Definitely recommend coming here, vegetarian or not.

Me and my girlfriend were on a lean and healthy diet to prepare ourselves for a trip to the Amazone. So  we were all ready to appreciate the vegetarian and healthy food. We ordered a bunch of dishes and didn't like any. It was very expensive for not much food and we couldn't even force ourselves to eat and left most of it. The place is nice though. Just the food sucks painfully.

My husband and I went there for a healthy and light lunch. We like the idea and we love to abc team's works always. 
We didn't have a reservation. They were busy but not like crazy busy. We like the idea! It is great! Ambiance, decor and all details were very nice! Food looks fresh, tasty and healthy! We ask to host a table for two, they have 3 tables empty at the out side but they said they have a reservations for those tables and they said it can take 30 min. for inside.  If we will wait 30 min. we can wait for inside off course because ambiance is so nice, we think we can enjoy to look at all details. After 10 min we decided to take quick tour in abc store until the table will be ready. After 30 min we went to restaurant because nobody call us. They said it's gonna take 10 more min. We start to wait again and the outside tables are still empty also 3 more tables also left at the same time. After 10 more min the manager came to us and she said our table is ready at the outside!!! We said why we wait 45 min. for outside table which was already empty when we were there!! And she said wants to check again and they said our table inside is setting. It was take already 10 more min. We were so hungry and angry. We need to left from the restaurant. We were so sad because they did a great job great ideas but sometimes even one employee's mistakes or unorganized and uncontrolled team work can messed up everything :( 
Horrible young unprofessional host ruined our day...
creative team and kitchen +A  managers and who control/ organize the team was F
Everything is curated and it's a beautiful spot. Expensive, but worth it. All the items are amazing and the service top notch.

Clean decor, flavor packed dishes made with the freshest in season ingredients, and service which leaves you wanting to keep coming back, this place is phenomenal. Can't wait to go back and try more dishes!
I really wanted to like this place, but the food was just OK. My favorite was the cauliflower.

Very very delicious.  Pretty cool space.  Shared tables.  Loud but not impossibly so.  Very attentive wait staff.  Interesting selection of healthy tonics to start. Musts: avocado cups, cauliflower, green chick pea humus, green spaghetti noodles.  Reasonable prices.   One complaint- check delivered without our request while dessert still being finished.

ABCV never disappoints.  Reservations are a must as the restaurant is packed breakfast, lunch and dinner.  The food is incredible, having impressed with vegetarians and carnivores alike, and the service is always well above par.  Menu highlights are the roasted carrots with nut/seed butter and the full head cauliflower.  

Also a great place to stop for a smoothie (order at the bar) for breakfast or light lunch while shopping ABC Home.

When I recently learned that Jean-Georges has a vegetable-focused restaurant (I'm terrifically out of the loop since I moved out of NYC), I was like sign me the eff up! With visions of crispy yuba, exquisite sauces and artichoke salads festooned with edible flowers dancing in my head, I made reservations immediately for the next time I would be in the city. Note that I didn't say "vegan" or even "plant-based." Semantics, I realize, but there's dairy on the menu here. 

My mom loves vegetables but is not a vegetarian. I'm vegan. Upon perusing the menu, I knew some of the dishes might be a bit adventurous for her tastes, but I figured if I insisted it was my treat, she'd relax a little bit and just go with it. I'm glad I made that choice because my intention was to order anything on the menu that intrigued me, start with a couple small plates and add on accordingly. There is only one dish, broccoli with farmer's cheese, that cannot be veganized (I asked to make sure).

That the restaurant is stunning is fact. If you're someone like my mom or boyfriend and hate the typical NYC fit as many tables in as possible - so that you feel like you're too fat to squeeze between tables without knocking over a bud vase with your ass (yeah, that happened)- you won't love the seating. The communal tables, while not ideal for when this restaurant fills up (and it will be completely full, trust), allow for more elbow room. The room is gloriously white, the lights are perfectly dimmed to allow for a gorgeous glow (everyone looks beautiful in here) and an entire glass wall allows you to see the magic going on in the kitchen, without it seeming like you're inside the kitchen! Perfection.

The lackluster greeting offered up by the three hostesses was off-putting (nor did they thank us upon leaving, just stared at us). This needs to change. As unwelcoming and lacking in hospitality these ladies were, I was dreading pretentious service, but that was not at all the case! Our main waiter was  seraphic, attentive and described the specials poetically. Another waiter who brought us food and drinks was very approachable and friendly. Great waitstaff from what I observed, so I'm not sure what's going on at the hostess stand.

Verdict on the four dishes we ordered: 
-pine nut lemon/harissa: good but I feel like the flavor wasn't very complex and the harissa, not as spicy as I'm used to (accompanying pita was also just OK. I've had better). The dried apricots on top were a nice touch, however!

-seared baby artichokes: a beautiful, generous plate (edible flowers! olives! mint!) These were my favorite as the flavors are unique, subtle yet extremely tasty.

-lettuce avocado cups: my Mom loved these, especially the fire roasted acorn squash that accompanied them. I didn't get to try them, however, possibly because I didn't want to take them away from her!

-spinach pasta: a disappointment. Dill dominates to an unpleasant level and the kale was so bitter, I thought that mustard greens might have been substituted. Note that this normally comes with parmesan which might balance out the bitterness. I have a feeling it might be essential to the dish in some way. In a restaurant of this caliber, the vegan option should not be to merely leave off the cheese, dairy, egg etc. I don't see why they couldn't have a cashew parmesan substitute. I feel like they overcompensated with olive oil as there was entirely too much of it drowning out the vegetables, pasta and bland breadcrumbs making it a mushy affair. I do not recommend it.

We didn't order anything else. Honestly, I wasn't that impressed with anything enough to warrant trying more. The price point is too high for 2 out of 4 dishes that missed the mark. A place that serves a pedestrian pasta dish for 19 dollars is not going to inspire me to order more, no matter how hungry I am feeling.

With vegetable-focused restaurants like Dirt Candy and Blossom, not to mention vegan restaurants constantly turning out incredible plant-based dishes, I'd be hard pressed to return to ABCV. My non vegan friends all seemed to have been amazed by almost everything they had here and it makes me happy that a place can bring vegetables to the main course for them. I've just had better.

Update. It's a shame they impose so many arbitrary serving rules. No eating at the window. No seating outside despite crystal clear temperate weather. We are repeat patrons, trying to eat and being denied for 45 minutes despite copious available seating. It's disconcerting and disrespectful. Please take note that their seating policies are not logical, far beyond customary "full party" rules.
Best place for veggie food in the city. I went there 2 nights ago and the service and food were amazing. They had the best mushroom dish I have ever had. Also save room for dessert.

Have been wanting to try for a while. My gf was lucky enough to grab us a table. It did not disappoint.  We started with the 

chickpea hummus - excellent esp w a little hot sauce that each table has.

Cauliflower- we shared a half order that was plenty. 
Really good with the sauce they give you on side (tahini) 

Beets- probably our #1 if we had to pick. The flavors on this dish are amazing. Little pickles and capers and chives 

Carrots. - very good goes nicely with the almond butter purée bottom of dish 

Spaghetti - amazing w spinach and fresh lemon and parmigiana cheese

Simple salad w heirloom tomatoes. - Really great w onions and cucumbers. Very light 

She had the mushroom blossoms  which were lightly fried. She enjoyed very much. 


We were too full for desert but can't wait to return. 

Also a beautiful open , white dining area. 

5 stars for food, service and ambience.
Kabocha squash was very good but the spinach spaghetti smelled like rubber or alcohol and it was bothering my sense of taste and enjoyment. Very loud during lunch.

ABCV is a beautiful, casual place to grab breakfast or lunch on a weekday. I discovered it on my way to work, and it's become a solid staple for coffee, juices, and other healthy breakfast snacks. There's a sit down area in the back I haven't tried, but the to-go area in the front is great!

I love this place! The wait is worth it. The cocktails are just delicious. I recommend the hummus, cauliflower, kale noodles, and the wild fried rice. And finish it off with the matcha creme brûlée. You won't be sorry!

I'm excited that healthier places to eat are now trending. It's a great vibe here, hip crowd, socialites and people who have healthy lifestyles. Lots of choices to choose from. This is a place the concierge recommended. Typically you order two dishes per person and it's meant to be shared. I think I could enjoy pretty much everything on the menu and I'm not a vegetarian.

Solid. One of my favorite vegetarian restaurants in the city. Came here once for the food but the real gem here is the DRINK menu! Such awesome seasonal cocktails that have natural freshly squeezed juices. Try it out!

I've had a bad experience at ABC Kitchen so I was very skeptical, but finally decided to try out ABCV for birthday dinner with a friend. We shared the pine nut and lemon, roasted beets, chicken of the woods, whole roasted cauliflower. Everything was delicious, but my favorite is the chicken of the woods mushrooms battered and fried to perfection. It's a rare dish to find anywhere else and is a bit small in portion. My friend loved the cauliflower, while I found it just okay, and we really only needed half of it. There were some clear plastic shards in the cauliflower dish, so I alerted our server. It just seems like a little mishap and not a huge hygiene/safety concern, but the staff were very apologetic and did not charge us for the dish.  

For dessert, we ordered the matcha creme brulee but our server also brought out a complimentary salted caramel chocolate tart completed with a happy birthday candle--both were amazing. I appreciated that the staff here were attentive and really tried to make sure we had a good dining experience.

Came here for my birthday celebration with friends and it was exactly what I was looking for.

RESERVATIONS: I called to make a large group reservation about a month in a advance.  If you have more than 10 people (so 11+) you have to do a pre-fixe menu of about $88/person.  Since I didn't want to do that, I opted for a group of 10.  When I arrived, my husband and I were the first to get there so they said to let them know when the majority of our group was there and they'll seat us.

ATMOSPHERE: I loved ABC Kitchen's vibe and this one looked even more awesome.  It has lots of white everywhere and feels very modern and trendy.  There are obscure/modern looking light fixtures and artwork.  One side has a bar/open kitchen and then the other dining area has a slightly open kitchen and more tables.  Each tables is adorned with various plants and succulents, candles and low lighting.  Perfect for the birthday celebration I was planning.

FOOD: It's a vegetarian restaurant, which I was skeptical about at first but like most people have said, despite that, their food is very flavorful.  I think with a smaller group, most of the dishes are meant to be shared but because we had so many people it just made more sense to order 1-2 appetizers and then each person order their own dish.  Don't expect to be very full coming out of here.

SPAGHETTI - very chewy green spinach noodles with lots of lemon/zest.  It is a big on the tart side so beware of that but it was perfect for my dinner portion.  

CAULIFLOWER - a whole cauliflower was enough for 10 of us and is a great sight to see with the knife stuck in it.  Pour all of the sauce because it is delicious.  It has a curried cauliflower type taste, almost reminiscent of some Indian side dishes.  Highly recommend and makes for a great photo.

HUMMUS - people raved about this so I asked for it with both the crudite and pita. A pita has 4 triangles so we got 2 (which they charged extra for).  It's good with the hummus, which has a slight thai basil taste and is just very flavorful.  If you enjoy hummus, I would get this and skip the crudite.

*CAKE CUTTING FEE - they charged $7/person because we brought our own cake and they helped us cut it. I did appreciate that they lit the candles AND put it on this classic white cake stand.

Overall, I enjoyed my birthday celebration here and would recommend it for a nice date night or birthday or celebration dinner.  It IS quite pricey for what you are getting (small, simple portions) but I gave it 4 stars because of the entire package (food + atmosphere).
Menu is filled with great selections. Enjoyed every dish and the service was terrific. Its tapas style and I think a party of two should be good with 4-5 dishes.

sounds silly but their bread is really well made. we saw it on the table next to us and asked for some. one is almost as dense as pound cake but both are so chewy and fresh. the cauli was awesome- the sauce and the crunchies they put on it- coulve been slightly more tender. the green pea hummus was my favorite. we alsogot the spinach pasta which was good but im personally
not a huge fan of lemon and it was very lemony. they took great care of us for my friends bday- vegan matcha brulee was surprisingly light and tasty- usually dislike matcha. my rec: get the hummus, get the bread, and get the half size cauliflower so its tender

Why are we here again?  My boyfriend and I asked ourselves this as we walked into the restaurant on a Friday night because neither of us are vegetarian.  But, we had heard good things, and it's a Jean Georges restaurant so we figured we would give it a shot.

Verdict:
Overall, although not my thing, I was pleasantly surprised by the food and would give that 4.5 stars.  I'd give the service 3.5 stars - although our server himself was pleasant, it look 20 minutes from the time we ordered our drinks and food for our drinks to arrive (we had already gotten and eaten 2 of our appetizers by this point).  And then, after our first 2 dishes came out, the rest of our items came out within the span of 10 minutes, which was very annoying.  Finally, I'd give value for food 3 stars.  For 2 people, with 1 drink each and 7 items, we paid 100 each with tax and tip, which seems like a lot for vegetables and no meat. Will I be back?  Probably when I'm feeling unhealthy, but not anytime soon.

Food:
We ordered the following (in order of my most favorite to least favorite)
Ramen - it's probably saying something about my taste buds that my favorite thing I ordered was something that didn't even have vegetables as a base.  The flavors were amazing, the noodles cooked perfectly and overall was delicious. 
Slow roasted beats - this was awesome.  The dish was incredibly balanced, the beats perfect and the dijon and avocado brought everything together. 
Avocado lettuce cups - although these were my second favorite thing we ordered, at 13 dollars for maybe 1/4 of an avocado and some lettuce, I found these to be overpriced.  That being said, the flavors were on point, and the citrus from one of the fruits really brought out the other flavors
Chickpea hummus - great grainy consistency with a subtle kick that brought together all the flavors.  They have gluten free bread so they brought some for my boyfriend, but forgot to bring me the regular pita bread, so I had to ask the server to bring me some of that as well.
Dosa with  yogurt, avocado, sprouts - if you like dosas, you'll probably enjoy this, but I find them a bit boring.  Though the flavors were pretty good, I didn't like this as much as the other things we got.
Half cauliflower - It's cauliflower that's pretty much it, though the pomegranate seeds and the pistachios did offer a nice crunch to an otherwise mushy vegetable. 
Fresh spinach spaghetti - my boyfriend ordered this with gluten-free noodles, and I didn't try it but he seemed to enjoy it

Wow! The food here was truly of excellence. It was a very unique, unparalleled experience. We came for brunch, and the menu was a bit small but regardless very versatile. I was a bit disappointed because they didn't have the cauliflower (which is only served at dinner!) but everything else was fabulous. I recommend the squash bowl, pancakes, and dosa. I would have given it 5 stars, but our server wasn't good at all. He had an attitude and wasn't attentive to our table. Nonetheless, the food was great, so I will definitely return.
My favorite vegan good in NYC , creative delicious, great vibe , servers were very knowledgeable about the menu
Great soba. However would recommend that the one stray leaf be removed from the bowl. It really irks me that they take the time to place it there so methodically. Get the soba but ask for no leaf.

While there were several highlights to our meal: green pea hummus, avocado lettuce cups, fried hen of the woods mushrooms, clean decor, salted caramel chocolate tart, the low lights were far more memorable: late seating, cold (as in ice cold) bread, still water being poured into glasses of sparkling, slow service, indifferent hostesses, the worst, most ill-conceived eggplant dish I've ever had. This place just doesn't stack up to either ABC Kitchen or ABC Cocina. Or frankly to ANY restaurant in the vicinity. I admit that the food is creative, but it's not great and the service was just too off putting for me to ever come back.

Food:
Green pea hummus ****
Pinenut w harissa and apricot ***
Avocado lettuce cups ****
Beets ****
Roasted eggplant *
Roasted cauliflower ***
Artichokes ***
Fried hen of the woods mushrooms ****
Chestnut pasta special ***
Spinach pasta ***
Dosa w yogurt **
Coconut custard ***
Salted caramel chocolate tart ***

The ambiance for every ABC store (or resto) is always beautiful, which is what helped the overhyped food options here at ABCV.

Table for 2 on a weekday for lunch without a wait.
The service staff was patient enough while my friend made her way here and service throughout was attentive and prompt.

Food though is healthy, flavourful for what it is and intriguing for novelty reasons. Unfortunately it is not somewhere I'd dine at again because ABC kitchen is better and the city has way too many other options..

Came here this past Sunday afternoon to catch our 1:30pm reservation. They asked us to wait. We waited about 25 minutes before asking them what's going on, after which they seated us immediately and we could clearly see a bunch of empty tables near us, so they obviously forgot about us. We asked the hostess if we could order immediately, since we were trying to catch a movie nearby at 3pm. She said she'd let our waiter know. Five minutes later and our waiter doesn't make an appearance, so we walked out of there having wasted a half hour. Hilariously bad service.

What an experience. Speaking as a non-vegan, I only came here to support my vegan friend. I came in with high expectations, especially given it is associated with Jean-Georges. 

Environment: This restaurant has really cute decor, as if it's straight out of a bumble gum pop music video. The lightness of the walls makes this place feel welcoming from the start. The cool plates and table utensils add character to the restaurant.

Food: I had the dosa with Swiss chard, fried egg, and zaatar along with the sweet potato brunch bowl and the green chickpea hummus (obviously I didn't have it all by myself, I have a figure to watch!). Overall, the brunch bowl and the hummus were excellent. It was very savory, and i felt healthy eating it. On the other hand, the dosa wasn't really that great. I felt the fried egg didn't mix in well with the zaatar, and it kind of tasted worse as time went on.

Price: 5/5. For a brunch place, it's pretty much in-line with all the other restaurants out there. However, the quality is much higher and I would say the value is out of this world.

All in all, I had a really good time here. I never thought I would have enjoyed a vegan meal, but here I am, dumbstruck. While I maybe ordered the wrong thing with the dosa, the other two dishes definitely brought enough to the table that I will gladly go back

Excellent food, terrible service. 

Came for dinner this past Saturday with a 5:30pm reservation. Our waitress clearly forgot about us after taking our drink order. It was 20+ minutes before she returned to take our food order (and even longer for the drinks to arrive). I asked for bread once (Sure! I'll bring that right out!). No bread. Twice (Sure! I'll bring that right out!). No bread. Thrice (Sure! I'll bring that right out!). No bread. Fourth time was a charm and in delivering the bread, she says, "Oh, there's a bit of a bread shortage tonight." Hmm.

We were there much longer than other tables because our service was so terrible. And she could've done more to upsell us (especially getting us more drinks). The other staff were a bit too "attentive" for my likes - sweeping dishes off the table before we were done. In what became comical, we were holding on to a dish to enjoy the sauce with that (elusive) bread and no fewer than 4 different (!) people tried to bus that dish. 

When the check arrived, I felt hurried out of there. Ironic since there was no rush previously. Our neighboring table (with the same waitress) also had issues. A glass of wine that arrived very late, rushed at the end, etc.

The food was excellent but I can't justify returning at these prices -- and with this type of service. If the waitress can't be bothered to care about her customers, why should I care to return?

This week's fashionplate features our satin Janis shorts at the new vegan/ veggie spot ABC V.  I went here for brunch with a gf and we sat at the bar as it was already packed at noon.  We both started with delish matcha coladas.  We then decided to splitzies some eats.  We got the sambal and cheddar dosa and omg so delish.  We also go the gluten free almond pancakes which were great, the little beaker with maple syrup was adorbs  too.  The fingerling potatoes were great as well.  I added a cold brew because we all know I need my caffeine.  This spot was so yummy and it was a mix of girl gangs and couples and families.

The food is creative, looks pretty (my oh my the colors!), and flavors are on point - what more can you ask for!?

Some of the more outstanding dishes:
Slow roasted beets - the avocado puree is heavenly
Seared baby artichokes - the tanginess of the dressing and olives make this a stellar dish
Green chickpea hummus - the thai twist is interesting

The only dish that failed was the dosa - lacked crispiness, the yogurt dip doesn't really go with it, and the avocado is just out of place in the dish

The decor is very clean, almost minimalist. Service is informal and friendly.

Definitely a place to return to.

I went here for dinner with a friend on Wednesday night and i have to say, it was quite amazing. I was slightly put off by the 20 minute wait even though i had a reservation, but the food and service definitely made up for it. I wasn't expecting the service to be great due to previous reviews, but the host was apologetic for the wait and the waiters were very efficient and attentive during our meal. 

To start off, my drink was amazing - i ordered the yuzu gin and tonic. We then ordered the green chickpea hummus, avocado lettuce cups, wok fried ramen, dosa with yogurt and sprouts, and the special fried mushroom dish. All of our dishes were amazing and different. They had a burst of flavor and was really satisfying. For dessert, we ordered the salted caramel chocolate tart, which was also an amazing mixture of salty and sweet to end the meal. 

Overall, if you can get past the expensive price tag of the restaurant, it is a great veg/vegan place to dine at. I truly enjoyed my experience there and would definitely recommend it!

I've been to ABCV a few times now and while the food is good I wasn't urning to rush back. The cauliflower is great and HUGE. Everything else was kind just okay. I hate to say we even found a piece of metal in one of our entrees that looked like it came from a cleaning brush. They were super nice about it but at a place like this you don't expect something like that to happen.

I'm still rooting for success and I'll give it another try.

Honeynut Squash!! *** Do yourself a favor and get several orders of this. It's a creamy blended squash topped with a tahini sauce, a lovely blend of savory and sweet. Comes with fresh pita, which you can stuff with that magical golden orange spread. 

Second favorite dish was the avocado lettuce wraps-generous on the avocado,  great crunch, spiced to perfection. 

Third favorite was the cauliflower, which is super savory with the pistachio crumble. The whole order is pretty huge, even if shared between three.

Chanterelle mushrooms, artichoke hearts, and lentils were all just OK- they leaned towards being too salty, which was totally unnecessary for such naturally flavorful food. The slow roasted beets were tasty but not life changing. 

Desserts are awesome (&vegan): 
-Pumpkin cheesecake was topped with gingery cookie crumbles and cranberries, creamy and satisfying. Not too heavily spiced like many pumpkin dishes are.

-Matcha brûlée uses super high quality matcha, so get this if you are a matcha geek- otherwise you may not appreciate.

-The fruity coconut custard was tasty and light. Not my favorite.  

Light, airy decor that has a very clean finish. Very modern interior to match the modern plant based dishes. Worth the price tag? If you love vegetables, are vegetarian or vegan, this will be your heaven! Just go with the dishes suggested above.
I love the decor and the food is fresh and flavorful. The tonics are fun to try and the crème brûlée was amazing.

Spectacular food, service and setting, but let's be clear that the V doesn't stand for value. The good brother Jean-Georges is stone cold charging $28 for a braised half-cabbage and $13 for a glass of glorified orange juice, to cite just two examples of the often-ruthless prices.

That said, if you're filthy rich or in the mood to splurge, ABCV is a damn fine experience.

ABCV isn't only a vegetarian's paradise, but a culinary heaven for all. My boyfriend surprised me with a dinner reservation on my birthday, and I'm still convinced that he made the best choice possible.

The ambience is relaxed, and at the same time, sophisticated. The decor is simple, with all-white tables and chairs, a select few colored lime green to make a statement. Chandeliers hanging throughout the dining room are perhaps the fanciest aspects of the restaurant's design.

The green chickpea hummus topped with Thai basil ensured that we started off on the right track. While we paired the hummus with fresh pita, I could have easily taken a spoon and eaten the entire bowl by itself. It completely exceeded my expectations.

The market carrots, believe it or not, were remarkable as well. Prior to dining at ABCV, I would have never imagined that incorporating carrots and stone ground nut and seed butter into the same dish would yield such delicious results. For a hint of spice, tiny slices of chili and lime were also added to the mix.

I wasn't a huge fan of the fresh spinach spaghetti's texture, although I did like its taste. The preserved lemon, garlic, and saffron crumbs carried the pasta's flavor, while the broccoli, kale, and parmesan cheese acted as garnishes. The noodles, however, were dry and pretty bland on their own.

The smoky eggplant with fresh shelling beans, sweet pepper purée, aromatic spices, and cilantro blended sweet and savory elements together to put a spin on the vegetable's usual preparation. The dense cannellini and lima beans complemented the softer eggplant, which soaked up the sweet pepper purée.

We ended dinner with a half portion of the roasted cauliflower, served alongside a turmeric-tahini dressing. The sauce, in combination with the pistachios scattered around the plate, imparted a nutty flavor, similar to curried cauliflower.

Overall, I'm very impressed. The green chickpea hummus and market carrots were definitely the highlights of our meal, and I can't wait to return to ABCV for more.
Good and creative fancy small plates. Over priced in my opinion. Special occasions. Been here twice. Second time for drinks by the bar and enjoyed the inventive drinks menu.

Great vegan dishes that were filled with delicious flavors. Makes me want to go fully vegan. Tried the sweet potato dish, savory oatmeal, tofu and mushroom dish. Will definitely go back again! Another great place from the ABC group.

The food here is delicious! My friend and I loved all the dishes we ordered. Our favorite of the night were the beets. It's a mixture of sweet and tangy that was perfect. The hummus was also delicious and the vegetables were really fresh. The only reason why this is a 3 star however, was the hostess. I would rate it a 2 star, because of her, but the food was spectacular and the waiter we had was great. We got there early 15-20 minutes for our 8pm reservation. And we were first told that we had to wait another 20-30 minutes. We went up at 8:10pm and told to wait a few more minutes. 10 minutes later, I asked another hostess that we had a reservation at 8pm, and wanted to know when our table was ready. The original hostess who came back gave an attitude with no apologies all 3 times I went up from when we got there to the 2 times past our reservation time. I have never had an experience where restaurants have a problem with their guest showing up early and letting walk-ins get a table before someone with a reservation. When it was 8:15pm the large crowd was gone and we were still left waiting. The sad thing was the food was delicious but I wouldn't come again since that experience ruined our night. This place was also a pretty expensive. We decided to come here because it was my friend's birthday and wanted to do something nice. I've been to all of other ABC restaurants and they were always top notch. This was extremely disappointing.

I came in from out of town to visit family and was brought here. WOW was I blown away! I am not a vegetarian, but I found plenty of items on the menu that were satisfying. One being the wok fried ramen noodle. It was so delicious and filling! Another personal favorite were the avocado lettuce cups. They were quite refreshing. To end our meal we had the salted caramel chocolate tart. If I could eat that dessert for every meal, I would. All in all my experience here was wonderful, and the next time I am in town I will be returning.

Their brunch is heaven for gluten-free vegans- yes, you can eat pancakes again!!!!! Delicious, wonderful pancakes. The rest of the menu is great and interesting too and the space is very beautiful. And if you overslept and missed the 10:30 brunch cut off, fear not, because the more limited cafe menu is still a really good consolation. In a city that loves its decadent, dairy-and-gluten-laden brunches, this place is a godsend for the rest of us.

I absolutely love the food at this place, but the only reason this place is getting 4 stars and not 5 is the service.

We had a reservation for 8:30 and they sat us at at our table only at 9:10. Its difficult to get reservations here, and after getting one, you don't want to be waiting for 40 mins to get a table.

The food was great!

pine nut and lemon, harissa, dried apricot with fresh pita was yummy,
Cauliflower head is a must - even for non-cauliflower lovers - if you're 2 please call for the half head.

avocado lettuce cups, toasted cumin, serrano and lime, pepitas - This was really good too!! 

Mushroom lovers please get this - wild mushrooms, enoki, arugula, spicy pine nut mustard, tarragon.

I didn't like the spinach spaghetti with saffron bread crumbs - it had a weird taste :/

fresh tofu, spicy szechuan pepper oil, fermented mustard, peanuts  - was awesome! Please have this

and of course the dosa, yogurt, avocado, sprouts - its such an off beat selection of things - but surprisingly they go well together!

Going back for sure...mostly next season :)

Delicious food and wonderful service!

We waited a while beyond our reservations time because we got bumped for what we later realized was a table for a celebrity, the management was very proactive to accommodate us and treat us well.  Will be returning!

Okay - this place is AMAZING. One of my favorite in New York for sure. I took a friend visiting from out of town for dinner on a Monday night, and of course, the restaurant was still packed. The entire experience - despite the crowd - was nothing short of five stars. Our waiter, Pedon, was memorably informative, attentive, and a lovely addition to the already stellar experience. The food: I'm vegan, and let me tell you, it is harder than you may think to find a "nice", non hippy, bar/dinner spot in the city. Also, that caters to those who don't have the same type of diet too. This new ABC addition checks all the boxes. Will definitely be returning again, dying to try their breakfast/brunch!

What a disappointment. I had only heard good things about ABCV (and love ABC Kitchen) so suggest my friends have a holiday dinner here. The night was a series of 2-star service and operations: 

- Mon night 8pm reservation and we weren't seated until 8:30. 
- During the wait to be seated, the manager and maitre'd had come over to offer drinks on the house but never came back or sent anyone to take our order. 
- Waitress left us with menus and never came back to take our order until we flagged her down
- Missed one of our entree orders
- Switched waitresses without telling us (and it wasn't a shift change)
- Gave us one of our neighboring table's dishes and we had to sort it out/passed it over ourselves. 
- Took our dessert away before it was done (without asking)

The food was a bit salty but pretty good overall. But honestly, for their own reputation sake, the operations really need some TLC. There were a few moments where there wasn't a single waitstaff on the floor and other times when there were multiple staff floating /socializing around the host stand.

I adore the ambience and decor of ABCV. The brightness and whiteness of the restaurant is a stark contrast to its darker neighbour, ABC Kitchen. The look and feel is very clean and "healthy" eats, very much like a Los Angeles restaurant. The restaurant is ideal for a group of 2 or 3.

The staff is very friendly and helpful in navigating the food and drinks menus.

For drinks, we ordered vibrations. The Joy tastes like an effervescent grape juice. It's flavours are richer compared to the Heart, which is lighter and refreshing.
For food, we ordered the green chickpea hummus, which was delicious. The Thai basil is a great addition to make the chickpea taste refreshing and light. Other stands outs are the fried wild rice and walnut bolognese. Despite being vegetarian, these dishes were "meatier" without feeling heavy. The walnut bolognese was savoury and the pasta cooked wonderfully. I definitely recommend if it is on the menu.

ABCV is a great restaurant for all diners, not just vegetarians.

Small Plates, Big Price tag, Average Service, Average Food = Average Experience. Two adults, 5 small plates, 1 glass of wine, $140.  I am surprised at all the "AMAAAZZZZING" Reviews.  If you've only ever eaten boiled unseasoned vegetables your whole life then your in for a real treat.  But, if you have been exposed to some High Quality Food Experiences, (VEGANIZED-NJ, Candle 79, Blossom, VEG-Philly, Frankie Spuntinos, Farmer and the Chick Pea-NJ) you will know this is very average food. I guess when you attach a celebrity chef to a kitchen; even average food will get a lot of fanfare.  After eating here I realized all the Media biased reviews of the food and dining experience never actually said it was good. Vegetarian; me too place at best.

Pretentious vegetarian fare. Very LA. The cauliflower and practically all of the cocktails are to die for. Turn over of staff looks high though. I rarely get the same server as it seems like they're always training someone. Which is irrelevant since the food is awesome.

I had a reservation and we arrived 16 minutes late. The woman holding a "PR" position said she give the table to another client because they keep the table just for 15min and if we want to eat she can give us a table but we should have to eat in 30min. So bad customer service!!!!

Interesting inventive food - not cheap but you get what you pay for.  Cool vibe and attentive service.  Rec dishes: chickpea hummus, lettuce avocado cups, cauliflower.  Dont come starving but come ready to be impressed.

Really impressed with ABCV. Their dishes are inventive and delicious. Their atmosphere is modern with a cozy touch. Their staff is friendly. Overall, a wonderful restaurant and great addition to the NY dining scene. I'd definitely return - even just for a cocktail and that cauliflower or one of the many distinct desserts.

The waitress was very patient with all the questions we had about the menu. We had a lot of questions, even though two of us had been before, and all of us had already looked at the menu online. I had the cold matcha with coconut milk to drink, which was nicely balanced... until I let the ice melt, and then it was watery. We ordered to share (in the order they arrived): sautéed leafy greens, fried wild rice, fresh steamed tofu, avocado dosa, vegan einkorn pancakes, gluten free almond pancakes and vegan matcha crème brûlée. I particularly loved the first two. I had insisted on the tofu because I was concerned about getting very little protein from this meal, and it was an interesting dish that I definitely couldn't come close to making at home, though it wasn't my favourite. I thought the hot sauce on the table improved it a lot. I was worried the dosa would just be like a regular dosa, but it was a good choice anyway. You could really taste the fermentation of the batter, and it was a nice texture; thin but not overly crispy and not oily at all. I preferred the vegan pancakes to the gluten free ones, especially because the dough tasted like whole-grain wheat, and the toppings were a great complement to each other. It came with raspberry powder, rather than the fresh raspberries mentioned on the menu (they're out of season, we know), pears, and quince compote rather than fig compote. Not that I really know what a quince is, but it was good. Thankfully quince allergies are probably pretty uncommon. They also brought us some raspberry jam after we asked about the raspberries. After ordering, the service was kind of hands-off, which I thought was fine since we were happy to sit around and chat for a while. It was a nice open, airy space. We shared a long table with other guests, and had to speak somewhat loudly, but I didn't feel crowded.

I absolutely LOVE ABCV. The only downside is that it is difficult to get a reservation! I would eat everything on their menu, when we went for my Mother's Birthday Dinner there were a few dishes that we re ordered. There non alcoholic cocktails are delicious as well and don't taste medicinal as you may think. We have a wonderful experience and would definitely go back, look forward to my next visit!

Beautiful ambiance, fresh and delicious (and expensive) vegetables, and fun, inventive drinks (both alcohol and non alcoholic). 

Came with a large group for lunch- would recommend reservations. The restaurant was packed today (Friday at 1pm). A few standouts:

- cauliflower: the sauce was amazing, love the pomegranate and pistachio that accompanied the fish 
- carrots: possibly the best carrots I've ever had, the ground nut and seed butter was mouth watering, wish I could purchase it by the bottle 
-ramen: delicious and very flavorful, absolutely loved the smokiness
-chocolate and salted caramel tart: loved the brulèed banana, pomegranate seeds, coconut whipped cream 

Overall, loved the vibe of the place (you'll like spot some stars- we sat a few seats away from Martha Stewart and saw Mark Murphy walk into the kitchen), would be great for a date, too!

This is a restaurant that exists as a dichotomy. On the one hand, the food is good and inventive and the servers are pleasant enough. BUT, the prices are $2-3 higher for just about everything, the entrees came out individually as opposed to coordinated which was odd, and the coffee refills could have been quicker. 

However the most galling instance- and why they lost a star here- was that they let an entitled diner bring her dog into the dining room and sit on her lap. A health code violation and pretty ridiculous behavior.

Anyway, if you like paying for good ruff-age by all means have at it. Be aware of pooches.

The other reviews make it clear that the ambiance here is definitely one to write home about. I can attest that ABCV offers a clean atmosphere, with contemporary design that makes you want to eat well just by sitting in there! 

I LOVED the fact sheet they gave you with a rundown with the benefits of different veggies and fruits (some of which I didn't even know the benefits of). It really set the tone that this meal was meant to be ate mindfully. 

We came here for date night and were blown away by the food. Our server was extremely nice, and offered a lot of knowledge for each dish. One thing I would change is getting to the table within 5 minutes of us sitting down, by the time he came over we were sitting there for sometime and had a lot of questions. While I know he was busy, stopping by to introduce yourself would have went along way.

For food my boyfriend (omivore) and I (vegan) ordered 6 dishes which was just enough to fill us to a comfortable standard. We ordered the lettuce cups, artichokes (although the price is a big of a rip off given the size of the artichokes they were filled with flavor), donko mushrooms, carrots, the mushroom bolognese (pasta soaked in carrot juice giving it a great blend of flavors), spinach spaghetti (recommend to order with cheese  so this is a great dish for vegetarians) and the coconut custard to top it all of. All of which were delicious.

I'm looking forward to my next visit so I can switch it up a bit!

I was really looking forward to dining at abcV and unfortunately did not get an opportunity. Here's why:

I had a reservation for lunch at 1:30 (on a weekday). Checked in at 1:30, host said some tables are getting their checks so they should be getting up soon. 1:35, nothing. 1:40, nothing. By 1:45, (standing next to the host stand) I have heard more than 4 other groups check in for 1:30 reservations, but had been fed the same thing by the host that "some tables are paying, some are eating dessert, they should be getting up soon". There were at least 3 other groups of 2's, and 1 or more slightly larger group (3+). 

From 1:30 to 1:50, only 1 group of 2 with a 1:30 reservation was seated and it was a guy who showed up later than myself and 2 other groups, but gave the host a ton of attitude so he got seated first. 

Finally at 1:50, we asked for another update. At this point the 2nd hostess offered us a drink while we waited. While this is a nice gesture, it was after 20 minutes of waiting for our reservation, and it indicated to me that our table was nowhere near ready. So we left because we had 3:00 meetings. 

Look, if this was Friday or Saturday night, I would get it. But this is a weekday lunch. If you're going to charge $25 for a plate of radishes, you should at least be able to figure out how to get tables in and out at a reasonable pace for a weekday lunch and seat people with reservations within 15 min of their reservation. And the fact that it was not just us, there were so many other groups experiencing the same shit show, that's what prompted me to leave this review. 

(PS we went to Barbounia around the corner, were seated within 5 minutes, served our food within 10 minutes of ordering, and it was delicious.)

Oh my goodness, this place is delicious.
Yes, it's crowded. Yes, the hosts are super attitudinal. But the wait staff are friendly and even at crazy NYC brunch time, while you WILL wait, you will eventually get some of the most delicious vegetarian food in the city.
Recommended: avocado cups, lentils, khichri bowl, all the salads. The dosas are huge but delicious. 
Yes, if you are vegan you can eat here, but there are also dishes with eggs and cheese.
Don't sit anywhere near the door in winter as it's freaking freezing!

I'm a big fan of all ABC restaurants (ABC Kitchen and ABC Cocina) and this place also did not disappoint. Like the other ABCs, you order 2-3 dishes per person, tapas style. I would recommend ordering one or two things from each section of the menu, so you get a good varitey of light, cold, warm & heavy. Everything was a bit salty in my opinion, but not overpowering - I wouldn't mind eating salty at this restaurant since all ingredients are healthy anyway.

The beet dish was amazing - the slow roasted beets were cut so thinly and were served with avocado puree and pickles. Very flavorful and delicious. Also want to point out that the plating is beautiful on this one. The avocado lettuce cups were also amazing and was a good order to add some freshness to the meal. The most popular dish here seems to be the cauliflower (the half size is big enough for 3-4 people to share) - it was good with the tumeric tahini sauce but wasn't that special in my opinion.  The wild mushrooms under the "warm & hot" section of the menu was actually more like a mushroom salad. My favorite dish was definitely the spinach spaghetti which came out last and was the perfect finale dish. It was so creamy and garlicy, even without the parmagiano.

You can ask for all your dishes to be vegan and everything would still taste amazing.If all vegan food tasted like this or if I could eat here everyday, I would totally go vegan.
Love this place! Everything is delicious, the atmosphere is wonderful and decor is so light and airy!

Let's just say I was underwhelmed. Had nothing to do with the food; the service was aggressive and did not allow for an enjoyable experience. Upon sitting down I was welcomed and had the menu explained the twice since apparently we had two servers. I was also asked if I wanted drinks on 5 separate occasions - apparently looking at the food menu first is not allowed. 

As the food started coming it became obvious that the goal was just to turn over the table as quickly. Just as soon as the dish was 3/4 complete they were back to see if you were finished and some dishes were cleared with food remaining. At one point we were asked if we were still working on a dish that hadn't even been started. And asked again 5 minutes later when we were half way through it. The was table was cleared, bill brought out, charged and collected within a matter of minutes. 

The food was however lovely. A great mix of flavor combinations with great presentation. Highly recommend the mushroom bolognese for its amazing texture and rich flavor. The tofu was also phenomenal - light and combined with many distinct textures and tastes. 

Had this spot on my list for months and was truly looking forward to catching up with a close friend over dinner. Perhaps the wrong place for that us to spend an ample amount of time and just enjoy ourselves.

Just went I thought it couldn't get better! Jean-George made a vegetarian spot! I was so excited to try and was not disappointed at all. Grilled donko shiitakes and the fresh spinach spaghetti were my favorite. And you have to save room for dessert, coconut custard with wild berries :)

My girlfriends and I came on a Sunday Brunch. We had a good experience overall. Both food and drinks were quite yummy. We were more impressed by the service. The staff were kind and helpful with recommendations. 

The hummus was one of my favorite dishes. The portions are not big. We still managed to share everything. We love the ingredients in the dishes. The Almond pancakes were really good too. They have an actual brick-oven in the kitchen. 

We had an issue with our reservation in the beginning. The manager Sparrow) was very professional and kind. He handled our party very well. We greatly appreciate his manner. This was our first time to ABCv. We would return. We left full and happy.

I was really excited to try abcV because I love all of the other ABC restaurants, but unfortunately, it was underwhelming. We ordered the roasted potatoes, roasted cauliflower head, roasted beets, fried wild rice, matcha creme brûlée, and almond milk cappuccinos. Although the roasted vegetable items weren't horrible, they left much to be desired and fell short when it came to creativity and flavor. The fried wild rice, matcha creme brûlée, and almond milk cappuccinos were extremely delicious, but not enough to make me come back. All in all, I would still pick ABC Kitchen or ABC Cocina over their new sister restaurant, but will give them points for a light and bright menu, doing something different.

Went here for breakfast with a friend on a Thursday morning. The place was pretty busy, but we were able to be seated right away.

We were pretty hungry so we decided to split a few dishes:

Vanilla chia bowl (4.5 stars): This was probably our favorite dish of the meal--I don't know where they got the fruit, but it was some of the freshest I've ever tasted.

Dosa with butter and maple syrup (4 stars): I didn't know what to expect with this dish, but I actually really enjoyed this flavor combination.

Scrambled eggs with dill and broccoli (4 stars): Another solid dish--not very large, but eggs were cooked perfectly.

Overall, this place serves up some super fresh, healthy, clean food and does it well. The atmosphere was also superb and really added to the experience.

Hostes has to go. Unpleasant, unprofessional, nothing positive about her.

The rest is excellent from choice of china, silverware, acoustic, furnitures, waiters, and of course food.

Party of two:
Fried wild rice with vegetable- very interesting flavors.
Tofu: just about right in spiciness.
Artichokes salad: I loved it. Very well balance citrus flavor and herbs.
Pasta with "meat": delicious (I believe it was a special that night.)
Coconut sticky rice: very sweet but overall enjoyable.
Matcha custard: not my favorite but still a good dessert and not heavy.
Coconut pudding: I enjoyed it very much and also not heavy to digest. 

My server was Daniel and he was professional, attentive, and polite. 

I will definitely go back to try more dishes.

While the food was delicious, service was a bit slow. We went for brunch on Saturday and were told there would be a 75 min wait. I left my phone number and received a text we were added to the waitlist and would receive a text when our table was ready. After 1 hour and 45 min, we returned to the restaurant to see if our table was ready. We walked in to see three two tops empty, so we were confused as to why were not contacted. When I asked how much longer the wait was, we were told that our table was paying the check. As we waited, we saw the server split a communal table with a flower pot and proceeded to tell us our table was ready.......

We sat down and were told that a server would be with us shortly. After contemplating what to get, and getting some recommendations from our server, we order the Sweet Potato bowl, Coconut Yogurt with Citrus, and Slow Roasted Beets. Everything was delicious. The sweet potato bowl was comforting, the coconut yogurt bright and refreshing and the slow roasted beets were the perfect combination of sweet, salty, and sour. 

Everything was going well until I bit down on a clump of dirt from the beets. At first, I wasn't sure what I was eating, but I removed it from my mouth and saw it was dirt. I asked the server for a new plate and fork because I had just eaten dirt and his reaction was a bit disappointing. While he seemed surprised, he just stated, "oh!" and walked away with my plate and brought me a new plate a fork. He then walked away. 

Normally in these situations, a manager would be called and he or she would would apologize for the mishap. This is at least how all mistakes were handled when I worked as a server. However I got nothing of the sort. All I got was an "oh!" We were also still charged for beets which was disappointing. 

I tried to just brush off the incident, however, I can't stop thinking that something should have been done about the fact that I had to rinse my mouth multiple times to get all the grit out of my teeth. 

I expected great things from ABCV, and while the food really was delicious, I can't seem to get this bad taste out of my mouth.

I went to dinner at ABCV with my good friend, and author, Rebecca Brooks, who happens to be a vegetarian. I'm always intrigued when restaurants make vegetables taste delicious and interesting. We picked a variety of small plates, but my favorite, by far were the carrots. The description sounded a little strange -- seed and nut butter, chiles, limes -- I didn't know if these things would work with heirloom carrots. But, this dish was outstanding.

The cocktails are fruit and veggie forward and they're amazing. Service was excellent - attentive without being overbearing. And we even had a celebrity sighting.

Vegetarians will love ABCV, but carnivores won't feel like they're missing out.

The mushroom walnut bolognese and honeynut dip were ....my issue with ABCV lands with the service and overall dining experience. I arrived with a close friend of mine and felt like I was being served as a number. It was as if the name of the game was "who can turn the table faster" as we had two servers that asked us what we wanted to drink 5 times prior to ordering.

Once the food started to arrive it felt better but then after the third dish, we were rushed again. It even got to a point where a dish hadn't been touched and were asked if we were done. 

Needless to say although I found our food to be quite nice, I don't feel a strong desire or need to return which is unfortunate as I was really excited to come here.

One standout dish out of many tried, mediocre ambiance, and mediocre service.

We had a reservation for Monday evening and came 10 minutes before, but still had to wait probably around half an hour to get seated. Duuuuude come on.

Green chickpea hummus: Good! But so is hummus from the grocery store. Basically, it's good but not impressive. Not hard to make good.

Honeynut squash: No flavor

Avocado lettuce cups: Good, but also not impressive. 

Whole roasted cauliflower: Mushy, not good flavor. It also took forever. Wtf? I thought roasted cauliflowers are a bit crisp, not wet. Ugh.

Whole roasted celery root: GOOD. Good flavor, unusual (at least to me) item, and interesting. 

Fried wild rice: It's just spicy and if you really want to know, I like my Japanese fried rice from Trader Joe's, the $2 or $3 frozen bag better. Try harder lol

The food takes literally forever to come. And if you usually eat meat, it will be hard to fill up. Maybe come during the summer when you want to eat light, or better yet, don't come at all!

Immediately walking in, I notice this place is packed. Food is tapas style. 
I will warn you that this is not the place to come to if you are hungry!

We ordered the following: Cauliflower, avocado wraps, ramen, edema me chickpeas hummus and the spinach spaghetti.

Out of these my favorite is the Cauliflower which is served with this amazing curry sauce that you can pour over the dish. Next favorite were the edema me chickpeas hummus and the spinach spaghetti. I'd say my least favorite was the ramen ( which was too salty and dry  for my taste, and not served with ramen). It is not served with any broth. 

For drinks: 
I ordered the pear drink which is a light drink but delicious.

I would definitely come back here again.
Horrible service. Staff are completely disorganized and seems like they have never worked in a restaurant before. Food is decent but entirely over-priced. Do not recommend.

*Qualifier:  I've been to most vegetarian/vegan spots in NYC and prior to my vegan lifestyle, have been to most of the top notch non-vegan restaurants in the city over the past 12 years.  

*Reaction:  This place is phenomenal.  Each of the 5 dishes we ordered were truly great and extremely unique.  The atmosphere was a perfect mix of trendy and super friendly.  Our waiter couldn't have been more helpful (checking in on us often and recommending dishes based on our preferences).  Most of the time when I go to vegetarian places, I feel like I'm missing out on the action.  Not at ABCV.  Seriously, new favorite vegetarian spot in the city.  We are going back.  Compliments to chef and management.
Awesome vibe and decorations, delicious food, wonderful service, and creative menu. The food is tapas style - it's pricey but worth the experience. Would definitely return!

This is one of the most amazing meals I have had in recent memory. Some of you might be skeptical because it's vegetarian. I get it. But this experience will blow your mind. We had the wild mushrooms, the honey squash, the hummus, the dosa (with vegan yogurt), the ramen and the cauliflower. I don't even know what to say is the best because it was all so flavorful and amazing! For dessert we had the chocolate tart which was the perfect mix between salty and sweet. The decor and the service of this restaurant is impeccable. I cannot wait to go back!
Excellent food and service. Overall a culinary experience!

Food: 4.5
Visual: 5
Staff/Wait time: 3

As a new vegetarian, finding a solid vegetarian restaurant is tantamount. ABCV is very solid. Went there for dinner and ordered: 

1. slow roasted beets: tangy and tasty
2. honeynut squash: sweet but balanced
3. roasted market potatoes: very good, my favorite dish of the night
4. warm crimini and chanterelles: umami 
5. fresh spinach spaghetti: good but not unique
6. vegan coconut custard: so fresh and amazing, particularly if you like coconut 
7. matcha creme brûlée: pretty good, get only if you like matcha
 
Cons: One of the hostesses was a little rude/seemed overwhelmed. Had a 8:30 reservation and was seated at 9:45 without much regretful acknowledgement or olive branch. 

Overall would recommend. But not often, as it is pricey and the wait time is long.

We made reservations for 8:30 pm dinner on Sunday night and were seated shortly after. Our servers were attentive, informative, and friendly. I would say the service here is decent - nothing extra spectacular but definitely not average. 

The dishes were all tapas size and would definitely recommend that you share the dishes. Our server informed us that the dishes go from light to hearty in the order of the menu. For two, we were full with the 4 dishes we ordered. 

We had the honeynut squash with pita bread, a half roasted cauliflower, wok fried ramen noodle, and the fresh tofu with Szechuan sauce. The honeynut squash was unique but not our favorite and something we probably wouldn't get again. We liked the soft texture of the cauliflower but did not care for the turmeric sauce that came with it, instead we preferred using the hot sauce that was on the table. The wok fried ramen noodles were chewy and had all kinds of flavor profile. I liked the soft small cubes that imitated the taste of meat and the tender Brussels sprouts. Our favorite was the tofu with the Szechuan pepper. The tofu was very soft and delicate and the sauce had the right amount of heat. It had very natural Asian flavors and was very reminiscent of the popular Chinese dish mapo tofu. 

We enjoyed our experience here. I liked the vegetarian take on the typical meat dishes. And I would come back again to try some of the other things on the menu.

One of my favourite vegetarian spots in NY. The portions are on the smaller side but I liked that I could sample different dishes - tapas style. Food is Indian inspired with light delicate flavours. The drinks were surprisingly strong too! I had the matcha mojito and it was so good. Only downside is that I wished they had a vegan menu to make ordering easier. The presentation of the food is beautiful, and so is the decor inside, as you would expect from an extension of ABC kitchen. Well done Jean Georges!

Ordered: Walnut Bolgnese and Butternut Squash Soup. Both could be made vegan.

Pros: The soup had an amazing taste. Gave me all the Thanksgiving vibes. Meant to look to see if sage was in it. The walnut was a great meat substitute in the bolgnese. A lady next to me at bar ordered the cauliflower and I definitely had food envy.

Cons: Though I liked the walnuts in the bolgnese, the sauce in general was not great. I couldn't pinpoint the ingredient that left a bad taste to my mouth. 

Would love to come back and try something else.

Finally made reservations here for brunch with a friend. 
The decor is soooo cute- I loved everything from the lighting  to the serving plates. 

We sat down and had our menu over to us quickly. My friend ordered the matcha coconut refresher which was delicious, and I had their cold brew with almond milk. 

For our meal- I had the mushrooms with poached farm eggs ($17) and my friend ordered the almond pancakes ($17). Our meals were okay- I was still hungry after devouring my dish :( and it's a little pricey for what you get. Glad I went there for the decor, but the food not so much.
Went here for breakfast by myself a while back, it was a really peaceful atmosphere the food was delicious.
Food was palatable, but nothing special, especially for the price (I went with the waiter's recommendations). Service was good.

Delicious food! But a little pricey for what it is and my waiter sadly included Cheese even though I mentioned I was vegan. The waiting space in the front is too cramped -- even for New York standards but the decor is beautiful. Definitely make a reservation in advance and get the ragu! Holy life changing!

I was so excited to try this restaurant because of the excellent reviews I read on Yelp, but unfortunately my expectations were far from met. The restaurant itself is beautiful, I love the all white decor and the interesting light fixtures. The staff was kind and accommodating- we added an extra person to our reservation last minute and they still sat us on time. We ordered drinks first; my wine was $15 but that's not unusual for Manhattan. When we started to order food the waiter informed us that we needed to order NINE entrees to share between 3 people. I've been to tapa restaurants before and would've been okay with this if each item wasn't on average about $20 a piece. I was not in the mood to pay for over $200 for dinner and drinks. We ordered 4 things between us. The food tasted good but the portions were so small. We left hungry and dissatisfied.

Dinner here was an incredible experience in a beautiful space. My husband, a carnivore, and I, a vegan, split 6 delicious dishes. We both left satisfied and impressed. They are very accommodating to gluten and dairy allergies.

I was really excited to go to abcV and we finally got the chance! My partner and I planned a date night, made a reservation, and even called ahead to confirm. When we got there they sat us at a table full of other people (when there were other private tables available) I understand the use of these long group tables and it would make sense to sit a couple there for a walk-in dinner, but we had planned this a month before and gave notice, even after we made a reservation, that we would be there. I found that rude of the hostess (we even got there 10 minutes early and waited!) For the price you pay you should have a nice experience and feel cared for, since the food is only good not great. I enjoyed the fried rice and pesto noodles, but had a bit of a stomach ache after so I wonder if they use a lot of oil... Portions are decent, but not consistent. From what we got and what I saw other tables had, some were normal and others quite small. I did really enjoy their Pear & Rose cocktail, we tried a few others and I would only highly recommend that one. We want to come again for brunch since that menu looked more appealing to me, but I'm really turned off by the hosting and seating situation- not very romantic.

Came here a few days ago for brunch last minute. I would suggest making a reservation it is very popular! I came with a date and we sat at the bar. The inside is beautifully designed and the staff is super friendly! The food is beautifully put together and is vegan friendly. As someone who eats first with my eyes, I was very pleased! Servings are a bit small compared to other brunch spots, but they make up for it in quality. I ordered a latte and the pancakes which tasted amazing. My date ordered the yogurt and we split avocado toast. They bake their bread fresh daily! Would come back for the extensive cocktail menu

This is a great place for a nice dinner out. The food was delish and the diversity of options was great. As a vegetarian an entire restaurant at this quality was like a dream come true! Don't worry meat eaters. You won't miss it! I would absolutely come again and recommend it to anyone visiting the city.

I had looked forward to going to eat here for a long time with a friend, from overseas,  that is Vegan.  Finally everything aligned and able to get a reservation this past Tuesday evening.  We were seated and it was soo loud!  we couldn't hear each other across the small table and the couldn't hear the server (nor could she hear us).  It was as if we were at a club on a Friday night .  We were told it was the bad acoustics of the space.  Definitely not like this at ABC Kitchen (which I love!).
The noise was deafening and I could see that my friend was miserable. So, we left without eating.   Really a shame.  Don't think the noise goes with the atmosphere or the vibe of ABC.  Maybe time to do a renovation of the space (?)

We came here to celebrate our one year anniversary and our servers Cooper and Nathan made it more memorable and special than we could have imagined.

They're service and hospitality was unforgettable and they helped us to pick dishes that were absolutely delicious. 

The cauliflower is great and won't disappoint you had it is nicely roasted and paired with a lot of garnishes that add multiple layers of flavor (the turmeric sauce is also great). 

The grilled shiitake mushrooms and mushroom "bolognese" were my favorites, and I'd pass on the preserved lemon and green kale pasta as it was a little too acidic from the lemon (it overpowered the other flavors and we love lemon). 

Thank you Cooper and Nathan!

Incredible vegan and vegetarian food! So fresh and flavorful and almost everything can be made dairy free. They are able to add so much flavor into all the dishes and use a variety of flavors. The lettuce cups, green chickpea hummus and dosa with cashew yogurt.l are some of my favorites. It's nice that everything comes tapas style to share. Matcha iced tea and matcha colada are favorite drinks. Don't leave without trying the pumpkin cheesecake!  Pleasant low key atmosphere with insanely delicious plant based cuisine - highly recommend!

Incredible, the food was SO good, as was the service. On the more expensive side, but honestly worth it. 

Started with the pine nut dip--delicious, but paled in comparison to the rest of the meal. The Cauliflower was superb with the turmeric sauce, and the carrots... Man the carrots were to die for. I'm a huge nut fan, so the savory nut butter was such a simple addition but made it above and beyond. My friend also got the spinach pasta which i couldn't try because of the dairy, but she loved it and ate every last bite as well. 

Have been meaning to try this place for a while, and definitely one of my new favorite restaurants--great staff, decor, vibe, food, everything.

Have been frequenting ABC V for some time and I love the concept and many of the dishes. However, yesterday I had the veggie fried rice and woke up to an MSG headache. I would never in a million years think that ABC V a place promoting health would use such a toxic ingredient in one of the dishes. It must be in the soy sauce used---but it's unacceptable for such a restaurant promoting health to use products containing dangerous chemicals. 

I will not be back after that experience.

The cauliflower and mushroom bolognese were standouts. Overall, very good food but weak and very expensive drinks. Three drinks (one weak, but tasty, mezcal cocktail and two glasses of wine) added ~$50 to the bill. Do happy hour somewhere else but come for the food.
