Had reservations for brunch on a weekday and was incredibly impressed at how this place made me forget that I was eating at an all vegetarian restaurant. 

We tried the vegan pastry basket which again, couldn't believe I was eating vegan and couldn't even notice the difference. 

What we ordered:
-vegan pastry basket - GET THIS! Perfect portion to share for 2 people 
-beluga lentils - so incredibly flavorful.  small portion, definitely have to supplement with another dish if this is all you're ordering. GET THIS! 
-avocado lettuce cups - GET THIS! again, so flavorful with the serrano and lime, pepitas gave it an interesting texture
-wild mushroom poached farm eggs - GET THIS! again, so much flavor! 

All in all this place made me want to become vegetarian for like 15 minutes. Then I thought about pepperoni.

ABC is 2 popular 4 me. I made reservations about three weeks in advance for Friday night dinner and when we arrived, we still faced a 20 minute wait in the cramped bar area. Not fun.

As you may know, abcV's shtick is vegetable-driven food, and apparently health in general as the drink list is dotted with juices, kombuchas, and "vibrations." We each got a vibration, I believe Connect and Mindful, for $12 each. Neither were enjoyed. I would stick with alcohol here.

They have a wide menu here, with dishes in the teens and low twenties. We did four and a dessert, which was just right for two.

First off was the green chickpea hummus with pita, one of their signature dishes. It's more pea-y then hummus-y, with a bright vegetal flavor. Good but didn't knock my socks off.

Second was the grilled donko shiitake, which ended up being our favorite dish. They brought out a nice meaty note from the mushrooms, and the sauce and fennel complemented it well. Recommended.

Third was the wok fried ramen noodle. It was a smaller portion and failed to have a coherent flavor profile. I'd skip.

Fourth was the whole celery root. This was unique and tasty, with a quite good curry sauce. The pomegranate seeds added visual interest but didn't seem to fit.

Finally we opted for a pumpkin cheesecake dessert, which tasted like Thanksgiving in a glass complete with cranberries. A little rich for my palate but enjoyed.

Service is well trained. When they brought the bill, they told us that we had drinks at the bar before being seated, which we didn't, and they quickly got it taken off. The meal ended up being on the quicker side, about an hour from being seated to finishing.

I don't know that I get what's so special about this place. It's more tastefully decorated than Cocina, and it's a good atmosphere, but the food didn't bowl me over. High prices and small portions, that standard Manhattan complaint, but really. I wouldn't say we feasted but it ended up being $70 a person after tax and tip.

Finally, I wouldn't recommend bringing anyone with a nut allergy here as they seem to use it widely in dishes and desserts. They will accommodate you if you ask but I would recommend not risking it. My boyfriend had an allergic reaction to a dessert that supposedly only contained almonds, which he eats occasionally and doesn't normally react to. Trying not to overweight that in my review of the rest but an FYI for those with allergens.

My favorite of all the ABC restaurants! Two people and I shared the following and it was more than enough:

+ plain dosa
+ beluga lentils
+ whole roasted cauliflower 
+ fresh spinach spaghetti
+ coconut sticky rice
+ salted caramel chocolate tart
+ pumpkin cheesecake 

Everything was excellent, but the cauliflower, spaghetti and coconut rice were truly exquisite. I'd never had dosa before and it was nothing like I expected, in a good way. The desserts were delicious. Overall, I found the flavors to be exciting and inspired, and the lentils offered some filling protein (I was concerned I'd be hungry if I just ate veggies, but this was a great solution.) Finally, service was great!

Ok guys- healthy. Vegetarian. Delicious? Yes! 

I know I was surprised too, but upon arriving on a Tuesday around 2:00 there was about an hour wait so we opted into sitting at the bar.

 My roommate and I ordered some energizing drinks and a slew of tapas style things from the menu. My favorites were definitely the beets and the pear tartine- so filling and delicious!

Now it might hurt your wallet a bit, but it's refreshing, FLAVORFUL and worth it if you feel like treating yourself but not feeling guilty about it!

If you are in the area, try it out and then go shopping at their coordinating store!
This Jean Georges restaurant is on the high end for price, but was easily the best Acai bowl I've had in NYC. Well worth it. Pretty trendy place so make a reservation before to avoid a wait.

My boyfriend took me here for a belated Valentine's day dinner and honestly just sitting across from him just about anything is 5 stars but I have to be objective here....

We had a 5pm reservation because that was all that was available on a Saturday night. Totally fine. We sat down right at 5 and were told to order about 3-5 dishes between the two of us. We ordered four and the waiter than says that we should actually do 5. Okay. Fresh spinach spaghetti, dosa, coconut sticky rice, and i think fresh hearts of palm and carrots? I actually don't remember the last two, even while reading the menu, though it is possible the menu has changed.

The food itself (and the cocktail I had) was extremely delicious, with complex flavors that I had not tasted before and that right there makes it a really awesome experience.

I was surprised with where we were going to dinner, so I did not have a chance to study the menu, but I find it concerning that nowhere on their website or the menu does it actually indicate that its small plates that you share. My boyfriend says he knew, but quite frankly $25 per entree is a nice dinner for us, and this was $25 per small plate.

I didn't really dock a star for that, per se, because maybe that's just something people fancier than myself know. However, while the food was delicious, even having 5 plates between us, I was still hungry. My boyfriend offered for us to get more food and I was like honestly I would rather just go home and eat real dinner at 8pm.

Which leads to my other major complaint--we were rushed, to say the least. Our second plate arrived as we were still finishing the first, and that repeated through all 5 plates. We were in and out of there in 1 hour--so my fancy Valentine's Day dinner lasted from 5pm-6pm. When I drop $150+ on dinner, I expect for it to be a whole experience. I have had meals at the corner pizza joint last longer and feel less rushed than that.

TL;DR: If you have lots of money and regularly spend lots of money on dinner, go here, enjoy it, the food tastes great. If you do not have a lot of money and you save going to nice places for special occasions, go somewhere else for a better full experience.

I have been here a few times and have enjoyed the food very much. I would recommend going here for that. 

The last time I went here, though, I was disappointed for various reasons. Firstly, it took great effort to get our water glasses refilled regularly. Secondly, I disagree with how many plates per person we should have ordered. We were told to order 2 plates per person which I honestly think may be a tactic to over order and get the bill higher. This is just way too much food! Perhaps some dishes are lighter than others, but the sweet potato dish we had at brunch was dense and filling and was enough for 1 person to be more than satisfied. I am glad we only ordered 3 in total (2 people dining), as we had leftovers (and we were hungry!). 

What really offended me the last time I was here was the price of the citrus fruit "bowl". It was $12 which is already robbery, but when this bowl came out it was SHOCKING. There were literally 6 pieces of citrus slices that I could easily cup in the palm of my hand. FOR $12!!! I complained about this to the waiter and he really had no justification for the price other than that they were recently increased. Not to mention, when the bill came, they charged me $14 (!!!) for it and I had to have it corrected! At that point, they should have taken it off the bill, But no. We had to wait quite a while for the bill to be adjusted while we sat there thirstily. I won't be going back any time soon.

ABCV is one of the best culinary experiences in NYC! From the stellar service to the fresh ingredients, genius recipes and soothing ambiance I cannot get enough of this place. I recently visited for the second time, on a weekday and they were just as crowded as when they opened last year. Despite the crowd, the host and bartenders were friendly, pleasantly and treated me like a guest in their home. The food was excellent (get the Cauliflower steak!) the drinks were refreshing, and the sever was SO sweet and knowledgeable about the menu. Run, don't walk to ABCV if you're anywhere near Union Square.

I'm only giving this place two stars for the waiters who served us (who were very nice, my Latino man and two black man) and I guess the ambiance 
Listen
I never do this
Look at my other reviews, it's not hard to impress me, but I was so disappointed in this place
I'm not the type of person to return a dish
Ever, I can find a hair in there and still not complain because hey shit happens
But when it's a high end restaurant, and the portions are small and expensive and you hear all these great things about the chef
Blabla, POINT IS, food was SOOO FUCKING SALTY
I will never return food just because I don't have the heart to do that, (i was raised Latina, we don't return back food, it's rude) I pushed down my extremely salty lemonly spaghetti but my sister could not, she didn't return her food once, not twice , THREE TIMES, she would have done it the fourth time if it were not for my lovely mother visiting all the way from South America, (we honestly just wanted to leave) but my mom got sad seeing my sister not enjoying her food so she was stuck to eat her third replacement, and if my own sister says it's salty, YOU KNOW it's salty because that girl puts extra salt on everything 
On the third dish we even told them to just please go light on the salt but still came out salty
Luckily my mom got some dish with grapefruit so she loved hers but she even said hers was a bit salty but not to the point of having to return it
Price and overall taste was not worth it
I'm like looking all around me , trying to see if other people were dealing with the same but all I saw were white people so who knows maybe they love the salty flavor! 
The only good thing was the green hummus, we kept asking for more pita bread because it was the only good thing
There is so much more better vegan places that are way cheaper AND healthier

I have been here for lunch a couple times, and left a little underwhelmed both times. I love the concept, but really don't quite understand the price point both for the food and the ambience. Enjoyed the hummus and carrots. Are you kidding me @ $19 for dosa with yogurt? Like omg that's literally like a tsp of fermented rice served with yogurt. I love NY city food scene, but I think sometimes we get carried away a little.

Everything about this dining experience was absolutely perfect.  I went there with a friend who had also never been there before, neither of us had any real idea what to expect.  The menu is a little intimidating, with many many items in all sections and ingredients I expect most people are at least a little unfamiliar with.  This said, every one of the eight dishes we tried were absolutely incredible.  The plating was beautiful and unexpected.  Each dish was seasoned to perfection.  I didn't expect that my likely favorite dish of this year was going to be market carrots, but here we are.  They're served with a nut and seed butter and fresh chiles, creating this wild spicy crunchy condiment that is honestly unlike any other sauce I've ever had.  The beets with dijon, avocado, and pickles are also not to be missed.  We had the vegan matcha creme brulee and the vegan coconut custard, and I was floored.  I've never tasted such rich creamy vegan desserts.  The staff was all wonderful and helpful.  Our waitress, Allie, was absolutely a delight.  It's a little on the pricey side, but this is definitely a place where there's value behind the price tag.  I don't think I'm going to have a better meal this year and I can't recommend this place hard enough.

Greatest vegan food I have ever experienced. Bright, friendly, energetic space and sophisticated preparation from top notch ingredients. While there may be some small issues regarding service and I can perceive that some may question value, I would definitely repeat. Fantastic flavors without being over seasoned and a good variety of options. In my opinion, the freshness of the produce came through in every dish. Desserts are excellent, try the matcha crème brûlée! I am not vegan nor vegetarian but can really appreciate what they are trying to do here.

ABCV is an upscale vegetarian restaurant that is part of ABC Kitchen & ABC Cocina. This place is good for a special occasion or if you're feeling like going a little fancy on the veggie night. The creativity and presentation of all the food is certainly 5 stars. The only reason why I can't give an overall 5 star rating is because taste was about a 4 and after trying many vegan/ vegetarian dishes in the city, ABCV didn't stand out for taste alone. Still recommend trying this place!

Had dinner on Friday night. Arrived around 8pm, joint was packed!
What they got right- environment is inviting and energetic. Lighting was good, restaurant was set up properly. I had arrived with a friend and we ordered about 7 courses. The two best are the Market carrots with the nut butter and the other awesome plate is the grilled baby artichoke with citrus and olive oil and basil. The dishes did not look to be anything unique but I will correct this, these were the very best dishes last night. 
What I did not find perfect- wines by glass options. I tried a couple  but they were mediocre to average. The fennel dish, one of the seven dishes ordered was overly oiled up. I enjoyed the avocado lettuce cups but there is an element missing in my opinion. It's close to amazing but could use a speck of cumin or perhaps another spice/herb.
Overall, a good experience. Vegan dishes can be difficult to achieve amazing but this joint was able to pull off a couple of great dishes.

Long overdue to try the newest restaurant in JG's ABC line, but glad to say that I did it with a bang (went with 7 people and tried a large part of the menu), and that despite not having any meat on the menu, abcV is still delicious. 

We tried the green chickpea hummus, avocado lettuce cups, fresh hearts of peach palm, warm crimini and morel mushrooms, wood grilled baby artichokes, whole roasted cauliflower, mushroom walnut bolognese, fresh spinach spaghetti, and dosa. Everything was fresh, delicious, and you can almost fool yourself into thinking that you're eating healthy. Standouts for me included the mushroom walnut bolognese, roasted cauliflower, and dosa. 

Finished off the meal with a selection of yummy desserts which included the salted caramel chocolate tart and vegan matcha creme brulee.

100% worth the effort to get a reservation.

One star ding because my cocktail tasted too medicinal (I got the matcha colada) and service was near impossible to get at points.

I have never been served such a ridiculously small portion of soup before. I posted a pic. The soup barely covered half of my spoon TIP. I questioned if it was possible my friend and I got the last of it given the portion was so small. The bar staff were extremely gracious and asked the question to the kitchen but it was returned saying it was a standard serve. Oliver Twist was served a larger portion!
$17 for half a mug of soup is pretty stingy by anyone's standards.  I spent USD$40 in total, soup, juice and tip, and left hungry. 
If they're going to serve that portion maybe they should at least consider a slice of bread?!

Brilliant, eclectic, creative. Those are the words that come to mind when I think of ABCV. The service is top notch and the servers really take the time and make you feel welcome. The food is unbelievably delicious and healthy, and you will leave as a raving fan of this place.
Food is great but portions are not small. Servers told us to get 4-5 dishes for 2 people but we only needed 2-3. We overate and also had leftovers.

As a meat eater, I'm surprised that ABCV was my favorite of the Jean George restaurants. Every dish highlighted the true aesthetic and flavors of the ingredients. The roasted cauliflower is the obvious star dish here but be sure to sample all of your favorite veggies done extremely well! 

-@EricHoRaw
We ordered cauliflower and avocado lettuce cups, both the dishes are simply amazing, good presentation. Rhubarb Pavlova dessert is so delicious, must try for everyone.

Sat at the bar w a friend on a rainy weekday for lunch. Grabbed two seats at the bar and watched people hustle in and out. The servers behind the bar were delightful, friendly and v helpful.

The food was gorgeous and delicious. Get the carrots. They will change your life. Everything here though is delicious, layered w flavor and will end up being a party in your mouth. Bon appetite!

Don't let overpriced food fool you, this place is nothing but average. The service is what is to expect from $$$ restaurant. Good bordering alright. The ambiance is nice and inviting. 

The food it's self is nothing that most couldn't cook them selfs if they too had a heavy hand with the spice drawer. The food is not bad and somethings we had were good, like the slow roasted beats and the shiitake mushrooms (even though they are not very consistent, each mushroom tasted different and one of them almost ruined the plate it's self for me). Other than that the rest is mostly over spiced and definitely not worth what your paying for. This place is not bad by any means but the food just isn't worth its price.

Where to start. I visited ABCV Thursday for the first time with high expectation after all it is Jean-George's restaurant. That being said I feel that the food was lack luster. The ingredients where fresh and amazing but the preparation was nothing special. I ordered the green chick pea hummus, sour croat and the warm crimini and morel mushroom. all three where way over salted almost to the point of being inedible. There are many better vegan place to eat in the city I don't understand the hype around this place.

This vegetarian member of the JG family lives up to the hype! Went for lunch on a Tuesday and it was slammed. We tried the famous roasted cauliflower as well as two other dishes- a spicy ramen and a light and fresh tofu. Every bite was flavorful and delicious. His food is unique and presentation is on point. The service was great! The price for lunch for two 85 dollars. Great place for a special occasion or a fellow foodie. Delicious!

I really enjoyed my dining experience here. From the bartender to the wait staff, and of course the food, were all exceptional. I recommend you book a reservation as my husband and I dined in on a Wednesday for early dinner (5:30) and it was packed! My favorite dish was the slow roasted beets; my husband loved the cauliflower. But seriously, they were all amazing. Can't wait to come back!

The reason I decided to try out ABCV was actually do to the buzzfeed worth it video about vegan restaurants. However, just to clarify, the V stands for vegetarian, but they can make almost everything vegan and gluten free. The food was overall really tasty. My favorite was the coconut sticky rice and matcha creme brûlée. I wasn't really a fan of the spinach pasta or morel mushroom wontons. The Kombucha was also amazing. They also say for 2 people that 5-6 dishes is just right, but I honestly would've been fine with just 4. Everything was really filling. I think it's worth trying out. The only reason for four stars is due to the price. Very overpriced.

Yum! Some of the best vegan food money can buy! Definitely unique flavors and combinations and worth the hype. I highly recommend the tofu and the roasted cauliflower. Won't be including too many details as many people have pictures and descriptions of these already. Just adding that I also thought they were delicious

The bolognese was a little disappointing, not much deep flavor and the pavlova was way too sweet and the meringue was too hard. Also, the price point is a little high considering everything. The food is definitely delicious but feels slightly overpriced for what they are, especially considering some of the dishes weren't "amazing". So overall I'm giving it 4 stars.
Food is great.  Service is awful.  Waitperson is never around.  They need to get their act together.
Not bad but really not worth the hype! Serving portions are way too small. And dishes are hit or miss. Net net it is ok, but won't go back

If every restaurant could serve this kind of vegan food, I might actually become one. 

We came here for my friends birthday and I was happily surprised. She is dairy free and LOVEs this restaurant so it was natural that we came here. I expected to need a meal after my meal, but that wasn't the case! 

The portions were good size and everything was delicious and filling. Plus if it's good enough for Chrissy Teigen, it's good enough for me!

Went on a Friday morning so didn't have any trouble getting a table. I ordered an americano and asked for it three times, and each time I asked a waiter, they said it was coming. After 20 minutes, my friend finished hers and I was still waiting. I asked again and they went back to check this time and said they never put it in.... but then why did you say it was coming, three times in a row?!

Ordered the vegan croissant, waited for 15 minutes, they come back and say they're not available. So put in for matcha muffins, waited another 15 minutes for these. These we're super yummy, I have to say. Not too sweet and on the smaller side. It was served warm and there were berries inside. Came with vegan butter- sooooo good! 30 minute later, got my smoothie bowl: sea buckthorn mango- pretty good! Light and airy, frothy on top. 

A bit pricey for what you get. Juices and smoothie bowls are like $18. If you're looking for vegan options, worth a try, but be prepared to wait for your food!

This is a great restaurant for when you're trying to eat healthy but also want to indulge a little bit. Everything i tried here was incredible. The cauliflower was amazing, as expected. 

The interior is really cute as well. Great place to grab dinner with a friend.

Disclaimer: Let me start off by saying I was totally being a hater when my friends said we were coming here for lunch. I had given up meat for a while but was back to eating it so the last place I wanted to go was a place that did not have any.

Annoyed and hangry I entered this cute little place. A little cramped in the front with people waiting but the tables and seating area is spacious one you are in it. As for the food, well it was....AMAZING. Ugh I cannot lie, I loved everything we ordered.

Green chickpea hummus: great starter. Yes, you CAN mess up hummus and this stuff was great especially with their house hot sauce. 

Avocado lettuce cups: Cute, filling and just the right amount of avocado.

Whole roasted cauliflower: I am not a fan of cauliflower and this was a surprisingly great dish. 

Wok fried ramen noodle: not a lot of noodles but a nice carb addition to the vegetables.

Fresh spinach spaghetti: again, not a lot of noodles, very small dish but a nice carb to add to the meal and substantial for anyone pissed about the meat situation.

The dishes again were great, however be aware that this place is pricey. I shared the above with a few people and we all left satiated. The portions are also very small so make note of that. This is def a cute place to bring an out of towner to show them trendy NYC and a great option (I think for both people who eat meat and those who do not). 

I hate to say it, especially since I was such a complainer to my friends, but I think i secretly would go back.......Okay I would def go back!

Despite a "false start" - hostess being a little difficult - we were glad to discover this veggie-focused place. 

Our order:
- baby artichoke
- asparagus
- peach palm hearts
- morel mushrooms wontons (a little bit small for the price).

Beware ... Place is quite noisy ... and busy !

This vegetarian joint is a great spot for breakfast during the work week. The ambiance is bright, light and a bit rustic, but in a polished way (does that make sense?) Anyway, I almost went with my old faithful avocado toast and decided to be a bit adventurous and try to yogurt and avocado dosa - boy am I glad I did. I LOVED it. I kept braking off a piece of dosa and making a little bite with avocado, yogurt and greens. I took my time and enjoyed every bite. Wow. When I got home from work, I was already talking to my partner about when we can go back. Go and choose the adventure!

As much as I love dairy and wheat, they do not love me. I was so thrilled to eat at a place with delicious dishes that didn't have wheat OR dairy in them and didn't give me a hard time about my dietary restrictions. I had the Elevate juice, which was tart and tasty. We tried the coconut yogurt brunch bowl, which was perfect. We had the scrambled and poached egg dishes, which were good. Then the almond pancakes with coconut cream on top. So. Good. I never get to eat pancakes, so I was so grateful for these. Would be happy to eat breakfast here every day.

I dined here this evening. I had made a reservation for two for 5:30 but at 5:40 got a call from my friend that she got the dates mixed up and would not be able to come. It's tough to get a table here so I asked the host if they wanted the table back or if I should just stay. The host and the waiters were all incredibly gracious and seated me anyway. The meal was exquisite and so nice to have something delicious that is still quite healthy. I was very grateful to the staff for taking such good care of me despite my party shrinking from two to one at the last minute.

Icame for lunch last week as I had to really want to try this place out. Super busy and with no reservations impossible to get a seat but the hostess could not have been nicer and I was able to squeeze in at the bar. They have hooks for handbags! Yay  bar staff was incredibly friendly and helpful. I ordered a glass of wine and the mushroom Bolognese dish. Excellent food! Very very tasty but at $21 it was a tiny portion. Really not enough at all... there was plenty of sauce I with they had added maybe 6 more pieces of pasta... other than that amazing.

This is a very pretty place to come for lunch. Every detail was beautiful, down to the host's butterfly button-up shirt and matching burnt-orange blazer. The server was very attentive and our food came promptly (although not all at the same time, unfortunately. There was about a 10 minute delay for some people's food.) We ordered non-alcoholic drinks, which were delightful, and everybody enjoyed their food. The dosa was the best dish, in my opinion, but everything was oh-so flavorful. You just can't get these kinds of flavors in many restaurants. I would come back here for a special occasion. Prices were steep for portion sizes, but the flavors were unique and colorful- honestly you don't expect to come to a restaurant like this and pay cheap prices anyway.
Best fucking places I've ever been to. Omg the most amazing food I've ever had. I'm definitely coming back

My friends and I have a Sunday brunch. It's a noisy place with a lot of people having conversations and laughing a. But that's what Sunday brunch about haha. We were aim at the toasted cauliflower but it doesn't have in brunch menu. The toast, the tofu, the pastry, every dish is good. But we would try another time at lunch/dinner time for toasted cauliflower.

Given this place's reputation, it has been on my list for awhile. We made reservations for 5:30 on a Thursday. The hostess stand is a bit tucked away behind the bar, and the hostess was a bit curt with us. I sat at the bar to wait for my companion, and ordered the mezcal cocktail. It was well crafted, and I'd recommend it. My friend arrived and we were seated in a back table. The layout of the tables is odd, and the person in the booth seat ends up getting pinned in by the table. (So don't sit there if you think you'll need to visit the facilities during your meal.) 
Due to the proximity of the tables, it also gets quite loud. At one point a couple next to us was talking at such a volume that it was hard for us to hear ourselves. Our waitress and her assistant for the night were good, if a bit busy with the number of tables they seemed to have. We ordered the artichokes and cauliflower, but were between another dish and the hummus. On their suggestion, we went with the hummus. 

The artichokes came out first. They were well cooked and complemented by the citrus and bitter greens served with them. The portion seemed small, but, we'd expected as much. 
The hummus came at the same time as the cauliflower, which seemed odd and crowded the table. (It also meant when we got to the cauliflower it wasn't as hot as it should have been.) We started eating the hummus and noticed that the veggies were... less than fresh. Like, had been sitting out for a while and dried out/wilted. This kind of dampened the experience considering, you know, it's a veggie based place. Fresh vegetables were brought out when we brought it to the attention of our servers. 

The cauliflower was definitely the highlight of the meal, as many others have said. It was fairly filling and well seasoned- close to a perfect bite with some of the sauce and lemon, pomegranate and pistachio. 

All in all, it just wasn't the amazing experience overall that I wanted for a $70pp veggie spot. The drinks and cauliflower I'd come back for, but I have a feeling there are equally appealing places for vegetarians that don't rival a nice steakhouse for price.

I came here for dinner and tried a multitude of options, and was not disappointed! I left here completely stuffed but with no regrets - Jean Georges knows how to make a vegetarian happy :) Although the prices are a bit outrageous, so sadly I am unable to frequent this spot. Highly recommend for a splurge!
Great food and wonderful service! The food was unique and full of flavor! The beets were incredible and so was the cauliflower! Would go back again.

Had a really enjoyable evening here! On the pricier end but the everything we ordered tasted great. We made a reservation for 2 at 6:30pm on a Tuesday and hardly waited at all. 

We shared 5 appetizers and out of the 5 my favorites were the mushroom dish and roasted carrots with ground seeds (please excuse my description, don't recall the exact names). 

The tomato and mango was a nice surprise! It's not on the menu but was a special dish of the night. The cauliflower was great - half a cauliflower is enough for 2 ppl. And lastly, the beets were really interesting- tart, sweet and savory all in one. 

Would come again to try their breakfast menu!

Well what a diamond.

Walking in a opening.  Had a reservation which is key.  I can't say enough good thing.  Waitress was so nice.  Experience was too notch.  
Had several items which my wife and me split.  

The star of the show Chicken of the woods. D Bomb

You leave the restaurant wanting more and knowing that a place like this is close by is such a great feeling

They are doing great things and if the only complaint which is the price. 

13 - for coconut rice ( super small)

When one of my business vendors tried to gauge my interest in a lunch at abcV, I was all about it!  Despite usually opting for meals with some kind of meat or seafood, I was a fan of the Jean-George empire and willing to give his vegetable-focused spot a chance.  The restaurant's emphasis on clean ingredients also translated into their sleek, white décor.   The layout of the space was very bizarre, though.  There was a large café taking up the left side of the front half of the room, and a lengthy bar taking up the opposite wall.  A long, standing-only kiosk was positioned between these two counters, leaving very little room to maneuver past the patrons to get to the hostess stand, which lay between the casual space and formal dining room in the back.   

Our server was friendly and helpful in our struggle to decide on which and how many items to order from the unique menu.  We decided to start with the Slow Roasted Beets, which were sliced thin and served like a carpaccio.  Their bright pink color resembled that of tuna, teasing our senses into believing were eating anything but vegetables.  The beets were topped with a variety of taste-enhancers, such as tangy Dijon, creamy avocado puree, spicy chili aioli, briny pickles, and herbaceous lovage.  Unlike many raw seafood or meat preparations, this vegetarian style possessed so many flavor profiles that all meshed well together.  Since we had several other dishes coming, we ordered the half portion of the roasted cauliflower, which was also available as an entire head.  The elaborate vegetable was served in the center of a large, round plate and elegantly adorned with pistachios, pomegranate seeds, sliced chili peppers, and what I think were toasted capers.  While the cauliflower was roasted so well that it was extremely easy to cut, this sweet and earthly slaw topping was the highlight of the dish.  I also could not forget to mention the accompanying turmeric-tahini sauce that added an Indian flare.  

While we decided to share these plates, we also wound up ordering some larger courses for ourselves.  My Mushroom Walnut Bolognese was as hearty as a traditional beef-based sauce, but with a nuttier flavor.  It was served over carrot paccheri pasta and sprinkled with celery and mint leaf.  It was definitely a satisfying entrée...unlike my companion's Dosa, which had been listed under "Sandwiches", but was anything but.  The chickpea flour crepe had been rolled into a giant burrito shape, but had nothing stuffed inside of it.  Instead, it was meant to be dipped in a yogurt spread and enjoyed with a boring salad of avocado, lettuce, and sprouts.  It was very bizarre, especially at a cost of $19.  Sure, order it in place of a side of bread, but definitely not as a main course.  If only he would have known...

Aside from this one deception, each dish significantly highlighted its vegetable ingredients, in color, flavor, and presentation.  abcV provided evidence to any carnivore just how scandalously indulgent a plant-based diet could be.

My boyfriend brought me here for my birthday last minute- we squeezed into the 5:30 pm reservation for dinner. I highly suggest making a reservation before coming here ahead of time if possible because this place gets filled FAST. By 6pm half the place was full, and by the time we left it was packed (it was a rainy day too).

Foodwise, I guess you can call this vegan fine dining.. prior to this I've only been to chains like byChloe and Cinnamon Snail, so this is a whole new experience. Its nice to have a legit, hot entree that you can use a fork and knife on for once instead of basic fingerfoods.

Would recommend the cauliflower and green hummus; pass on the szechuan ramen though, it was way too salty to eat without tearing up. Overall, it was a pricy experience but you're paying for the ambience and bougie dishes.

We have been there a couple of times - our favorite so far is the garden salad and the beet root with avocado sauce for brunch and roasted cauliflower and spinach spaghetti  for dinner - do ask for the specials of the day - have tried the Tomato with mango with chili - 
drinks wouldn't recommend the Bloody Mary - black current with tonic was refreshing! 
Dessert chocolate mousse with mango was alright 

Would definitely recommend!!

Dress code - could get with causal

My roommate and I met here after work one day as we had been wanting to try more vegetarian restaurants and had heard some great things about ABCV. We started at the bar before our reservation where I had the matcha colada - it was light and refreshing. Once seated, we ordered the chickpea hummus, wood grilled baby artichokes, and the whole roasted cauliflower. The baby artichokes came out first and I wasn't particularly impressed with the dish. There was maybe 1 whole baby artichoke on the dish and while it was good I would have liked a few more artichoke pieces as a part of the dish. The chickpea hummus came out next (crowding the table because the artichoke plate had come out 1 minuet before that). The hummus itself was delicious and flavorful - but the veggies brought out with it were all wilted which is unacceptable for a restaurant that specializes in fresh veggies. We asked our waiter about this and were brought out fresher veggies but it was still baffling. The whole cauliflower was excellent and filling! The turmeric sauce was a great addition to it and gave it a little something extra. For the money I expected a little bit better from ABCV, but that being said I would absolutely recommend the cauliflower.

Nice service, thoughtful decor, good vibe. 
Ordered hummus which was delicious and had a good texture; wonton and noodles, both dishes were way too salty; Spinach spaghetti interesting and rich in flavor. Healthy selection of drinks.
I would go back only to try their cauliflower and a fresh juice in a hot day.
Had the pasta "bolognese" (vegan) and it was amazing!! My only disappointment is the portion size - felt like an appetizer. Amazing ambiance and lively.

I am a vegetarian and I ate here on my birthday with my boyfriend (who is a proud carnivore) and we loved it! Delicious food, beautiful decor, great service. We LOVED the green hummus and half cauliflower. It ain't cheap, but I will be back!

Ok I had previous reviewed that this was overpriced but I've been thinking about it and that might be unfair to say. So the portions are small but they are obviously very cared for and they do come out perfect. Very specific flavors in each dish I ordered. The waiter let me know that customers will order about 3-4 dishes each so I would say they are kind of like super fancy tapas. The place is very well designed.

One of the best vegan restaurants in NY! Every single menu item looked all good and was hard o decide which one we want. Not a long wait at Thursday night if you come here even ard 6:30pm. We ordered this crazy looking Califlower and was amazingly delicious. However, the propotion was small so we had to order 4 dishes for two people to be able to feel full.

I'm normally a big fan of abcV, or any restaurant that does creative and exciting things with vegetarian food, but the last time I came here I got bad food poisoning. My table and I figured out it came from their juices (FWIW, I ordered the root reboot). When I called the restaurant to let them know in case anyone else called in sick, the manager's response was that it was unlikely to be them because foodborne illnesses take at least 24 hours... um, no? The most common forms of food poisoning can happen within 2-6 hours. If something is really contaminated, it will happen more quickly. I had dinner at 7, and got sick in the middle of the night, so thanks guys. I would normally not expect this at a nice restaurant, but clearly someone didn't wash their hands or the vegetables they juiced were dirty. It happens, especially when you're juicing raw things. But take ownership or offer to make it right when a customer is telling you nicely. This was the first time in my life I've had food poisoning-- I normally have a stomach of steel-- so this was bad. 

Also, while the food is delicious, I'd recommend ordering the more creative (complex) dishes (you know, the ones that take effort...). You can get authentic dosas, with actual fillings, anywhere else in the city, and NOT pay $19 for a plain dosa, a dab of Greek yogurt, and 1/3 of an avocado sliced. The avocado lettuce cups are similarly hilarious. A colleague advised against ordering it, because the last time she ordered it, she said it came with two lettuce leaves filled with a tiny amount of avocado and some seasoning and garnish. That's literally it. Two pieces of and 1/5 of an avocado for $15, folks. If you want to order for a table of four, that's $30 you've just spent on some lettuce leaves and maybe one avocado. The juices are $13 for 8oz, served in a wine glass. Go to the juice generation nearby and get better juice. Don't bother with the desserts. I found them unexciting. The menu here is an odd mashup of cultural appropriation. Go elsewhere for authentic tofu dishes, pita and dip, and dosas... Minus the food poisoning. 

Honestly, if you're one of those people who have money to burn, who care about the "brand name" of where you're eating, and you're looking for Instagrammable furniture, then yes this is your spot. 

Dishes I'd recommend? The toasted cauliflower, spinach spaghetti (though too acidic and lemony last time I was there), pea hummus, and smoky eggplant.

Update: New York City Health Dept reached out and I submitted a report.

Very elegant (found out wasn't fully vegan) cuisine that offers a plethora of options, all plant based. Portions are a little on the small side and very pricey, but it's one of those "special occasion" places. The coconut rice was to DIEEEEE for.

LOVE love love this place! Beautiful, clean aesthetic and atmosphere. Friendly staff. And most importantly, delicious food. The restaurant is from the same group behind ABC kitchen and abc cocina. 

I was hesitant to try at first because I am not a vegan and certainly enjoy eating meat. I was worried the menu would be restrictive and I wouldn't find something I'd enjoy. I'm SO glad I gave it a shot because now it's one of my favorite places. 

Some of my favorite dishes (menu is seasonal so might change):
- hummus 
- sweet potatoes 
- roasted cauliflower (sauce is delicious) 
- coconut sticky rice 
- spinach spaghetti 

Also, the yuzu gin and tonic is a delicious and refreshing cocktail, perfect for summer! 

I have now been 3 times and each meal has been more enjoyable than the last. They also do brunch, which I'm eager to try!

Amazing food, good service, but I will never go back to this restaurant because the acoustics are the worst I have experienced in many many years in a public space/ restaurant.

Last night during the dinner service the restaurant was full but not over-crowed.  Even once the tables thinned out towards the end of our meal the sound in the room was still deafening prevent my husband and I to have a conversation let alone communicate without shouting.  We opted to eat in silence instead of shouting. 

For the price of the dishes and number of customers I don't  understand why this place has not invested in sound panels to absorb the noise.  My ears were literally ringing from the excessive levels of noise in the restaurant.  

Really disappointed.

A great restaurant with even better service! Came here for dinner and ordered the half roasted cauliflower, walnut mushroom spaghetti bolognese, and the green chickpea hummus. Everything was incredible but the green chickpea hummus stole the show. Highly recommend getting it to start. What's more is the service! One of the servers took away our plate of hummus that we weren't quite done with (an honest mistake!) but the bartender Jammie quickly noticed and ordered us a complimentary full new plate! So kind and thoughtful! Be sure to visit Abcv as soon as possible!
Extraordinary vegetarian never tasted so good! Ordered the hummus (a little chunk for my taste) delicious! Then roasted beets great but cauliflower is the STAR!!!

This is one of the slowest restaurant prep lines I have ever seen. It took over 30 min to pick up an order. It wasn't even started. This was not an isolated incident. Another customer also asked to speak to manager to get order filled. The staff at the front are extremely rude when inquiring about an order. I suggested the manager to observe how Made Nice operates. They have 10x the volume with half the wait.

Love this place! Their morning glory muffins are to die for! A solid staple to pick up mon-fri mornings. Nothing on this menu disappoints. My first time here the waiter was super helpful and knew a ton about the menu, made great recommendations. The market carrots and seed and nut butter is a must! Also as seen in the pic attached, best chocolate mousse I've ever had! Definitely make a reservation to be on the safe side if you are looking to dine here.  Tapas style and a little pricey for the food portions but hey it's New York.

The staff here is slow, rude, and it's kind of perplexing they get away with it. Are there really no other high end Vegan places out there? This place is the epicenter of pompous service.  Sorry, but even if the food is ok, the experience of dining out is not just about the food. 

We had a reservation last night that was made well in advance. Showed up and were made to wait for 20+min while the table was literally in front of us, set and ready to go. They corralled our big group near the hostess stand so we had to hover over other diners. Sorry for them, they also probably wanted to enjoy their meals. 

We sat down and it was 30min before anyone even approached us about ordering a drink. I couldn't even get their attention and when we finally did, it wasn't "the right person to talk to". Meanwhile; there's about 3-4 managers standing over us not doing anything and conversing amongst their selves. There's an incredible amount of staff running around this place and I can barely tell what any of them are doing. 

So if you're keeping track, that's 20min at the door, 30min to order a drink, and we're almost about an hour into our dining experience with nothing to show for it but hangry and thirsty people. 

We had a prefix menu and I enjoyed the food. The problem was that the staff clearly didn't plan ahead and just kept bringing us plates and trying to remove the old plates, which we were still eating off of, because there wasn't any room. This is real 101 stuff. Our entire table had the same reaction - "excuse me, but let us enjoy our $20 avocado wrapped in lettuce we just waited an hour for".  My favorite moment had to be when a staff member tried to put another plate almost on top of another plate with a really sassy passive aggressive attitude. Almost as if to say, we were the ones that should be making table space for him. Seriously, perplexing. 

Again, the food was decent. We knew what we were getting into and planned to overpay for well-seasoned vegetables. There are enough reviews on this place that offer opinions about those details. 

At the of the day, we spent $200 per person and our total bill was around $2,500. You'd think for that, maybe someone might get a little service around here. This place brings to light everything that's wrong with the modern dining experience.

While I'm not vegetarian, I usually love going to vegetarian restaurants because the flavors are amazing.  ABCV fell short in my books.
Main thing that soured my taste for this place was the server was telling us about their polenta special and convinced us it was his favorite dish and we had to try it, so we did.  Little did we know, the tiny polenta SIDE DISH was $50 and the server failed to mention this.  It definitely was not worth $50 and if it's double the price of the most expensive dish on your menu, you should definitely mention the price.
So the polenta was a bust.  
We also had the spinach spaghetti, there was a strange, sour taste to it, not into it.
Had some dips, pretty decent but not worth coming back just for some dips.

The A/C was freezing when we're dressed for summer heat. The tables are too close. The spinach spaghetti is too small a serving and way too salty! There was a salt bowl on the table where you can take a pinch with your fingers which just looked like a petri dish to me. They charge $20 for an empty dosa that you have to make a sandwich out of with the yogurt they serve on the side. This place is best gone to in groups so you can all share a bunch of the expensive dishes. The decor is light and airy with beautiful lamps. That contrasted to the dark bathroom with aged mirrors so it was hard to put lipstick on and see if I had anything food between my teeth. I was not a fan of the old faucet and how close it was to the bowl. Everyone who worked there was friendly.

Just had dinner here last weekend and it exceeded my expectations.  My partner and I really enjoyed every dish we ordered, including some that we didn't "compliments of the chef."  Our server Phyllicia S. was awesome. Great upbeat personality, amazing service, and her recommendations were spot on - definitely try the roasted cauliflower, and coconut rice. Kudos to her, and the rest of the staff at ABC-V for making it such a memorable, delicious meal. I will definitely be back!

I'm sorry but what on earth is this restaurant? 

- SO expensive but the food is disgusting over seasoned (saltier than a soft pretzel)
- the roasted cauliflower head was fine (salty of course) but it feels more like a joke than a luxurious dish (it is as if the chef said, how much can we trick new yorkers into paying for a simple head of cauliflower?) 
- Service is bizarre - staff will not leave you ALONE (*takes sip of water* *server comes and refills that one drop of water*)
-aesthetics of the interior are very nice (1 point for the interior decorator)
 
do not waste your time and money here.

I was taken here for my birthday and I absolutely loved it!  The roasted cauliflower accoutrements are so creative and flavorful, the warm mushroom appetizer is amazing and the basmati lemon rice blew me away!  We also tried the pine nut and lemon harissa and the morel mushroom wontons which were just okay (though I must say, the broth for the wontons was so wonderfully complex for being vegan).  I went for the coconut custard for dessert, and they also brought out a matcha creme brulee as a birthday treat - both are solid choices for the perfect end to a creative meal.  Honestly, I still think about that basmati lemon rice - it was even better the next day for breakfast!  If you are vegan or want to impress a vegan someone, ABCV is not to be missed.

What a nice experience! I had a reservation but my Lyft was late and I called and they agreed to hold my place for a bit longer than their 15 mon rule. 
The server helped to make great recommendations for a quick and light lunch! The sparkling rose water lemonade is so refreshing , perfect in summer! The avocado lettuce cups were fun with great complex flavors! But the best part was the coconut custard... it is happiness on a plate! I was tempted to order another one! Highly recommend this lovely place!

We absolutely loved it here. So upscale and classy, a very sophisticated feel at every moment dining here. We like to sit at the bar and watch the action, and the bar was set very nicely for food. There is an additional bar for drinking only. The dining area is beautiful and modern. The service is incredible with such attention to detail. 

We ordered the eggplant hummus and the pine nut spread. My husband liked the hummus and I preferred the pine nut dish. Both were divine. The spreads came with a veggie platter and pita breads. We left very full after two cocktails and two tappas, for $71. 

We would definitely come back! It was a lovely date night.

This is probably the best Vegan Restaurant in NYC as far as the setting & service goes. But when it comes to the food, portion size and pricing; this is not the place to go. It was so bad i didn't even bother to order something to drink here and i probably will never return. My Girlfriend had the pancakes and she said they were good. They give you a very very small amount of food here so please expect to not be full after your food. and the menu is so conflicted as they don't substitute things and there no room for editing things. The waiter was very respectful and tried his best to help me decide on something to eat. i ended up getting some type of tofu item that had pistachios in it and i just was so upset with the food. I'll never return sorry. I wanted to give 1 star but i gave 2 based on the decor being really nice and the service being good.

I am not usually impressed with food. Even pricey places cut corners and usually fall far short of their potential, yet price and a few details aside, ABCV far exceeded expectations, and is probably some of the best vegan food to be had anywhere, yet I wish I ordered less- I felt guilty not being able to finish everything.

The dishes here have strong flavors- and that's good considering the portion size is pretty small. The flavors are probably too strong for some tastes, but the complexity of flavor and texture in each dish is really admirable.

The dishes that didn't stand out (yet were still excellent by usual standards) were the lentils and cauliflower. You simply can't sufficiently season a big chunk of cauliflower, and the sauce was not sufficient to elevate it. The beets and eggplant spread both stood out. The morel wontons as well. Intense flavor. Simple sun-gold tomato salad was excellent. Green hummus was lovely; pitas and crudite were nice. Nut-butter carrots, intense also. A bit too rich for me. 

Drinks were also good- although the sulfite crystals in the bottom of the wine glass were matter-of-factly explained away as a normal thing in biodynamic wine. The wine clearly wasn't biodynamic though, and the server probably should've comped the glass rather than lie about it. At that price point ($17), there shouldn't be hiccups like that.

The chocolate mousse was an impressive dessert, while the pavlova and coconut custard were milder, and matcha creme brulee was a bit too bitter.

Despite so many other (vegan) restaurants to try, I'd return here for a special occasion/to try some of their other dishes.

Excellent place for vegetarian and vegan fare. The service is great and the food is spectacular.  They have a great variety to choose from and the mixture of ingredients makes for a very tasty night out. 

Our favorites were the avocado lettuce cups, grilled cauliflower and green chickpea hummus.

Incredible vegan food, thus incredible food.  Charming, refreshing, whimsical dishes.  This is how you wished you ate every night.  Watching them prepare fare in the open viewing area is akin to watching an artist paint.  Super friendly staff.
But boo on the dishes that include honey.

This place has been in my radar ever since I saw it on Buzzfeed's Worth It. I wanted to try Roasted Cauliflower for myself. So decided to check it out. 

We ordered the Roasted Cauliflower, Mushroom Truffles and some coconut sticky rice. They didn't have the mushroom truffle (one of the dishes from the video) on the menu but the server said we could still order it but failed to mention that its going to cost $55, which was not worth it for such a small dish. 

All the food that we got was delicious. Would I come back here again? Probably just for the roasted cauliflower. Overall was a tasty experience.

Great ambiance.  A little bit loud, extremely busy, and they took 20 minutes to seat us after our reservation, but still a good vibe/energy.  

For 2 people we got, in decreasing order of awesomeness:
1. avocado lettuce wraps were an easy 5 stars.  Light, healthy, flavorful, a little kick, highly recommend
2. The bolognese was also easy 5 stars.  Perfectly cooked pasta with savory sauce and good seasoning.
3. I really like the beats (4 stars) but they're rather pickley so not for everyone.  My friend found them to be meh.
4. Eggplant was OK.  Nice texture especially as a spread for the pita but not super flavorful and a little bland.
5. Mushrooms were a little too overseasoned/over-peppery.  Might just be a personal preference thing but they weren't my favorite.

Overall a good experience though.  Would recommend/return.  Pricey though; 100/person with drinks and you don't get *that* much food.

I often go to vegetarian/ vegan restaurants hoping to find something amazing, but always leave feeling dissatisfied and still quite peckish.  This was absolutely not the case with ABCV!

I came here with a friend last Monday night, and the service was fantastic.  We had made a reservation, but were seated right at our reservation time & were well-attended to throughout the course of our dinner.

We ordered the pine nut & lemon dip, the market carrots with nut butter, the half roasted cauliflower, and the basmati lemon rice with squash and peanuts.  

To start, the pine nut & lemon dip was amazingly refreshing.  A thick, almost yogurt-like dip was accompanied by a wide array of fresh, crunchy vegetables and a full wheat pita.  The nice thing about this dish was that they gave you quite a bit of dip & a large amount of things to dip with.  I always hate going places & quickly running out of things to dip with, but that was not the case here.  I highly recommend this as a starter-- great value!

Next we tried the roasted carrots & the nut/ seed butter.  After reading many rave reviews about these carrots, we just had to try them.  The carrots were perfectly roasted & sat atop a creamy, salty, and somewhat spicy nut coarsely ground nut butter.  The combination of flavors was very unexpected, but extremely delicious.  The only problem with this dish is that you don't get very much at all.  For $16, you get a few pieces of carrot that add up to be maybe one full carrot.  Kind of a bummer.

Next came the roasted cauliflower.  Wow, this plate alone is worth making the trek to this restaurant.  The cauliflower is roasted with a good amount of seasoning and nicely blackened in a few areas.  It's not overly oily or greasy, like roasted vegetables often are.  The plate is garnished with a plethora of items: pistachios, greens, baby onions, sweet peppers.  And it comes with this luxurious turmeric sauce to drizzle over the top.  This dish sets this restaurant apart from other places.  The amount of food you get on the plate and the combination of the roasted vegetables, with the salty, crunchy, & creamy pistachios, and the lemony tahini sauce really make this dish a standout.  I've never had something quite like this & wish I could be eating this again right now.


Lastly, our meal ended with the basmati lemon rice with baby squash, asparagus, jungle peanuts, and herbs.  This was a very filling dish, yet still felt light and fresh.  Again, nothing was oily or overly greasy here.  The rice was perfectly cooked and the squash retained a bit of  bite.  The peanuts provided an interesting contrast in both texture and flavor, and the dish was overall really well balanced.

After four different dishes, my friend and I were fully stuffed and extremely satisfied with the meal.  Everything was cooked just right, and nothing felt like it was greasy or oily, which I've found a lot of veggie-focused restaurants do.  I'd recommend this restaurant to anyone, veggie or non-veggie lover, as it's so easy to find something you'd like off of the expansive menu.  At first the prices seem high, but the quality of food is some of the best I've had in Manhattan so it's definitely worth forking over those few extra bucks to have a delightfully healthy meal that will undoubtedly blow your socks off!

We went here for dinner on a trip to NY. The food is for the most part delicious. For the three of us we ordered 8 dishes or so. The only one we didn't like was the spaghetti (none of us liked it). So many of the others were really delicious.  Carrots with nut butters, the cauliflower everyone talks about, delicious pasta in a "bolognese" sauce, avocado lettuce wraps...and the desserts! The berry soup was superb and the chocolate mousse (which I didn't want to try as it had an herb in it!) was fantastic (did not taste the herb!)

I came here for brunch after working out, and it definitely satisfied my healthy food craving. They have a lot of different options to choose from-including drink options. I got a tonic and an açaí bowl with lettuce cups to share.

Just because of the mere options, I want to go back. Service was also great-friendly but not overbearing. ABC Cocina (which is connected to ABCV) has a better ambience in my opinion; whereas, ABCV is more bright and airy.

I love places that can really showcase delicious vegetarian foods! You are coming here to try the innovative creations and tasty innovations of the vegetarian sort. Although it is a little pricey when you think of the ingredients they put into this (most of the ingredients are not that expensive), everything is beautifully put together and tastes great. 

The ambiance is trendy and not too dark. I enjoyed it, as I don't care for restaurants that are too dark. The service is excellent.
Amazing superb customer service and absolutely delicious food. I was throughly impressed.

This is the last ABC restaurant that I finally got to try. Was really satisfied with ABC Cocina and ABC kitchen, and it's been on my mind to try ABCV, and boy it did not disappoint! This is a great place to go to if you like sharing small plates and having light & refreshing cocktails. I ordered the Galia from the cocktail menu and it arrived in a martini glass, which made me worry that this would be a strong drink. The flavor and alcohol were well balanced and it almost tasted like watermelon juice. For food, my friend and I got the pine nut and lemon, saison sweet potato, and mushroom bolognese. They were all very good and you can't go wrong with any one of them. The bolognese is on the heavier side and I couldn't really tell what kind of mushroom they use. The taste was certainly unique. The sweet potato for some reason made me feel like I was eating fried chicken (not in a bad way). For dessert, we got the matcha creme brûlée, which was also amazing.

This is my favorite restaurant in NYC right now! Jean-Georges Vongerichten knocks it out of the park.  The menu is a quick study in elevating simple, seasonal plant ingredients using culinary techniques from around the world. I love the selection of natural wines and non-alcoholic beverage options, and have never encountered a dish I didn't like. I would truly recommend almost everything on the brunch and dinner menu.  For a party of two, plan to share five or six dishes and leave comfortably full. I have eaten here five or six times, never with a practicing vegetarian or vegan - this place is a win no matter what your ethical or dietary needs may be.
I had the beets, the carrots and the spinach speghetti.  The beets was decent, but the other dishes were ordinary.

I found out about this place from their buzzfeed episode. My gf is a veterinarian and I wanted to give this place a try. This review is for our experience at 3 different times that we came here. First time, it was nice, had our reservations which we made online easily. We sat down and we order the food was great except one of the order I never received got charged and really didn't mind because we were full and it was super busy. The second time same thing online reservations our server we really really nice and the food was great. One thing was my gf got sick and sick where to I need to go to the nearest pharmacy to get her something for it. Third time the charm? We got there a little early so we had to wait. I believe staff were having meeting our fault still had our reservations. We got seated, ordered etc. this time I got very very very sick. I threw up and all the extras. Didn't eat anything for the rest of the day. I don't know if it's something they didn't clean but to have this happen twice and the third time my gf also got sick plus the second time. Just won't be coming back after that.
Came for brunch and left impressed! Almond pancakes and avocado toast were our favorite dishes. Great coffee and service.

FOOD: Nearly perfect. Cauliflower: A very special appetizer. Loved the spices, turmeric sauce and the presentation. Super tasty and unique. Hummus: Not special at all (despite the waiter's recommendation that it's AH-mazing. It's okay. But I would've rather saved the space (and money) for something unique. Spinach spaghetti with veggies: Awesome. Super tasty and unique. Corn Won Tons: Super delicious and unique. Chocolate mousse with crushed peanuts, cherries and sauce: Absolute perfection. 

AMBIANCE: Perfect. If you love ABC you will love the decor and all the special details of the vases, plates, etc. It's what you'd expect from ABC: Awesome.

SERVICE: No. I felt like we had too many people "on us" the whole time. Like servers just hovering behind my friend, waiting to clear plates (even when we were nowhere near finished). It was the kind of annoying that you can only imagine that the managers would make them behave like that. With this kind of special food (taste and expensive) I want to savor it. Not rush through. There were two of us and we ordered two apps, two dinners and shared a dessert. They had us in and out in two hours--they were grabbing plates just as we were barely finished, or not even--and plunking down the next course. I didn't realize how annoying all this was until they put down a $15 dessert (a heaping, big spoon's worth of chocolate mouse) with the check AT THE SAME TIME. WTF? I don't know why I found this to be totally unacceptable. My friend was treating me for a bday dinner, and had I not thought he would've been mortified, I'd have told them to take the check back until we asked for it. No time to linger through the dessert or sit for ten minutes to digest. BTW I should mention that our reservation was at 6pm on a Monday. It was crowded at the end but sorry guys, it's not my fault if you over booked the tables. I felt the service was pretentious, and too involved in my meal. In a way it was very New York  so I guess I shouldn't be surprised. But with such unique and carefully designed food, I believe the service should balance things out with more approachable, friendliness because otherwise it all just feels pretentious rather than special and artful.

Not sure I'd go back. You can get great, unique food at Matthew Kenney's restuarant's around town--but without the pretentious service.

As a vegetarian, I really, really wanted to like this place...but alas, it didn't live up to the hype. I was pretty excited to finally go to a place where I could order from the whole menu, without skipping parts, or asking for substitutions or looking for other creative means to find something to eat. Jean Georges being the best in the business, I thought this was going to be vegetarian food heaven. But it just stopped short of hitting the mark from the beginning. Our server, who was friendly as they can be - so this is nothing as to the wait staff, suggested that my three friends and I order at least 12 dishes from the menu. Given that the menu only had some 20 items on it, that meant to feed four females, it would take more than 50 % of the menu. We skipped that suggestion and decided to opt for 6 plates. The plates were definitely on the smaller side, but I think 12 would have been way too much, between 6- 8 for a party of four I think is plenty. 

The first dish to come out for us was the avocado lettuce wraps. It was good, but something so basic that PF Changs has them on their menu - I was hoping something more sophisticated when it came to this upscale restaurant. Next we had the beet dish, which if you are not prepared for smushed up beets of different colors, will definitely catch you by surprise. The dish was too acidic and lacked the beet taste that was supposed to be part of the dish bearing that name. We also had the green pea hummus. Our waiter told us that it was named the best hummus in New York by the Times - it was good, but best? I don't know about that...
Then we had the cauliflower. I have had great cauliflower at other places, and this was just meh. It was not crispy as one would hope and the dressing was a little too heavy handed with the turmeric. 
One of the dishes that we all loved was the coconut rice, which was delicious and the hit of the night.

We tried many different dishes, and came out thinking - it was good, but given the sizes of the plates, the prices of each dish, and the lack of anything that stood out as stellar - we didn't think we would come here again unless something changed. This is a shame given that his ABC cocina, which is not vegetarian, is amazing - maybe I will have to stick to to going to places where I can only order from parts of the menu - it seems it would have served me better in this case to go to Jean Georges other restaurants.

Some good dishes, some pretty average; quite expensive for what you get.
Ordered a $7 latte and they burned the milk, asked them to remake it and they gave me a cappuccino instead.
Service was pretty mediocre. They brought out the first half of our meal, but took 45 minutes to bring out the second half so our appetite was pretty much gone.

This is definitely not just for vegetarians!  The cuisine is flavorful, crafted with conviction, and quite innovative, both in presentation and taste.  The space itself is light - a la ABC Kitchen - and upbeat, and the staff are wonderful - helpful and friendly.  Overall, definitely worth a try and great for a group meal with friends.  I highly recommend getting a wider spread and sharing so that you get to try more of the dishes.

Some highlights:
1. Mushroom walnut bolognese: Creamy and savory tomato ragu with a nice nutty kick from the walnuts and a hint of mint.  The pasta was perfectly tender.  It's not a bolognese per se but still delicious and a great comfort dish.
2.  Roasted cauliflower: This was my fav dish with a perfectly roasted head of cauliflower that is slightly charred and simultaneously crispy and tender, with a creamy and spicy tumeric tahini sauce and roasted pistachios.  I am a meat lover but this was good enough to make to want to turn vegetarian if I could eat this everyday.  
3.  Crispy sweet potatoes: Creamy, sweet, tart (slightly), savory, and crispy!  The batter is very light and crispy and the honey, sesame, and umeboshi blend into a flavor journey from sweet to savory to tangy.  I was very pleasantly surprised and really enjoyed this!
4.  Coconut sticky rice: This is more of a sweet dish vs savory side.  The coconut flavor is not very strong but subtle and the rice is sweetened with coconut sugar.  It's good but i wouldn't really use Thai coconut rice as a basis for comparison as this wasn't quite that "sticky."
5.  Matcha creme brulee: This was great - creamy with a hint of matcha and not overly sweet.  It's decadent but still pretty light.

I was really excited to come to this place bc I was hoping it'd be different since it's a Jean-Georges establishment.  Boy was I wrong.  This place is so pretentious and overpriced, I would never think of coming back.  

We first arrived and asked for a table for two.  We were told there were two seats by the window where there was a table that was literally 12" wide.  You could barely put a plate on it, so we asked to be seated at the bar where there were two empty chairs but no plate settings.  We were told we could sit there as soon as they reset the settings which we were cool with.  It took them a good 15 mins to set the table.  The hostesses were arrogant and didn't care to even ask the settings to be set.  

We sat down and had ordered food.  We ordered the lettuce cups ($18), protein shake ($13), pancakes ($18), pastry basket ($17), another smoothie ($13), and the poached egg with wild mushrooms ($17).  The total bill came out to over $100 for a simple brunch.   The lettuce cups were excellent, but the rest was disappointing:  either too sweet or just plain wrong.  For that kind of pricing, I would go somewhere else.  

What really got me was the service was horrendous.   We were brought dishes that we didn't order twice and my wife's poached egg was improperly entered into their system and didn't come out until 45 mins after the rest of our food.  

This place is the type of place you see in sex and the city.  The food is very hit and miss, mostly misses from my experience.  I'd avoid it at all cost.  I could go to a Michelin star restaurant for brunch for that price.

The service was excellent. I really appreciated the people who work there. ABC V is vegetarian only. The cauliflower was very good. So is the mushrooms with peppers. The rice definitely needed an ad on. Drinks Were marginal. Had to go to red wine. Their Bordeaux was very good.
Incredible vegan spot. The highlight was the spinach spaghetti. Pricey place with small portions, but worth it.

Heaven for fellow vegetarians! Giving 4 instead of 5 stars because we had to wait 45 minutes for our table despite having a reservation. The quality of food, drinks, and a cheerful and airy atmosphere made for up the lack of seating organization on their part. Breakdown of our order: 

- lettuce cups: worth reordering and were a fresh burst of flavor. 
- roasted beets: a bit too "pickle" or vinegar flavored. 
- basmati lemon rice: the BEST thing we ordered (and I'm not a huge rice enthusiast). 
- sambal dosa: a must since it is their speciality, however, it was a bit too salty for my taste buds. 
- matcha creme brûlée: not too sweet and strong on the matcha flavor.

The serving-style of the dishes and utensils seem resistant to sharing, thus leading to little table messes (see my photo). Otherwise, ABCV is perfect. Creative, cruelty-free food, enchanting atmosphere, expert service. You can't go wrong with the menu, and take care not to overlook downplayed descriptions like "market carrots," which are divine. Oh, and they do have seasonal outdoor seating, despite what the Yelp description says.

I dined with two friends on Tuesday night.  I found the restaurant to be a major disappointment and certainly is not in-line with the quality at other Jean-George restaurants.  I found the restaurant to be expensive for what was offered.  The restaurant has many good options for vegetarians.  We ordered the smoked eggplant which was oversalted as was the focaccia.  Some other items including the cauliflower and the dumplings were overcooked.  I would definitely not return.

Mark is one of the best bartenders I've ever had, very nice, enjoyable conversations, down to earth, the food is great and the atmosphere is enjoyable.  I'm no vegan or vegetarian but I am very happy I got to experience this place and it's delicious food!

BIG fan of this place.  

There are so many good things to say about ABCV!  I've been there twice, and each time was as good as the last.  

First: I love their concept of vegetables being the star of the meal.  I've taken vegetarian and non-vegetarians to this place, and my non-vegetarian friends admit that they would eat more vegetables if they were always made this well.  

Second: I love that everything is done family-style.  I'm a huge fan of family-style meals.  I find that they make the setting more intimate and you can try so many different kinds of food! 

The one thing I will say is that if it's busy, service may be a bit slow.  We didn't get our drinks until 1/3 into the meal.  Not a big deal, but something to keep in mind.  

Recommendations: most of the dishes seem to be seasonal (which I love, guarantees fresh vegetables) and there are, of course, a few staples.  Everything here is delicious, but I LOVE their smoked eggplant dip and you must get the cauliflower.  The last time I was there I got a bowl of their fresh grape tomatoes and figs--so good I almost ate the whole bowl by myself.  The wantons are a nice addition of spicy, and the spinach noodles are delicious.  

I don't know how they do it, but ABCV makes vegetables absolutely delectable!

So overpriced but so good at the same time.

This is one of those places where you order a ton of small plates because you want to try everything (with a food buddy, of course). Then after you thoroughly enjoy the amazing meal, you glance at the check and quickly add tip and your signature before you rip up the customer copy and destroy all evidence of anything that would make you think negatively of this restaurant and the delicious food you just had. 

I went for brunch and shared the smoky fingerling potatoes (nice & crispy with a delicious aioli), the chop salad (not your ordinary chop salad - sticky rice, avocado and herbs), the sungold tomatoes (peach is added to the mix which makes it refreshing), and vegan einkorn pancakes. I also had the Thai Julius cocktail which was comprised of lemongrass infused tequila, coconut cream, basil, and other things I don't remember. It sounds strange, but it wasn't. It tasted like how you would imagine an alcoholic Thai iced tea without the half and half (kind of). The vegan pancakes were the only item I was 'meh' about. The toppings were good, but the actual pancake wasn't very flavorful at all.

I'm not a vegetarian, but I would totally go vegetarian if I were able to replicate the food they serve at ABCV in my own kitchen at home.

Great food - innovative menu and lots of options. Making reservation for Sunday brunch was easy. Very nice decor and customer service. Vegan pastry basket included delicious chocolate croissant. I'd recommend this place, even if just in town for the weekend.

Came in on a Sunday morning for brunch. We made the reservation around 11 and they had a 1 and 1:30 available.  My friend is vegetarian, so this was a great option for us! 

We got there at 1:30 and requested to sit outside since the weather was great. We debated sitting inside just because of how cute the decor was. 

I got the mushrooms with the farm poached egg, and the tofu.

The mushrooms were good, the egg was slightly over cooked so I didn't really get the effect of the yolk turning into a sauce unfortunately.  Nothing exciting but a solid dish.

The tofu had a lot of textures and flavors that I really liked! All sorts of veggies, corn etc. it was spicy too! I would recommend this.

Note to anyone that wants to sit outside; the bees were everywhere. Some people had to move inside to deal with it. We also got a bowl to try to trap a few. We luckily made it out without any stings! 

Cute place. Decent food. I would come back to try more items on the menu!

Came here on a Saturday night for dinner and drinks. The only good thing about this restaurant was its ambiance. Food quantity was very less and taste could have been much better. For such mediocre food, they charge you with sky-high rates. I am a foodie and do not mind the cost if it satisfies my taste buds. They have DOSA on the menu and being an Indian, I know how authentic dosa is prepared. Avocado dosa was on their menu and it sounded interesting and something new. But the way they prepare it is not at all authentic and something which makes you wonder that is this non-authentic food worth paying for? They provide avocado filling(mix) on the side, not acceptable! And it is not just about dosa, I don't understand why do theyhave to charge $20 or more with quantity which I could finish in a minute, huh ! I feel there are many other better restaurants which charge you the appropriate amount, and not just rip you off, for an average food taste. Never going to visit this place again !
