Great food and vibes. Love the cauliflower, amazing soups, and appetizers. Make sure to make a res ahead of time because they get very busy. Decor is beautiful and clean. Will definitely be back

I've been to a few Jean-Georges restaurants and have generally been pretty happy, so I was game for a vegetarian version.  I'd seen a few pictures, read the menu, and heard a little about ABCv, but I didn't know quite what to expect.  In general, I was pretty happy with the overall experience, but I don't know that it was my favorite of the ABC family of restaurants.

I'll start by saying that immediately when we walked into the restaurant, we weren't greeted and we had to wait for what looked like one of the servers to finish flirting with the hostess and finally take our names--not a great start.  We were seated in a back corner of the relatively open dining room with whitewashed walls and white tables.  The service, aside from the aforementioned annoyance at the beginning of the meal, was fine.  Servers were friendly and accommodating, but in general, things were pretty average.

While the service was mediocre and honestly would have lead to a two star review, the food was actually better than expected.  I was most pleased with the effort to reinvent new items and attempt new flavors.  We ordered the chicken of the woods mushroom, which were essentially mushrooms that were friend in attempts to resemble and taste like fried chicken--I wasn't mad at it.  We also ordered the corn wonton, which was essentially a dumpling with corn inside, and the grilled cauliflower, which I thought was a little soggy and nowhere near as good as Domenica's in NoLa.  We also had the mushroom bolognaise, which was probably our favorite of the night. 

I'll echo what others have said that it might be a little overpriced for the actual product, but overall we were generally pleased.  It feels a little casual to ask for such high prices and might be better for a brunch or lunch, but overall, I'd return or recommend it, especially to vegetarian and the vegetarian-friendly.

You can't go wrong with whatever you order. The menu is designed for dishes to be shared. The flavors are so distinct and the dishes well executed. The service is attentive and the staff is super friendly. Great ambiance and nice space. The almond pancakes at brunch were our favorite dish to share, but again, you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. Other favorites were the sweet potato brunch bowl, market vegetable chop salad, green chickpea hummus.

As a vegetarian, always happy to have a spot catering to us in town. My short review is: this is a better daytime place than a nighttime place (in terms of the food). 

The food makes for a great spring brunch, but disappoints in terms of an autumn dinner (perhaps the opposite of what I'd say of ABC Kitchen, actually!). That said, it's a beautiful space and a creative, well-executed menu. Recommended.

For the most part, I enjoyed my experience at AbcV. However, when I made my reservation for Sunday, I wasn't aware that the menu was different than the everyday menu. I was a bit underwhelmed by the menu options. I wish I had known that the menu was different on Sundays because I left feeling like I didn't get the full AbcV experience. I would have loved to try all those vegetable sides and main dishes that were on the regular menu. However, overall, I enjoyed my experience here. I stepped out of my comfort zone and tried the "Vegan Einkorn Pancakes with coconut cream, fresh fruit and grape compote." I don't even know what Einkorn is but I know it was good. The aesthetics of the restaurant itself were beautiful and the drinks were great. A bit pricey for a vegetarian place, but that is expected when dining at any Jean Georges restaurant.

I'm sure it's the lighting. The lighting causes your food pics to look just awful soooooooo for once in our technology infested lives we have to just sit back and enjoy the food. Not the imagery. Not your friends comments about the food. But the food. 
This review won't be a surprise. If anyone gave this place less than 5 starts then they were born without taste buds (no offense to those born without taste buds). 
Every. Single. Dish. We ate. Was delicious. The sautéed mushroom medley special was so gooooood. My friend and I shared everything and I left so freakin full. 
Yeah yeah yeah get the cauliflower. It's a must of course.  
I can always judge the quality of a vegan spot based on whether I can replicate the dish at home. I'm an excellent cook so when I tell you that I would have a hard time replicating what I had tonight, please consider that a compliment. 
Superb!!!!
Loved the "vibrations" (tonics) we tried here. Attached is a picture of the very famous roasted cauliflower. It tastes as good as it looks

Excellent!!! Im not vegan but this was super delicious. Service was terrific, and the food was so good. Each dish was so different but tasty. The chicken in the woods really tasted like chicken. The food and most drinks are organic and I will definitely head back here again for dinner.
I had a poached egg and gluten-free avocado toast and a green juice. Everything was delicious. My friend had a drink with turmeric. Also amazing. Will definitely come back!

I'm a girl who loves my fried chicken, ribs and meat in general.  So when I heard of ABC launching a vegan spot, I wasn't sure what to expect.  But after experiencing a great meal here...I'm all about dem veggies.

Our waiter was friendly and knowledgeable about the menu.  For two, he recommended  ordering 4-6 plates.  We ordered the following dishes (in order of my favorite to least favorite)

- Roasted cauliflower.  This was the highlight dish of the evening.  The dish was punched with flavor and texture.  I loved the tumeric-tahini sauce that came on the side.

- Avocado lettuce cups.  A very refreshing appetizer that comes with two lettuce cups.  So much flavor with the cumin paired with pepita seeds

- Fried chicken of the woods.  Interesting dish that mimicked fried chicken but was made out of mushroom.  I really enjoyed the first bite along with the chili honey sauce because of the novelty.  However, after having several more bites, I felt the dish was just ok.

- Fresh spinach spaghetti.  The spaghetti had a bitter aftertaste. I loved the crunchy saffron crumbs that was mixed in with the cheese which added a lot of delicious flavor and texture to the dish.

- Beluga Lentils.  There was nothing special about the lentils and it was very pricey for the amount of food that was served.

Overall, it was a tasty experience, but a pretty penny for just veggies.  I would recommend giving ABCV a try, as it is not only for vegans, but for those who seek new, creative foods.

Did dinner for two. Slick white space makes the place look more open than it is. Two bars at the front seemed like where the action was at, and regret not being seated there as we dragged into a cavernous corner of the dining area behind a pillar. Complaints end there. Ordered 5 plates to share and they were all excellent - each showing off the restaurant's top notch variety in the face of not utilizing meat (and for a significant portion of their menu, animal products at all). 

Crisp greens - fresh on fresh. Sliced mushrooms and apples accented the greens expertly. Perfect start.

Honey squash with sourdough - a dip that leaned on its combo of flavors and not oil. Only fault was there wasn't enough bread.

Basmati rice - the simplest dish we got. Ended up being the perfect complement to all our other dishes.

Bucatini - thick noodle. Fresh lemon taste. Nice amount of greens to make it a ten.

Shiitake mushroom - was very good but the onions they put as almost an afterthought dish accent were the best thing here. Have not had a better onion.

Dinner was pricey but did not disappoint. Great spot for special occasion - has that extra upscale nyc vibe too for the out of town crowd.

Get. The. Cauliflower.
The whole one. 

Make a reservation.
Dress nicely. 
Be impressed.

Amazing ! 

I am not vegetarian but this restaurant is impressive. 
The cauliflower is amazing, as is the dosa. The ambience is nice, and it is nice to eat outside on a nice day too. Reservations are hard to come by but I think it is possible to walk in, there are a lot of bar tables.

ABCV is incredible!! As a plant-based lady, I am still interested in exploring vegan fine dining! ABCV truly delivers with chic décor, excellent customer service, and mouthwatering dishes. I ordered a Half-Cauliflower, not exactly sure what to expect. The flavors in the sauce and the spices that the cauliflower was cooked in were out of this world! I think everyone would eat more veggies if they tasted ones these delicious! 

My boyfriend ordered Soba Noodles which were so hearty and the mushroom broth gave us both ideas for future plant-based cooking adventures! We also ordered the pea hummus with half pita bread and half veggies as dippers. I will dream of the pea hummus! I wish wish wish I could recreate it! 

I let the staff know that it was almost my bf's birthday and they brought us a green tea crème brûlée (also vegan of course) with chocolate writing that spelled "Happy Birthday" and a little candle on the plate. Just like all the food from the evening, this dessert was amazing as well. This place is a dream come true and I could keep singing its praises - go see for yourself!

I went here with my family because of all the press recommendations. Buzzfeed guys on Worth It seemed impressed. Normally I don't leave reviews. I hardly have time. I certainly don't do negative reviews but this might save someone from making the same mistake. I can only conclude that the reports are truly overrated. I was utterly underwhelmed. That is the nicest way I can put that.

The first time we came, we arrived at 4:30pm, unaware that it was that early because we were out enjoying the city. The host, with a slight air of superiority remarked that we could return in an hour. Since it was our children's first visit to NYC, that didn't seem too problematic. We said we would return when they were opened for dinner. We left to peruse the area shops for a good solid hour before returning to the restaurant, promptly at 5:30pm. At which point another host remarked that she could seat us at 6:45pm at the soonest because we did not have reservations. How inconvenient that the first host left that detail out, knowing that we would return. The dining room was empty save for two customers. I explained that I would have gladly made the reservations when I showed up an hour ago, but it was not specified as necessary. I turned to my husband and declared we would eat anywhere else, but we would not wait another minute to be seated in a dining room that was just about empty. 

Ok, I get it. It is NYC. The big apple. You need to keep up the appearance of demand and exclusivity. Fine. 

I decided to give it another chance. I made reservations two days ahead of time. We showed up. Again, the dining room was still virtually empty at 5:30pm. We were made to wait a few minutes before seating us. I had to make the reservations for a party of six instead of five, which is what our family size is. The website was rigged that way. I figured, if you have room for 6, you should invariably have room for 5. Maybe this was the reason for the wait. It takes a while to remove a place setting, perhaps. Our waiter told us that for a party of our size, typically 10 dishes would suffice to feed us as the dishes are small and are meant to be shared. With the average dish costing $20, I had my doubts. If it was really good, we would happily order more later. We ordered 5 dishes. Our waiter looked surprised and encouraged us to order another rice dish that would better pair with the tofu dish we had ordered. I decided to hold off on doing that. I actually saw him roll his eyes. I politely ignored the ill manners. 

The food was nothing special. The cauliflower was seasoned with the enthusiasm of a young chef who did not understand restraint. The tofu dish would be passable for anyone who is used to tv dinners, but nothing delightful about it, especially if one is accustomed to Asian fare. The potatoes were something of a joke with a few potato chips on top. The lemon rice dish again tasted of someone who was trying too hard. The hummus was nice, but I expect hummus at a restaurant to be good. We considered the culinary experience to be an utter waste of time and money. 

Please, send the chef to Thomas Keller to learn to cook and season properly. This food at abcV is only good for drunk tastebuds that are too inebriated to differentiate between underwhelming and worthwhile. 

Please teach your wait staff to never be caught rolling their eyes at the customers. Please tell the tall snobby host that his arrogance is ingratiating for those of us who understand the worth of a human being and the richness of extending kindness and consideration to all people, even those who roll their eyes and look down their noses at us. 

This was the worst dining experience I have ever had the misfortune to endure. .

I had been long looking forward to coming here, and finally had the chance to last night with a friend. The food was phenomenal, the service was not. We ordered drinks shortly after being seated and didn't receive them until halfway through our meal - had to ask twice as our server did not come by to notify us the drinks would be awhile. When we did ask, we were told the bar was "backed up" - what? How can a popular, trendy restaurant not know how to manage their bar flow on a Tuesday evening. No apology was made either. Also, my friend and I each ordered an appetizer and a rice dish. Her app (the half cauliflower) came out almost immediately - they must just constantly make them, but I had to sit there and wait an additional 10 minutes for mine (the potatoes). Within minutes of my app being served, my rice dish followed - but hers didn't. So out of whack to be served like this. Our waitress was hard to come by the whole time, and then shows up with the bill before asking if we wanted anything else.

This is literally my favorite restaurant in the world. I came here not expecting much just based a recommendation, but now I'm rethinking how good vegan and vegetarian food can be.

If all food tasted this good I'd be set for life. If you're a carnivore and dislike veggies you might wanna try coming here to give you a new perspective. 

What was so good? Everything. I loved all of the dishes in terms of the flavors, freshness of ingredients, plating, and just overall creativity. Every dish was a crazy adventure with punches of flavors from all around the world. 

Hands down my favorite dishes were the beet carpaccio and the cauliflower. There was just the right amount of tanginess and creaminess and literally wanted to lick the plates. The flavors were so well balanced but they were unique and played great together. 

Not all the dishes are vegan (some use egg and milk) but many can be made vegan. If you are looking for a knock your socks off experience that is so delicious and innovative, come here.

The ambiance is very cozy and warm, the tables are small and it's a tight fit but it was a great experience with very helpful servers. The restaurant is pretty dim so it was hard to read the menu, but that was the only minor issue. The whole experience was perfect even though we strolled in soaking wet and on a whim.

I've eaten here a number of times, more brunches than dinners, but both are excellent. Everything here is so good. Haven't had 1 thing that disappoints. For brunch I love the avocado lettuce wraps, the dosa, and the almond pancakes are amazing. Everything is so delicious. One of my faves at dinner is the cauliflower. Service here has been consistently good - I recommend eating at the bar at least once. We had a nice experience here with the bartender who steered us in all the right directions on our order. The decor is bright and airy. 

Make a reservation in advance, it does get very busy. Speaking of which, I'm about to go make my next reservation because just thinking about all the yummy food here makes me want to go back again!

One tip - at brunch the last seating is near 3, but the kitchen also closes at 3, so if you are seated near closing you will be asked to put your full order in and not be able to add additional items. Since it is tapas style, I feel they should close the kitchen at least a half hour later or make their last seating half hour earlier to accommodate additional items. So, if you arrive near 3, be prepared to know what you want. 

Food tips: brunch - Dosa, Almond Pancakes, Avocado Lettuce Wraps. Dinner - Cauliflower

What a really neat place that serves plant based, non gmo, sustainable, artisanal and organic dishes. 

Three of us ordered family style so we can try multiple dishes: Avocado lettuce cups, Half roasted cauliflower, and Mushroom walnut bolognese. Happy to say they were all incredibly flavorful and tasty!

The Mezcal Maracuya was too smoky of a drink for me but I really liked the Espanya.
Everything is super fresh,... it was amazing!every course was different with extraordinary tastes! Love the matcha creme brûlée; EXCELLENT SERVICE.

ABC Vegan is a quaint spot nestled on the East side of New York, not far from major transportation. We were running late for our reservations and grateful to still be accommodated once we arrived at the restaurant. The tables are set up close to each other so you're seated with people you don't know - this would be questionable for those looking to have intimate conversation with their party however, everyone appears to be very much indulged in their own conversations so it doesn't seem to take away the privacy factor. 

I ordered the soba noodle, aromatic dashi, oyster mushrooms, sea lettuce and broccoli. The meal was tasty but the portion size was so small. It was literally just enough to dab our tastebuds yet we were still hungry.  We voiced our disappointment in the size of the small meal so alas, they brought us bread to appease us. The bread was delicious- crispy on the outside and soft sourdough in the middle. The bread included olive oil we could dip and eat. Frustrating to receive the bread after the meal was done. The waiter was polite and a bit humorous. The rest of the staff was kind and professional.  
If it weren't for the somewhat exorbitant prices in comparison to the meal portion size, I would probably give it 4 stars.

I am a new fan; this place is amazing even for those who are not vegetarian/vegan. I came here with a friend who is not vegetarian and he enjoyed the food very much. Dinner menu. 

AMBIANCE

Very simple, white, clean decor that gives it a classy feel but not over the top. 

SERVICE

The staff is pretty friendly and makes good recommendation. The only thing I didnt like is that they were constantly coming around to grab plates while we were conversing when we were at the bar and there was no reason to rush the plates off. However, maybe they try to clean them immediately or keep clear space so no biggie. 

FOOD

DELICIOUS. They have amazing creations and they all tasted so good. They recommend you share 4-6 plates between two people and they were right; it allows you to try a good portion of the menu while getting full. We ordered the mushroom bolognese, roasted cauliflower, coconut rice [those three were my fav], my friend had a soup which was amazing, some squash rings...i am forgetting something but either way- SO GOOD. 

I ordered the matcha creme brûlée and did not like it. the consistency was off to me and the matcha was overwhelming- its my favorite dessert of all time so I just didnt like this variation.

Do NOT let the vegetarian/vegan menu deter you - it's just damn delicious food!  Been there for dinner and breakfast and both times I was blown away!  All the items are much more than as described, the flavors, textures, taste all meld to fantastic dishes!

The avocado lettuce wraps are full of fresh and vibrant flavors. Roasted cauliflower is to die for and carrots with nut butter are on a def level!  Lentils were just ok, mushroom bolognese was good.  I Didn't like preserved lemon in one of the pasta dishes. We got 4-5 desserts, all were amazing and I remember really liking the coconut custard!

For breakfast - fitness and protein smoothie was so good it tasted like it was bad/unhealthy.  The vanilla chia bowl is delicious - be sure to pair each bite with date to add necessary sweetness, Brazil nuts are def a nice touch!  Vegan einkorn pancakes don't even need syrup bc the coconut cream makes the whole thing pop!

Don't miss out on any chance to eat here!

I've been to ABC Kitchen, ABC Cocina, and ABCV, and I thought ABCV was unfortunately the least tasty of the 3. All 3 restaurants are beautiful, but ABCV's food didn't have as much complexity/flavor as the other two. The famous half cauliflower tasted somewhat plain to me. The avocado wraps and dessert were good though! I'd go back to the other two, but not sure about ABCV

Decor is super pretty and modern but still warm. Crowd was quiet and diverse. 

Standout dishes included: sticky coconut rice -- think of the inside of an almond joy in carb form, crispy cauliflower (half is plenty) is presented beautifully and is light but filling (loved the taste of pomegranates here). Also loved the smoky eggplant appetizer (the mint on here is soooo good)

Only thing I didn't love was the mushroom Bolognese, only because the pasta was a lot harder than I expected but all in all, a great vegan spot. Would definitely want to come back to try other dishes.

Ambience 
Beautiful restaurant with well lit chandeliers and you walk via one of their bars and a mini kitchen
Once you sit you get to see the other main kitchen 
Service
This was exceptional ; our waiter was courteous, helpful and guided us to get the best dishes 
Food 
Others
The bathroom is very old school , no separate taps for hot and cold water
My only disappointment was their coffee for a $7 a cup I wished it was better
Great restaurant wonderful service
We have to come back for dinner

Food is absolutely delicious and original.  Quite expensive per dish but we felt still very worth it :) Waitstaff were helpful and fairly friendly but unfortunately hostesses were extremely snooty and unfriendly.

I had been excited to try this place ever since I heard the indomitable Jean Georges was opening an all-vegetarian place. drinks were really tasty and a great way to start the meal. One thing I really liked about this place was that it was very vegetable-forward, but not in the traditional way. I've been to plenty of Michelin star restaurants and their vegetarian option almost always consists of a ton of root vegetables like turnips or parsnips cooked in various forms- which is FINE, but this was nice because it had some other veggies.
Starters- we had the avocado lettuce cups and the pine nut harissa. Great start to the meal. the pine nut harissa wasn't quite a hummus and wasn't a pesto but was delicious regardless. We then had the dosa, which was probably better than most dosas I've had at authentic south Indian places. I think it's the combination of rice flour and gram flour that helps it become thic(c)ker while remaining crisp. We followed this with a mushroom/walnut "bolognese" which was probably better than many meat versions I've had. MY wife didn't enjoy the pasta but I really loved it. For dessert we had a matcha creme brulee, that didn't really have a crispy top but was good regardless. Definitely recommend this place!

V for veggies! Upon walking into ABCV, I was a little overwhelmed by the beautiful yet simple decor and how they used the space so aesthetically. We were seated promptly with our reservations and service overall was very pleasant and quick. The only downside was that the restaurant was very loud, and I honestly heard almost none of the specials essay our waiter recited for us.

The food was all spectacular. I loved that it was all vegetarian, as I've been trying to eat healthier, but for those of you who find that appalling there are pasta dishes and imitation meat dishes as well.

My personal favorites:

Cauliflower: we got the whole cauliflower, which seemed to be glazed with a curry and then baked. The sauce was savory and light, and was a perfect addition to the bite that cauliflower gave.

Carrot with legumes: the carrots were soft and covered with a sweetish lagume. Felt very healthy.

Bolognese: I believe the Bolognese was made with mushrooms. This felt pretty similar to meat, and the sauce was very savory and had a texture similar to ground beef.

Shitake mushrooms: the mushrooms were plump and covered in a sweet, mayo-like sauce. My favorite course of the night!

one of my favorite restaurants in the city! you can always count on good food and amazing service here. The brunch is insaneeee especially the vegan eikorn pancakes... the best pancakes I've ever had. Dinner is delicious too if you are into small plates to share-it's all about the flavors and quality of the food here. You will not be disappointed by the chef's creativity and ability to make an abundance of diverse flavors with plants here!

Wow.  As a vegan of 5+ yrs and a vegetarian before that who has been to many different restaurants and had almost every type of vegan food possible.... I cannot fathom how this restaurant has so many stars and positive reviews.  Let me just state of the bat that I am not someone who cares about the price of food.  That being said I do have a problem when the price does not add up to what you actually get.  Most of these dishes are worth half of what they charge.   I have never had a broth so watery and flavorless as the soba noodle dish  and don't even get me started on the $17 bowl of "wok fried shoots". Which that night was Chinese spinach made up of all stems that you couldn't even cut or chew swimming around in a salty watery mess.
Then there is the mess of a plate which boasts itself as an artichoke dish... I won't even waste my time describing that.

Anyway, the waiter had just as much flavor as the broth and should probably find a new place to be playing his brooding New Yorker act.  

Though the rest of the group was very friendly and attentive.  

Mediocre decor ..... mediocre food.  Sad.  But notice it does have Trendy in its description   And we all know how trendy things fare in this city especially.

We had a reservation for 7:30pm for a party of 3 on a Thursday night. We arrived 5min early and were told they would come get us when the table was ready. After waiting for 20min without hearing, I asked the hostess if she knew when we could expect to be seated. She explained that they were just waiting for the table to leave and it should be soon. The manager, Nathan, came over 5min later and explained the table had paid their check and they were just waiting for them to get up. He apologized and handed me his card. We were finally seated a little after 8pm.

We were understandably hungry and ordered as soon as the waiter came over. We got the hummus with pita and veggies, the indian style yams, lemon rice, whole roasted cauliflower, and mushroom bolognese. The waiter recommended we order one more dish as it might not be enough food for 3 people and he recommended the asian shoots which we got. All of the portions were small which is aggravating as they are expensive. The hummus, yams and rice were all good though nothing to write home about and the other food was extremely disappointing. The shoots were bitter and sitting in a flavorless liquid. They had no flavor and a soggy texture. The cauliflower, which one of us had tried before, came out as complete mush. It is supposed to crispy, but it was completely overcooked and fell apart, so much so if you touched it with your fork it crumbled. The bolognese had great flavor but the pasta was completely undercooked. It was RAW in the inside. We sent it back and were given another bolognese on the house.

The other main issue was the service. Our waiter never told us the specials and never gave us clean plates (if you've had the cauliflower, it takes over the entire plate and makes a mess). For an upscale restaurant, you expect fresh utensils and plates. This however, is all forgivable except for the fact that when I brought this up to the manager, Nathan, after we had paid the check and were leaving, he looked completely disinterested and made eye contact for 10% of the conversation. He said they have a policy of not replacing plates unless asked per the chef's wishes (though the waiter offered the table next to us fresh plates) and was in disbelief about the cauliflower as it is their "signature dish" and said we should have said something. I explained we decided not to because so many other things had gone wrong so we let that go and he continued to look away (almost like I wasn't talking to him). I had started the conversation by saying that we were not complaining, merely letting him know because if I was a manager I would want to know and I repeated that throughout, but he acted like a disgruntled child who was being chastised. I explained I had eaten at other Jean Georges restaurants and was surprised by this experience. He never apologized, never invited us back so they could make it up to us, NOTHING. This is  unacceptable for any restaurant, let alone a fancy establishment.

Needless to say this is one of the worst dining experiences I have had in NYC and I would never go back.

I have been wanting to get down try this spot for awhile now. Last night was the night. Great vibe, I was originally excited to be seated facing the open kitchen (through a window) but after sitting the for the dinner and chat I got up to use the bathroom (unisex and half in the kitchen) and saw the room with was much more interesting then the kitchen. I would suggest closing the view and giving Great Wall maybe with mirrors. 
Ok the wine was great and all of the 7 dishes (for 2 of us) were amazing with the exception of the $62 tofu skin with truffle. It just had no flavor and was rubbery! But the desserts were amazing! I would definitely be back. Different view and no pricey tofu skin.

Best vegan restaurant I've been to!! 

All dishes are meant to be shared and the presentations are very well executed. 

Love the ambience and the interiors as well!

OH. MY. GOD. This is one of THE BEST restaurants I have been to in NYC and probably the best vegan/vegetarian restaurant I've ever been to. 

Let's start with the interior - it was absolutely beautiful. But what else would you expect from a furniture store? 

The wait staff was so friendly, knowledgeable, and attentive. 

They advise 2-3 dishes per person for dinner. My friend and I weren't starving so we decided to order 4 total to share. We started with the honey squash with tahini. It was served with warm bread for dipping but you could also spoon the squash into my mouth and I wouldn't complain. Next we had the coconut yogurt curry yams which were a *slight* bit spicy but when mixed with the yogurt were perfect. It was topped with pomegranate seeds for some acid and fried potato shoe strings for crunch. We also ordered the coconut sticky rice which had a great salt to sweet ratio, but not the best sticky rice I've ever had. Last on the savory list was the mushroom walnut bolognese. The pasta was thick and chewy like it was homemade and the sauce had the same texture as a meaty bolognese. 

For dessert, I had the chocolate mousse which so rich but the best vegan dessert I've ever had. My friend had the matcha creme brûlée which was on the smaller and lighter side but still amazing. 

I can't recommend ABCV enough. I wish I lived in NY so I could go here for all of my special occasion meals.
Amazing food, customer service, and atmosphere. We had the best birthday dinner. We loved the cauliflower, sticky rice, and yams the most. We will definitely be back next time in NYC!!

Have had the chance to go to abcV a few times.  The restaurant is very white and open, with a bar in the front and tables in the back.  It is typically crowded, so I would recommend making a reservation or showing up when it opens.  Service was good.

I tried the following dishes:

Green Chickpea Hummus, Thai Basil, Fresh Pita (3.5/5): I had hoped that this would be more spiced, but it was a little bland for my taste.  Did go well with the pita.

Smoky Eggplant, Tomato Chutney, Yogurt, Mint, Fresh Pita (4.5/5): Very smoky, flavorful eggplant that went really well with the pita.

Market Carrots Stone Ground Nut and Seed Butter, Chilies, Lime (3/5): Okay carrot dish.  The carrot was not very well-seasoned, and its accompaniments did not elevate its flavor.

Roasted Cauliflower, Turmeric-Tahini, Pistachios (1.5/5): I did not like the cauliflower.  It was pretty soggy and not well-seasoned.  The turmeric-tahini sauce, while good, was not enough flavor to season the cauliflower.

Soba Noodle, Aromatic Dashi, Oyster Mushrooms, Sea Lettuce, Broccoli (3.5/5): This soba noodle dish is okay, nothing special.

Mushroom Walnut Bolognese, Carrot Paccheri, Celery, Mint Leaf (4.5/5): Really tasty, a must-order.  The bolognese is so rich and complex, and the pasta is so well-cooked.

Bucatini, Artichoke, Spigarello, Fermented Garlic, Mint (4/5): Tasty bucatini that is a must-order, very savory and good.

Dosa, Yogurt, Avocado, Sprouts (4.5/5): Really good dosa, rivals that which you can get an an Indian restaurant.  The yogurt is really rich.

I have enjoyed my experiences at abcV and would return!

This was my first time at any of the ABV restaurants and I was pleasantly surprised. We went there for Sunday brunch and had made a reservation via reserve.com which was smooth. When we reached there we had to wait about 5 mins before our table was ready.

The place is more like a tapas style vegan place where you order small plates to share. We started with Japanese tea for the table. They have a good selection of Teas, coffees, Juices, wines, and cocktails. We ordered sauteed leafy greens(5/5), beluga lentils(5/5) and half avocado(3.5/5) for a party of 2 which was the perfect amount. 

We will go to try their other restaurants next time.

Great place and great food. My brother and I were blown away. We loved lunch so much (and ate many items) we went back the very next morning to try breakfast. At 9am they were closed for breakfast for a private event. A little annoyed they didn't have a warning about it when we were there the day before, but we will be back!

This place makes it seem easy to be a vegetarian. If I had a personal chef this is the food I would be eating all the time. Healthy, beautiful, inventive and a wide diversity of international flavors and cooking techniques. 

I had the dosa with avocado and yogurt. It was simple but amazing. My wife had the mushrooms with poached eggs. This dish I've had in so many ways.  Two ingredients that go so well together and if done right creates a divine pairing.  In fact I make my own version that is one of my go to dishes to impress friends. ABC's stand ups to some of the best I've had it made myself. 

We also had two fresh pressed juices and two cups of coffee. All beverages were wonderful. 

This simple breakfast was satisfying and nourishing. The space is elegant, bright and tranquil. A great place to dine. 

But all this thoughtful food and ambience comes at a very hefty price. This meal (two breakfast entrees, two coffees and two juices) ran us $100. Worth it?  Sure to me it was, but can't afford to eat here regularly. However if I want to treat myself to something delicious and healthy this is at the top of the list.

When the ingredients are so good and fresh, you don't need complicated recipes. Every dish was an explosion of flavor, with interesting textures and unexpected pairings. The ingredients are seasonal and their taste is intense and rich. Loved the carrots with hazelnut butter, the squash dip with sourdough (see pic), but what caught my heart were the winter radishes, fresh and crunchy. Great cocktails, too! The staff is polite and very helpful, giving suggestions about food & drinks. Plates are meant to be shared, which creates a very intimate experience.

Beautiful from start to finish. The decor is simple, sweet and sleek - a devastating achievement of minimalism, which translates to the menu offerings. We had a pot of mint tea which ended up being a french press size portion to hold us over the entire meal and shared the slow roasted beets, wok fried shoots and mushroom walnut bolognese. 

The shared plates outshined the main by a mile in both visual and gustatory categories. The beets were bright and punchy (thanks to the pickles, chilli aioli and Dijon) yet unctuous with the avocado purée. The presentation was also a stunning opener to the meal, a muted fireworks display of magenta and lime green. The shoots were both hearty and light and the warmth of the broth was a lovely balance to the preceding cold dish. 

The pasta didn't stand a chance after the above were set. Through it claimed to have celery, carrot and mint leaf, none of that came through on the palate and thus rendered a bite one note and dull, both in sight and taste. 

I would happily return and stick with the big V items until they can sort out how to have the veg shine even on heavier offerings. 

Lastly, service was exemplary with the exception of the hostess who appeared bored and whose polite words belied a disdain for those arriving.

It's such a rare and beautiful thing when you can have a thoughtfully-prepared, indulgent yet healthy breakfast over good conversation. This is one of the top breakfasts I've had. I really enjoyed the coconut yogurt with figs, the overall aesthetic and as I mentioned the painstaking care that appeared to have been put into our meal. Loved it!

Came here for a work lunch and was really blown away by the quality of the food here. Who knew ABC Carpet & Home held such secrets? I guess literally everybody but me. But I'm glad I'm in on the secret now, because what ABCV does, it does quite nicely.

What ya got here is fancy vegan tapas, so you order a buncha little dishes and split as needed. I myself am not vegan (or even vegetarian) but I appreciate vegan restaurants because usually the food is super fresh and the recipes are really interesting. And ABCV is certainly a solid choice in those respects. I got to try the green chickpea hummus (VERY excellent), market carrots (solid), fresh hearts of peach palm (not normally my bag, but I was very pleasantly surprised by this passion fruit and basil situation), market vegetable chop salad (an excellent salad served over sticky rice which works surprisingly well without feeling kitschy), kimchee fried brown sticky rice (solidly spicy), and the smoked tofu and shiitake bahn mi (big enough for two, for sure, and markedly excellent). 

The ingredients here can sometimes be a little left-field in their attempts to reinvent the wheel-there's nothing straight forward, even the carrots include chilies and lime-but everything together tastes fantastic so in that sense it feels almost like a tasting menu style restaurant. The prices of these dishes also reflect that (speaking of, the carrots are $17), so it's definitely a little much for me to come back regularly. But if you're vegan, this seems like an especially fun fancy place to check out or treat yourself to.
Coconut yogurt and avocado toast were insanely good! Definitely coming back next time I'm in town.
Delicious lunch in bright open spaces; new favorite when I'm in this neighborhood.  Ban mi was amazing and shared dishes of carrots and mustard greens memorable.

I'm not sure if I get the hype about this place although I admit my experience here started off on a negative note: My friend and I had a reservation for brunch and were made to wait 20 minutes from our reserved time. No apologies or anything for making us wait.
My dosa was fine but I was still hungry after eating it. My friend's dish was pretty flavorless. I didn't really feel there was anything special about this place to warrant a second trip.

A group of us came for a birthday celebration and we are so glad we did. The ambiance is modern, classy and intimate. The service was great and the food is just amazing. We shared 6-8 plates and opted for all vegan. There are some items that are not vegan but they can make it vegan. For example, the dosa we chose came with avocado, sprouted greens and cashew based yogurt. The lettuce avocado cups were so flavorful too. The pasta bolognese was "meaty" and perfectly flavored. The kimchee stir fried brown rice was also interesting and tasty. We also asked for hot sauce and it was a homemade habanero style sauce which was amazing. They also had rock sea salt on the table in case you wanted to sprinkle it on your foods. For dessert we got the coconut custard with seasonal fruits (gooseberries, pears and pomegranate). I definitely recommend making reservations. Great for date nite or with a group of friends.

Incredible. I've been here for both breakfast and dinner and I'm consistently blown away by how delicious everything is and how intriguing the menu options are.

Even if you tend to frequent these kinds of health-focused hipster restaurants, you still won't know what half of the ingredients on the menu are, and you'll find yourself Googling exotic cheeses made from thistle rennet or the names of arctic berries you're not familiar with. 

I've tried maybe 12 menu items in all and not one failed to utterly blow my mind. You can't go wrong ordering anything with mushrooms, and all of the cocktails are well balanced and satisfying.

If you're the kind of person who is turned off by unfamiliar menu items/dishes, or who need huge potions to feel like your money was well spent, or who needs meat to be on the menu, I'll be honest, you might not love this place. But for anyone else, I promise if you take a chance on the food here, you will find that vegetables can be more delicious than you ever thought possible.

YAY! I am literally a fan! I really have no negatives here. And I don't give out 5 starts that easy! Have been to ABC Kitchen before, and am planning to go to ABC cocina now!

This was my birthday dinner with my husband and as expected the food was GREAT! I started with their KOMBUCHA SANGRIA. It was great, such a nice balance of sweetness of fruits with the sour kombucha. Next from Light fares we ordered "pine nut and lemon, harissa, dried apricot, fresh pita" which was a perfect combination of creaminess against the sweet and sour apricots with a crunch of the pine nuts. Also we ordered the "tatsoi and butter bean, citrus broth, avocado, kale, herbal crispbread". This was a soup with spicy and sour broth with avocado and kale in it and let me tell you this broth was truly a delight on a cold winter evening! Next of course we had to get the "half or whole roasted cauliflower with turmeric-tahini and pistachios". The cauliflower was so perfectly cooked, you could just slice through it effortlessly and no question about the flavors, they were top notch. Next can the "fresh tofu, spicy szechuan pepper oil, peanuts, grilled and pickled cucumber". This dish was so different than anything else that I have tasted till now. Let me tell you, if you haven't tasted fresh tofu, it tastes VERY different than the store bought tofu and it is for sure worth trying. 

For Dessert, we had "chocolate mousse poached pears, almonds" Such a delight! This will make any chocolate fan HAPPY! And on top of all of these great dishes, they brought me a complimentary "matcha crème brûlée" as a birthday dessert! This experience just made my day! Loved the service, loved the food, and will definitely keep visiting!

First of all this place is just gorgeous!  Everything is white, light and spotless.  The staff is lovely.  Brooke helped us and she was amazing!  All her recommendations were perfect.  The food is all healthy, beautiful and so yummy!  The vibe here is fun... no wonder there is a line outside waiting for it to open at 11:00am.

Hands down one of the best restaurants in the city! We are regulars here and I have to say, every time we come in it just gets better and better. The menu is fantastic, the cocktails are great, the service is fabulous and the restaurant is beautiful! Every single dish leaves us feeling wowed and I cant wait to go back again soon!  Also, for those who are wondering which ABC to try if they are only going to try one, I personally would say this is the best! Abc Kitchen is a close second and while Abc Cocina is good, the other two definitely outshine it.

Wonderful lunch here over the fall. Decent drinks. We had the foragers salad which actually had decent black morels which are certainly difficult to get grit free so color me impressed.
We had crudités with the pea guacamole which was delicious BUT they took it away before we were finished. 
Lentils amazing and almond butter amazing.
Dosas are my new favorite obsession.
Matcha brûlée delicious as can be. 

Beautiful dishes in a beautiful space.

The emperor has no clothes!

Wow, this place must have a great marketing team but if you look closely it is a pretentious overhyped overpriced sham. 
The food is good but served in teeny tiny portions by a  disheveled staff  wearing t shirts that look like dirty dishwater to "compliment" the all white decor.
There were lots of signs that this place is absurd, like the chunk out of a, not particularly fresh, head of lettuce served preciously along side the eggplant dip. 
The straw that broke the camels back was an $18 small plate of beans. The waiter upselled us on adding a poached egg to the dish which was not on the menu. 
The added cost? $7 !!! After tax and tip... over $9 for a freaking single poached egg!!
The food is not exceptional. 
Never again.

Nice experience with a vegetarian menu. I love that you can see them making the food; the wall of windows and open bar area is so interesting to watch! 

Unfortunately, we made a reservation at 9:30, and were a little upset that they didn't sit us until 9:50. Wish they could have planned that better.

Best Dishes:
1. Plain Dosa! The dosa is perfect. Crunchy in some parts, and a little fluffier in others. I'm sure dosa with herbs and yogurt is good, but we enjoyed dipping ours into the sauces of the other dishes we ordered.

2. Hummus/pita: great hummus! Glad that you can get refills of pita too!

Other dishes:
Carrots! The carrots and the nut butter combined to make a flavor I never had before. The red sauce was a bit too hot for me.

Bolognese: very al dente and savory.

Artichoke hearts: grapefruit and the hearts were a great combo!

Shiitake: not super rubbery, but nothing spectacular 

Cauliflower: really good! I didn't really like the sauce that much, but loves the herbs, pomegranate seeds, and pistachios

This place would have gotten a 4th star from me if it wasn't so overpriced. I know certain places exist to be upscale and overpriced but ABCv had only a few dishes worthy of the price. It's definitely a place you go to on a special occasion but not just a regular dining spot. The cauliflower was bland as was the dressing for the cauliflower. The coconut rice was to die for, though and really made us want more. The cocktails were overpriced and small. As I said, I expected that. But they need to step up their game to justify the price and small portion size.

I live nearby and have been here 3 times (twice for brunch, once for dinner). I have yet to have a seamless experience, but food is pretty tasty. 

For dinner, I highly recommend the cauliflower entree. For brunch, I love the avocado dosa, the roasted beets, and wild mushrooms with poached eggs (I'm vegan and have not had the eggs but friends seem to like it). 

Getting to the service... everyone here is very nice but overall execution needs improvement. When I brought my husband here for his birthday dinner, they forgot to put a candle in his dessert (I had written this in the notes of the reservation and also called ahead to confirm). They were nice enough to comp us for the desserts. But come on.. this was a BASIC request that an abc restaurant, or any restaurant for that matter, should not have had difficultly to fulfill. 

When I  came here for the first time for brunch, they did not separate the poached eggs from the wild mushrooms as requested - this was pretty disappointing for a restaurant that specializes in catering to people with dietary restrictions. 

The second time I came from brunch, I ordered the same wild mushroom dish and it was half the size of what I ordered on my prior visit. Also, our food came out before our drinks arrived.

My fiancé and i have been here a few times, it's quite pricey so we only come on occasion. I saw it on a buzzfeed video and it just looked so delicious i have to try it. The atmosphere is minimalistic, and reservations are a must. The plates are small so you will need to order between 4 to 7 plates to share if you want to fill up. The food is so beautifully plated it's almost a shame to eat. This restaurant really impresses me with the amount of preparation that goes into each dish, while still keeping the ingredients simple and clean. We indulged in a few desserts, the chocolate tart and chocolate mousse. They were both phenomenal but if i had to choose i would choose the tart. I love how it was paired with fresh fruit and sorbet.

Amazing vegetarian spot! From the vibe, decor, menu, ingredients used, I highly recommend to try this place. Plates are large and definitely shareable, good cocktails for brunch. Gets very crowded, I highly recommend making reservations. The staff made some great recommendations and ate everything clean.

Went here for vday! I'm glad I experienced it but Nothing really stood out to us. Kinda hyped up. Food was good but portions were small for the price, especially when you go with a meat eater you wanna show them a good time at a vegan spot. Ambiance was great, but bathroom is weird!! In best to worst order, we got he campenelli pasta, the califlower and the beets. Not in a rush to go back.

I'll start by saying I'm an artichoke snob. So we ordered the hummus, nice and green tasted fresh & actually green. Highly recommend that. The smoked eggplant was equally excellent. It was mentioned that it would be spicy but coming from someone like myself who's nose runs at the sight of the word spicy, it was not! Ok, onto the artichoke dish: do not get it if you love artichokes and the actual flavor of artichokes and if you want to actually taste artichoke! What an odd paring of flavors it was! So the dish was generous with 3 artichoke hearts stuffed with some sort of purée I couldn't place along with the predominance of pignoli nuts...ugh! The chokes were choked out by those intense flavors and besides, the menu said grilled when they were actually torched on a high brow Japanese burner complete with the torched gas flavor....I know raw fish cuisine isn't only produced by the Japanese but leave the torch behind on those Italian artichokes! Garnished with a nice intense olive oil and the extremely green olives where their flavor may have been rancid nooo!!!! And placed on top of the tastiest orange, grapefruit and blood orange slices. Sticky rice meh. Yams were cooked to perfection with way to many flavors going on alongside them but still yummy on some level. Cocoa drink in a wine glass so don't think your ordering a gym sized smoothie. The place is huge! Spanning 18th-19th Street. Be sure to walk around the whole place. We entered on the 19th street side not knowing there was more. Hence that's the side on which we sat. Save for the warm lighting & tea light candles, the place was cafeteria loud! I don't know if I ate too much or what but upon leaving I began to feel bloated, full, crampy & now 4 hours later gas pain...must have been all those cruceriferi or that tasty eggplant! How is my bloated body going to get any sleep! Goodnight.

I was shocked by how much I loved this meal.   Don't let vegetarian cuisine fool you, this place is awesome.  My favorite dish was the carrots.  Capanelle pasta was a close second, but I enjoyed mostly  everything (cauliflower, lettuce cups). I could live without coconut rice and asparagus special.  Waiter was fantastic.  Yay!

This is the best restaurant in the city. Not only is the food incredible but the staff is great too. Peyton and Kevin at the bar during the day are wonderful. I highly recommend sitting there if you're alone.

Had my anniversary dinner here last week with boyfriend. Came ontime for our reservation at 6:30PM, and host attempted to seat us at a high-top, while many two-tops were available. Asked for the reg dining table, we got it with a little wait, idk why. We all know high-tops are for walk-in, or emergency seating cus the floor is full, or if a reservation specifically asked for it. Also the sommelier or the manager, idk which, checks on tables in a very stalker-y way, made eye contacts every other minutes but no smile.. like? can I help you?
Shavonne, our server, who was v friendly, made up the annoyance caused in the front. 3 stars for the food; we loved the Grilled Donko Shiitake, Mushroom Walnut Bolognese, and Coconut Custard (We had the Beluga Lentils and Kimchee Fried Brown Rice too). Must try drink; Mindful (green juice).
Would I come back? maybe if my boyfriend drags me there again just because he's vegan ‍

Food is good but every time I go the servers aggressively try to rush my party. They come by the table every 2/3 minutes so they made it pretty obvious. I recommended abcv to a few coworkers and they had the same experience. The table next to us tonight even said the same thing. It's annoying and doesn't make for a pleasant experience.
The famous cauliflower dish was actually not as good as everyone recommended. It was saying bit on the mushy side. But the lettuce wrap, roasted baby carrots, and avocado spread was delicious.

I had really high expectations of ABCV after hearing so many great things about this place but I left disappointed and hungry for more. I ordered the wild mushroom, poached farm eggs, shallots and herbs and the avocado lettuce cups to share and each plate was more disappointing than the next. The wild mushroom dish was ok but expected more for the price tag (same went for the avocado cups). Overall, if you're on a diet and in need of some healthy, guilt free food, I would recommend this place but otherwise eh, I'd probably pick somewhere else.

This was my 4th time at ABCV and loved it as much as the first. Dishes are creative, robust in flavor, and very satisfying! Definitely pricy, but worth it for a nice occasion. Nearly everything is vegan or could be made vegan. Even the vegan brunch options are phenomenal. Thats where I typically struggle the most. 

Came for Brunch with a group of 4 and ordered the following...

Vanilla Chia Bowl 
Super yummy, one of my faves. Not overly sweet
Egg Cheddar Mint Dosa -- group said it was very tasty & herby!

Mushroom and Eggs
Group said this dish fell a bit short, mushrooms were a little slimy and underflavored

Sweet Potato Bowl 
Crowd favorite. Sweet potato was cooked perfectly. Had a great mix of greens over top and a delightful crunch. Really good dish 

Beets 
DELICIOUS. These were really a star of the show. Sweet beets enhanced with oil and a light vinegar, tiny pickles, and an avocado puree.  Will make a beet hater love beets. 

Green Hummus w Pita 
Expected a standard hummus. This was shockingly good. Not your average hummus. Nice minty / herby flavor. They offer extra pita for free when you run out

Smoked Potatoes
Another crowd favorite! Super crispy. Smoky touch is not overdone. The aoli is vegan and so yummy. Eat with the hot sauce on the table.

Vegan Einkorn Panacke
This is really good. The butter on top is delicious. Fruit is baked into the bottom of the pancake. Really really good

We were very satisfied after this much food. They recommend 3-4 per person If you don't come for the food, come for the celeb sightings. I have seen both Maggie Gyllenhaal with her family and Seth Meyers with his the last two times I was here. The only reason I gave this 4 stars instead of 5 is that I wish it were a bit more affordable. For the more innovative dishes I get it, but a $7 drip coffee is absurd.

This is the best (and probably most expensive) vegetarian restaurant I have ever been to. Went for a work dinner and shared a bunch of things. Everything was delicious, but the most memorable for me were the green chickpea hummus, carrots with stone ground nut and seed butter, grilled shiitake mushrooms, strawberry salad (an off-menu special), and matcha creme brûlée. Nothing is heavy here and the best part is that can eat a bunch of stuff without feeling gross later. The cocktails are also great.

Had Saturday lunch here and it was a pretty good take on vegan food. We ordered the dosa sambal kimchi rice, the hummus, and a coconut custard. The dosa sambal was very good but I would skip on the kimchi rice ( it takes like soy sauce). The hummus is a must and coconut custard nothing special try something else. The staff is very friendly and the drinks are very good. It's a good experience just read on what's good before ordering.

abcV is open for breakfast on weekdays, lunch and dinner on weekdays and brunch and dinner on weekends. A table here on a Saturday for brunch at 12:00 PM wasn't easy to get. The entire restaurant was fully booked with reservations until 3:00 PM when I asked. If you want to dine here for their weekend brunch, I'd suggest to make a reservation in advance! My group of three decided to sit on the counter, but we still had to wait around 45 minutes for a spot.

WHAT I ORDERED:
Fresh steamed tofu - roasted cauliflower, harissa, coconut yogurt, pistachio 

Vegan einkorn pancake - banana, pear, salted coconut butter, maple syrup

MY THOUGHTS:
The first thing I noticed was that the restaurant menu was easy to read and well-designed. It wasn't overwhelming with options like some brunch places. A lot of their dishes I've never seen before so I really liked how it was unique. I really enjoyed my fresh steamed tofu with roasted cauliflower, harrissa, coconut yogurt and pistachio. It was such an unique dish and all the ingredients worked really well together. The vegan einkorn pancake was also amazing. I loved the banana and pear inside the pancake and the salted coconut butter and maple syrup made the dish even more perfect. My friend ordered the Chia Pudding. Not sure how much he enjoyed it, but he didn't complain that it wasn't good. It wasn't one of their more unique dishes though. 

I didn't get a chance to order dessert because we were extremely full. However, I did see a lot of dessert bringing brought out for people and it looked delicious! I've posted the dessert menu below if you want to take a look. 

Service was a bit slow, but that's because they were so busy! It only made sense! Food was great and the price wasn't ridiculous. I would say abcV was one of the best plant-based restaurants I dined at during my visit in New York. You should come check it out if you have the chance!

Delicious food. Their roasted turmeric cauliflower is bomb! The baby mustard greens were good, a lil salt heavy but still good. The portions are good so don't order too much or you'll be asking for a doggy bag later. The creme brûlée was solid. They make a good mushroom walnut bolognese too! (Yes, i eat a lot lol). Pretty white, glossy ambience. Prices are pretty average to most nice Manhattan restaurants. I sat at the bar and the bartender was very nice and attentive. Drank one of their ginseng tonics. It was light and refreshing. Give this place a try, I'll definitely come back.

Horrible service. I was 10 minutes late, I called the restaurant to tell them that I'm gonna be late. I couldn't reach to them in my first three tries. Then I finally got on the phone with a person after 15 min wait on the phone. I was then re-assured by the person on the phone that my table is being held for me. When I reached there they didn't hold my table and asked me to wait another 30 minutes. The arrogant hostess whose role is to greet and treat guests laughed at my face when she realized we missed the reservation by a minute. Horrible staff, service!

Came here for brunch on a visit to NYC and this was by far our best meal in the city. First off, the space is beautiful and so zen. I loved the chandeliers and the rustic vibe. The service is impeccable and our waiter offered some great recommendations. We decided to share our entrees tapas style, and I'm glad that we did as everything was so delicious. We started with the dosa with sambal, cheddar, egg and mint. The egg and cheddar literally melted into the dosa and the sambal elevated it to the next level. The kimchee fried brown sticky rice had so much depth and the mushrooms were so flavorful. The fresh steamed tofu with cauliflower, harissa, yogurt and pistachio was quite tasty. I was pleasantly surprised with the sweet potato bowl which was cooked perfectly and had great texture with the addition of seeds and peanuts. The chef was very accommodating as one of our friends had dietary restrictions which was much appreciated. Can't wait to come back and sample the rest of the menu!

Finally made it here for brunch! Wonderful service and the ambiance is inviting, warm, and upscale. Our server informed us that the servings were tapas sized and that we should get 2-3 per person. My husband and I decided to start with 4 and go from there. When the dishes came they were NOT tapas sized. We were stuffing ourselves by the 3rd dish and asked our server if the 4th dish (vegan pancake) was already being made, we told him we were expecting smaller portions as he advised us and we were not going to be able to eat the 4th dish. 

He checked and came back to tell us that it was already on the griddle and there was nothing he could do. He packed this 4th dish in a to-go box and bag for us to take. We told him that we were expecting tapas size like he told us and he said there was nothing he could do. 

The food could have been a bit more flavorful and the whole experience wasn't horrible, just extremely disappointing at the end since we felt as though we were mislead. We also waited about 10 min for the 4th dish to come out from when we told our server to see if it could be canceled. 

We will be back, but will keep in mind the serving sizes and hope the overall experience is better.
Rya and Megan were amazing the food was absolutely delicious and it's such a chic space it's one of my favorite places in New York City!!! Don't miss.

Whether you eat meat or not (I do), the food at abcV is incredible. I love my veggies, and I was really excited to see such innovative and delicious preparations here. We ordered the green chickpea hummus, roasted carrots, the half roasted cauliflower, mushrooms, the coconut sticky rice, and the fried wild rice (this was also all vegan!). The highlights for me were definitely the hummus, the cauliflower, and the coconut sticky rice. I'd seen pictures of the roasted cauliflower everywhere and was a bit skeptical, but it definitely lives up to the hype. So delicious -- perfectly roasted, and I loved the turmeric sauce! 

The service was pretty good, although it does take a while for the dishes to come out here. In terms of vibes, the design of the restaurant feels bright and modern in a way that reminds me of IKEA, which I mean in the most positive way (love me some IKEA). Honestly, it is really exciting to me whenever I find a vegetarian restaurant that emphasizes the flavors and textures of the vegetables, instead of trying to pretend to be a more omnivore-friendly place. Looking forward to having more meals here!

Really great use of flavors but way to expensive for the quantity being served. Each dish was 5 bites and the bill ended up with a 250$ bill. It's a great place to check out if you want to sample a bunch of plates. Really cool interior and a decent staff.

Absolutely amazing! 
Went there few times and every time was so happy. Their avocado wraps are amazing i could eat them All day. Cauliflower is the best i ever had! 
Everything is super good. Service could improve though, waiters were kinda slow.
My new favorite place! Everything is perfect I don't even know what else to say. The vibe was light and airy in the best way. The staff was warm. The music was fun. The food was made with with.

The food is very good however went down hill from there. 2 plates were chipped and broken the response from the staff was " it adds to the shabby chic" really? What about possibilities of Being cut. Wow! We were 4 in our party 2 got food then waited 20 minutes for the other 2. Food coordination could of been better. And the final why does everyone working there have a "subtle rude" attitude. Why is that needed. Plenty of other places to spend good money

Brunch on Easter Sunday - food was good - I ordered scrambled eggs and asked to replace or pay for the sweet potato  that came with another item on the menu  instead of the broccoli - explained medical reason - was told no -  and the broccoli never came out with the eggs for others to share-  chips in plates were explained as - we are saving money and it's shabby chic here anyway  - you have to be kidding  - waitress and manager were flippant and a bit rude - the waitress was clearly trying to close her station and took my placemat while I was still drinking my coffee.  Was told the kitchen was closed and 10 minutes latter folks were seated next to us and were served . 
Would not go back ever

I've been to the following Jean Georges restaurant in NYC - Jean Georges, Nougatine, ABC Kitchen, Mercer Kitchen - but ABCV was different. Not because I'm not a vegetarian/vegan. 

The interior is beautiful like ABC Kitchen with beautiful chandeliers. A lot of white was used for the interior design which was very fitting for the cool vibe. 

Food is delicious here. It's tapas style so make sure everyone at the table is comfortable sharing dishes. I've only dine here for dinners and the dinner menu is much more extensive. Also, they refresh their menu every season but some of the diners' favs have remained. 

I've had the following dishes here (listed in the order of deliciousness):
- cauliflower 
- asparagus (special of the day)
- yam
- shittake
- pine nut and lemon
- green chickpea hummus
- beets
- lentils
- coconut sticky rice
- mushroom walnut bolognese 

Do be aware - service here varies depending on the server you get for the night. One time, my second drink came out too late that it was eventually on the house. 

Drinks and desserts - I've had only cocktails here but there is a wide variety of non-alcoholic drinks available. Also, don't skip out on the dessert. Everything on the dessert menu is amazing! 

Overall, if you are looking for a different Jean Georges experience that is a little bit more casual, fun, with delectable vegetarian/vegan food, check out ABCV. You'll leave the restaurant very full and guilt free~!

Vegetarian! I'm not a vegetarian, but I thought I'd check it out as it is part of the ABC family and I like the other two restaurants. 
Service is friendly, but slowwwwwwwww - much like the other two spots. 
I love the space, it's bright and you can see the kitchen working through large glass panels in the back. 

Brunch order: blueberry bowl and einkorn pancakes. 
The blueberry bowl was good, but not amazing. Came out chilled, but it wasn't slushy or icy in any way. There's a dribble of peanut butter (unlike other bowls that give you a big scoop), but I actually thought it was a bit too little. Portion is small. Not a lot of fruits... I was hoping it would be loaded with fruits. The fruits that they do give you aren't guaranteed to be sweet (but at the price they're charging you for, the fruits really should be sweet). So overall, it's alright and overpriced. 

Einkorn pancakes. First time trying einkorn pancakes so wasn't sure what to expect. The menu description made it seem like there would be, again, a lot of fruits, but the pancake came out plain (and sort of ugly, could use better plating techniques) on the outside with a few fruits stuffed on the inside. I'm guessing this is because the pancake itself is a little dry, and adding fruits would give it more moisture. Wasn't impressed. 

I had higher expectations for the food given that they specialize in plant-based food. Going in, everything seemed fresh and easy to like. A lot of items on the menu looked pretty good. Thought I'd be having an engaging brunch, but everything came out falling short. It's a great choice to get some vegetables, but not the best choice, and not what it purports to be.

Came here for brunch. Everything was very delicious. My partner and I ordered the mushrooms, the juices, Swiss chard dosa, and slow roasted beets. All the vegetables were properly prepared, cooked but still retaining the integrity and structure of the ingredients. The food was quite light and refreshing. The juices were good, but perhaps a bit overpriced and not as adventurous in flavor as I would have hoped.

I am in love with this restaurant! I went for the first time last night with a friend who is Vegan, I am Vegetarian..The food is so good and everything is well prepared, it takes some time but SOOOO with the wait..Very friendly good looking staff..Looking forward to my next visit..;-))

Tapas style vegan restaurant, I do not find the food amazing but you will feel hungry after a high price meal. The dosa crepe was the best item in their menu. A dosa is a type of pancake or crèpe, originating from the Indian subcontinent, made from a fermented batter.

Let me start off by saying I love NYC and I understand everything here is expensive. However this place reminds me of everything wrong with this city. 7$ for a drip coffee? Are you serious? I don't care if it's laced with gold, that is ridiculous. There's a reason mom and pop type businesses are becoming a thing of the past and it's because of places like ABCV. Seemingly trendy, pretty aesthetic, reasonably good food, but total lack of realness.

I am in love with his restaurant (I'm not a vegetarian), and I keep going back! The service is alright and sometimes the loud sounds when it's busy, can be overwhelming, although this does not stop me from going back to eat this food again and again. Great attention for detail and the highest quality and freshest ingredients are used.

What a great atmosphere they have! I'm not a vegetarian but loved the concept and the interior so decided to give it a try. All the ingredients were so fresh and the smell of every dish was amazing. All the dish were flavorful and delightful to watch.

The service was pretty nice and fast. I made a reservation at 7:30ish on Satuday and sat right in. The place was packed and felt little crowded because the tables were so close by each others. 

Grapefruit vodka cocktail - it was a tonight's special drink with grapefruit infused vodka with micro leaves. It was pretty strong but the aroma was strong too, it was pleasant sips throughout.

Strawberries - fresh strawberry (it was pickled lightly? It tasted little sour and soft) with avocado. Very light and flavorful. The aroma was so fresh and pleasant, I'm not sure where is that coming from since it's a simple dish. 

Beets - the avocado puree was a gem, it was a new way of eating beets, I wouldn't have known this was beet just by tasting it. 

Half of the Cauliflower - didn't really like this dish, still had some its significant Cauliflower taste, nothing really special.

It was expected but my fiancé and I were still hungry after three dishes, but felt healthy :) I would love to come back with my girlfriends, and take my parents to this place.

A vast and extremely array of things plant based delicacies even the innermost herbivore can marvel at. A contemporary decor mixed with casual service aesthetic was a nice touch to take away a from what would initially ooze pretentious ambience. My fiancé and I were plentifully hydrated by a wonderful server who honestly could have received the whole tip if I'd had anything to do with it. The food was phenomenal, and honestly the lettuce cups being the pinnacle of the mains selection, with the rhubarb ice cream dominating dessert. Dining without drinks and service cost us around $95 minus the tip (so around £73 for us brits). My suggestions for improvement? Lil less Hollister lighting, fried tofu for the chilli tofu and colder taps!

Beautiful interior, clean crisp cocktails (both alcoholic and nonalcoholic), delicious vegetarian and vegan cuisine. The lighting here is amazing. It is one of the three ABC restaurants located attached to the ABC store.

I've been to ABCV twice now and they still take claim to having the fanciest vegetables I've ever had in my life. The food is decently small portioned and pricey, so I'd recommend only coming here for a special occasion as you can expect to spend about $100+ for two people on dinner, not including drinks. The atmosphere is upscale yet executed in a way that it's not pretentious, but instead eccentric and cozy (much like its storefront namesake). 

Don't let the menu intimidate you - the food is simple in execution yet bold in taste. Whatever you get; you will be pleasantly surprised, though some things are better than others. My absolute go-to's are the avocado lettuce wraps and roasted cauliflower. Trust me on these - they will not disappoint. It's a shame everything is so expensive, because I'd love to venture from my known order without there being such a steep consequence if I don't like the dish at hand. We tried the Szechuan tofu this time around and would have rather ordered a second helping of the lettuce wraps instead (but that's hindsight for you...)

Overall, the experience is one worth having. Plates are great for sharing, so get a large group together and try one of everything!

This is one great vegetarian restaurant.  It doesn't look as upscale as it really is,  but don't let that dissuade you.  It's definitely worth a visit.  The variety of choices on the menu should make a vegetarian's heart pound.  But the real payoff is in the flavors that come from the kitchen.  What wonderful combinations.  The only drawback is that the visit will come out a bit pricey.  Each dish on the menu is only large enough to feed half a person.  So figure about two or more dishes per dinner.  With drinks and desert figure to spend close to a hundred per.  But worth it.

My girlfriend and I went to this restaurant while in town after hearing rave reviews from our New York friends. This restaurant seemed perfect as my girlfriend is a veterinarian and everything on the menu was vegetable based. Unfortunately, our trip to ABCV fell far short of expectations as the food was not in line with the price point the restaurant was placing for it. Not the worst place in the world, but would only recommend if you're looking for nice ambiance, a meal you'll feel good about eating after, and you're not scared off by paying $25 for vegetables. 

Service: service at ABCV is fantastic. Our waiter was very knowledgeable and food came out fast and warm. No issues with service.

Atmosphere: the ambiance at ABCV is great. Very nice setting for a date night or casual dinner with friends. Volume in restaurant wasn't too loud where you can't hold a conversation. No issues with atmosphere.

Food: the food is where ABCV severely fell apart for my girlfriend and I. We ordered the house favorite cauliflower and it lacked any real flavor. Simply just steamed cauliflower with fancy seasoning but did nothing special in terms of overall flavor. Other dishes included yams, tofu, and beans, all of which were trying too hard to be "upscale" but again didn't scream unique or entice the pallet.

As I mentioned, this is a fun/trendy spot to get a night started, but if you're looking for a truly flavorful dinner where the food is the main focus, save your money and go elsewhere.

Note won't seat you until whole party has arrived. Went for a late brunch and thoroughly enjoyed it! Lovely ambiance and pretty table settings. Had a Strawberry Hill cocktail that was delicious and perfect for May! The ideal is to share and they lost a point because they recommended 1 dish too many. The hummus was amazing as was the poached egg and mushrooms. Coconut fruit yogurt bowl was also refreshing and unique. Whole wheat toast and Dosa dish were fine. I'm allergic to pitted fruit including avocados which feature heavily in the menu and they kindly offered to put it in the side if desired.

The food was outstanding! I appreciated the originality of so many dishes, I tried many dishes and was blown away by depth of flavor everything had. Our servers shavvone and Will were professional and attentive. Thanks for an awesome meal!

Love the food at this place. The chef is incredible and so creative. The ingredients and flavors are top notch. Honestly I can't get enough. Only reason it has four stars and not five is that I have had inconsistent customer service. Most of the time it is great! But there have been times where the staff is forgetful or a little rude. Overall though one of my favorite restaurants in NYC!

A great dining experience, from start to finish. The food here is inspiring - the flavors are well-developed and the dishes are really thoughtful. I have been both for brunch and for dinner, and think they shine brightest with the later. I love the focus on celebrating vegetables vs making faux burgers or hotdogs, etc, so I truly enjoyed many of the vegetable-focused dishes I tried. I also appreciated that almost everything can be made vegan. My favorites were the avocado lettuce cups (better than expected, a wonderful, light crisp appetizer), and a Japanese yam dish with coconut yogurt and some crispy wonderfullness on top (I'm a sucker for potatoes so this was a home-run to me). The green hummus is also quite good, and the pita is delicious and the vegetables they were served with were incredibly fresh and flavorful. I have also tried the vegan pancake, which had bananas and strawberries baked in and came with a beaker of syrup. The service here is also excellent. You can barely take a sip of water without your glass refilled. One downside: I do think the food is very expensive; that said, I tend to eat very cheaply so it was just odd to me to spend so much on food. That said, it is an exceptional experience and definitely worth a trip for special occasions or a fun treat.

Fancy, expensive, and good.  I ordered a dosa made of yogurt, avocado and sprouts (sprouts were not very noticeable, which is 100% fine with me).  I also had an iced tea with lemon verbena and agave.  I was then served the fanciest looking dosa I ever saw.  It was good!  If I am in the area I will definitely go back.  If the other food is as good as the dosa I'll probably bump this review to five stars.

I don't understand the hype at all. I love vegetables and am happy to pay for good vegetables, but I just left the restaurant feeling extremely ripped off. In many ways, ABCV encapsulates all that I dislike about New York's dining scene - lots of hype, expensive, noisy, pretentious, and yet still difficult to get into. 

We ordered:

Beets - Probably my favorite dish, with thinly sliced beets in olive oil, but the vinegar was too heavy handed.
