Dosa - Good but nothing spectacular. Dosa itself is too thick to be a true dosa, ends up being more like a crepe.

Bamboo shoots in broth (daily special) - Wow it was ~$20 for what amounted to 5 half pieces of bamboo shoot in a broth. Which didn't even taste good (way too bland). I love bamboo shoots and this dish was an affront to bamboo shoots.

Mushroom walnut bolognese - Didn't like the pasta itself, and disliked the taste of walnut with the pasta. 

All in all, I left feeling that there was a flaw in execution with each dish, which is a rare experience for a restaurant of this caliber. Prices are also crazy high - everything is in the $15-$25 range which is a lot given the small portions of veggies that are provided. You can easily drop $70 and still leave feeling hungry.

OMGosh. You will hard pressed to find somewhere with better food and drinks. It's kinda crazy how good this place is. Original too. The dishes are unique as are the beverages. It's a real treat to eat here. It's going to be a regular recommendation. I'll eat here as often as possible!!!
Favourite vegetarian place in NYC! The lettuce wrap, the dosa, the beets are my absolute favourite!!!! If only all place tastes like abcv, it wouldn't be too hard to convert to a vegetarian.

The food is fantastic! I've been a couple of times and was 100% satisfied with every dish. As a vegan, it's so relaxing to be able to order freely from a menu. Some of the dishes we tried: wontons in a lemon broth, dosa with yogurt and avocado, eincorn banana strawberry pancake, fingerling potatoes, green chickpea hummus, rigatoni with walnut "meat" sauce, cauliflower... everything is delicious!

I went for a work lunch today and spending 7$ for a fried or poached egg seems ridiculous, almost as bad as 8$ for half an avocado. I love the environment and the staff is really attentive, the light & fresh lunch menu is so good and great for sharing. I recommend the green chickpea hummus and the casarecce was an amazing entree. I think it's overly expensive, but alas that's the city and in retrospect, you do get a lot of fresh veggies and it's a great atmosphere - so I would come back!
One of my favorite restaurants in the city. The food is fresh and delicious. The cocktails are a perfect match to the food. The service was also 5 stars! Can't wait to come back!

Yoooo first off let me say that there instagram page can be a bit confusing because I thought that this place was all plant based but it's not

But that is ok because the food here is OMG so good. Although there smoothie bowl tasted like a vegan ice cream bowl more than a smoothie the Avocado toast was something special, so crunchy, seasoned to perfection

The pancakes were the absolute best pancakes I have ever tasted in my entire life. They are just to die for so bomb

I have been to abcV during my last two trips to NYC. It's a chic and roomy restaurant. The food is vegetarian and most of the items are either naturally vegan or can be modified to become vegan. I ordered: the rose water lemonade, which I enjoyed tremendously during the hot early July evening, the sautéed beans, which I initially thought were oily but enjoyed more and more as time went on, the bolognese, which I found both attractive and delicious, and the chocolate mouse, which wasn't my favourite. I was seated at the bar but had a server wait on me. Overall, it was a pleasant experience! 

I've been to so many good vegetarian and vegan restaurants in the City, it's hard to decide between 4 and 4 stars. I've taken off one star because of the dessert and also the fact that the place is a bit overpriced.

Unprofessional MaÎtre d'.

We arrived one minute passed our 15 min grace period of our reservation. Even though we called in advance to let them know we were running a little late, she explained to us that as a result we couldn't sit at our table, but instead would have to sit at the bar. 

I would understand this decision except for the fact that there were reservations available for every 15 minute period for our party size for the rest of the night. Clearly the maître d' felt like acting in a petty manner rather than working towards the satisfaction and mutual benefit of her customers and the restaurant. 

I've been here multiple times previously but don't think I'll return in the future.

Four of us went to ABCv for dinner last evening; it was the first time for all. 
The greeter was a bit frosty but not terrible, the service was appropriately efficient, and the food was very good. 
The main issue was the noise level, which was BY FAR the loudest of any restaurant any of us have ever experienced. 
I carry a decibel level meter on my iPhone (a wonderfully useful app, by the way) and just for the fun of it I turned it on -- the arrow was right up against the red line of 95 decibels (the equivalent of a motorcycle engine cranked up to full roar). This made conversation extremely difficult as we were literally yelling to be heard. I've been to quieter rock concerts; my ears are still ringing.
Our reservation was relatively late (7:30 pm); things quieted down a bit later on but the first hour was an aural challenge such as we've never experienced.

The food was highly inventive and mostly very good, but the portions were shockingly small and quite expensive. Considering that it takes three plates to equal an entree, the meal is way too expensive.  The photographs on the site look nothing like the food portions they are serving in July 2019. They are 30 to 40% of the size. As for complimentary bread, that is also a thing of the past.

In addition, it is very loud. We were a party of six seated at a table for 9 and could barely hear anybody who was not right next to us. 

I am a vegetarian and will stick to other places in the future.

We went here for lunch and all I can say is - wow.  Started with the avocado cups - they were amazing. Just a few ingredients come together for a tasty party in your mouth. On to the green hummus and cucumber and avocado salad - again - simple but amazing.  And a sticky rice dish for the main.  
The host was a tad pretentious but it did not stop me from enjoying my experience here.  I will for sure be back when I return to NYC.
Food is better than abckitchen. Service is okay. Get the rice dish for sure. Potatoes with yogurt is super tasty. Skip the califlower.

Where do I begin? The acoustics are so bad that you cannot talk. It was difficult to even speak to the waiter. I recommend bringing a microphone to place your order.

1. Great start. The green hummus and lettuce wraps were very good. Although the pita bread was nothing special and would have been better if they warmed it up a bit.

2. Cauliflower was huge!!! Over cooked so it was mushy. Too many pistachios and herbs. Bland even when we added the tumeric sauce. 

3. Heirloom Carrots. I don't even know what it was???? There's was a mix nut sauce and  that just didn't work. There was no balance of flavors just weird nut sauce and white and orange mushy over cooked carrots. We  could  not eat it . Really bad! 

4. Bolognese pasta. Well congratulations!!!! the pasta was cooked perfectly but the flavor was just ok. 

5. Beluga Lentils were also cooked perfectly and the taste was good . I could of done without the huge chunks of sweet potatoes that just seemed to be dumped in the plate. It over powered the lentils that actually tasted good (when I could find them).

5. We ordered both the sticky rice and fried rice. Someone in the kitchen must of lost the top to the salt. That's all we tasted !!! Sticky salty rice. The fried rice was just ok. Nothing special.

6. And just when I thought we were done with mush then came out the eggplant Dodd's. A thick mushy crepe filled with mushy bland eggplant. I do not think that is the  way dosa   should be prepared . Not good!!!

Dessert - we didn't bother. 

With all that said the restaurant was packed and it's really hard to get a reservation. So maybe it was an off night or missing I am missing what the hype is all about.

The food and everything was wonderful. I'm very impressed, but we sat outside and what is up with the  chairs? I was wearing a dress and had rows of wire that were  digging into me. The entire time I was in pain from the chair. I might have ordered a 3rd cocktail but I couldn't take it anymore.  Those  chairs are painful and need to be replaced or have a cushion.  My guest agreed. Who thought to  use those wire chairs? They are not chairs that say sit and enjoy your dinner rather sit here as long as you can tolerate the pain. The chairs were the main negative to  an otherwise perfect experience. This is close to my house and I want to go back but the chairs! Hands  down the most uncomfortable restaurant chairs ever. I got home 40 mins ago and still have wire indents on my legs lol.

What a delightful experience! Andres and Alpheny were an attentive and professional team, and the atmosphere was just what I wanted for a Sunday brunch. We sat at the kitchen counter and were able to watch some of the cooks prepare dishes, which was a real treat. The cold brew was smooth and delicious, the green juice refreshing and crisp. And the food was just incredible. Everything was so fresh and expertly prepared, you could tell how much thought went into the execution of each dish. Well balanced and perfectly portioned, it was worth every last penny. Will definitely be back for dinner in the near future.

I have had consistently outstanding meals here. The service is excellent, it's beautiful inside, and it is truly one of the best restaurants I have ever visited. All four times I've gone for dinner, the food has been ~transcendent~ and I wish that were an exaggeration. I tend to eat more vegetarian than not but am not a strict vegetarian or vegan, and this place truly makes you forget to miss meat. Everything is so unbelievably flavorful. The lettuce cups are nothing like you'd expect- there are so many colors and flavors going on and somehow they work perfectly. The applewood smoked butter beans are so rich and creamy and the mushrooms are the perfect addition. The yams are probably one of my favorite dishes of all time- the tartness from the fruits and the coconut yogurt and the tandoori flavors and the crunchy garnish work so perfectly together. The carrots have made me feel things I have never felt about carrots or nut butter before and they have the perfect amount of spice- the lime is especially important. I recommend going here with people who really enjoy and appreciate food. It sounds ridiculous but every dish really feels like a work of art.

This review started with a one star because We were seated 15 minutes later than our reservation. No one was friendly and the hostess was a bit smug. Our waiter was in the weeds and seemed stressed. Place was LOUD LOUD LOUD!
The food was delicious and when things slowed down, the waiter became helpful and kind. Still, we were here a good two hours waiting on seating and food.

Dining in a carpet store turned out to be an incredible experience, as soon as we located the entrance. With scaffolding everywhere, it was a little hard to find.

Once inside, ABCV was even better than I expected, and my expectations were pretty high given raves from people whose endorsements I trusted. The decor is mostly white, which lends a sleek aesthetic. Service exceptionally friendly, with our server almost too enthusiastic about all the offerings. 

The dishes are individual works of art, reminding me of Vegetable in Studio City CA, one of the most memorable vegan restaurants I've tried. Unlike Vegetable, we were told that the chef would make adjustments if desired (we didn't). 

I don't typically take pictures of every morsel I consume, but the ABCV dishes were Insta-worthy, and tasted even better. The white yam was a favorite, but the cauliflower was pretty amazing too. Definitely go with a group -- there were four of us -- and get a bunch of dishes so you can sample a range of items. The gods only wish they'd had an ABCV on Mount Olympus.
So... I like this place and I use to be more of a four but the food just seemed okay this time. Maybe I wasn't feeling this season of the menu. Although the corn dumplings were delish!!

I'm not really a fan of vegan restaurants, but I knew I could trust J-G. I was very excited to try his new restaurant, and sure enough, we were thrilled. 

J-G's abcV embraces the ingredients rather than trying to transform them into something they are not (i.e. a veggie burger). Every dish was phenomenal, tasted fresh, and felt healthy to eat.

The decor and atmosphere of abcV are also wonderfully sophisticated, yet simple and classy. The cocktails were also excellent.

Highly recommended for trying "vegan" food. Definitely make a reservation!

Came here for a celebratory dinner on a Thursday night and I cannot give enough credit to the staff.  We were a party of 7 and they were more than accommodating (who knew how tough it was to find a vegan/vegetarian restaurant in the city who provided high chairs ), as well as attentive.  They took their time to go over the menu and made a couple of suggestions that did not disappoint.  Hen of the woods - you can (almost) mistake it for an actually poultry dish, was delicious and clever.  It's apparently made from a mushroom (I forgot the name) in limited quantities and shreds like chicken breast, was fried perfectly )for those who don't know how difficult it is to draw moisture out of mushrooms, it can be very difficult).  The smoked white beans and the spinach is a must as well.  Don't forget the beets either.

Dear Diary,
I am in food heaven. May I never need to squeeze myself into tight jeans again. Literally every item we ordered was supreme. And we ordered the entire menu. 
Amen.

Not vegan or vegetarian but visited with a friend who is.  Was skeptical going in but was pleasantly surprised.  All dishes were really good and incredibly fresh.  

Service was good overall but really really slow.  Overall a fan!
Great ambience, amazingly flavorful dishes will please any vegan foodie who needs lots of spices to their dishes.

abcV is truly an exceptional restaurant. Small plates to share with each one a carefully balanced mix of ingredients and seasonings. Both the vegan and omnivore members of our party were impressed. We tried many things. None of them disappointed. Dosa with smoky eggplant and  tomato chutney was very well received by all. The spicy tofu had a bit more kick that we prefer, but we ate every bit of it. The slow roasted beets are a real standout. Fantastic mix of flavors. Honestly, you can't go wrong here. We will definitely be back!

The head! It was the head!!!! Head of the cauliflower that is truly the star of the show! It had the right consistency, texture and taste that you can't help but devour it. 

My only irk is how noisy the place is. I don't think it has to do with the crowd I guess it's more of the acoustics of the place that we felt we had to speak loudly to understand our conversation. 

Love the food but would probably be back on down times to get a more peaceful ambiance.

Loved dinning here! Hands down the best vegan food I've ever had. But the host was really rude to us, she made us wait for like 45 minutes for a table, which was fine, but when we went back she said she'd sit us at the bar, and that we should wait for another 45 to get a table. She was not apologetic and gave us the nastiest attitude. The food was AMAZING THOUGH!

Loved loved this restaurant. Went from brunch with friends and everything was amazing. I had the pancakes and wasn't sure what to expect, but it was amazing! The dosas and any of green juices also worth a trip back. Desert was also fabulous!

I used to work for ABC Kitchen. And as such, I have a certain level of expectation from. John Georges restaurant. And this was not it....The menu appeared to be a melange of random ingredients forced to duke it out in your mouth. Case and point...the weird savory yogurt. Just go to ABCK

I know I am not a part of the cool NYC crowd that brunches, my review is based on all components of this brunch experience.  This place was a recommendation based on the fact that we are vegetarian and love to support restaurants with sustainably sourced food.

They are vegetarian so that is great. I am GF and there were some options for me so that is also good.

Service was good but the place was packed. It was very loud and we were 5 people placed at a table for 8 (possibly ten) so between the distance between people and the noise level, conversation was hard.

I ordered the GF pancakes (they were good but not great) - I tried other people's dishes and some were delicious and some were ok. All of our portions were very small.  I had a turmeric beverage that was fantastic (about $12 worth).  We spent over $250 and left hungry.

All in all, I am not a fan of the bougie brunch scene, but I understand that it is a "thing" in NYC.  I am going to recommend it for those who want that experience and ambiance but don't care if they feel satisfied after the meal or who just have really small appetites.

One of my favorite vegetarian restaurants! The avocado cups which always stay on the menu are delicious! We also ate the summer melon salad with pink sea salt and basil. The whole roasted cauliflower is also a classic and should not be passed up. I also tried the corn wontons which I would pass on, the flavor combinations just didn't astound my taste palette. For dessert, I had chocolate gnache with passionfruit which was a great combination! For the average foodie, I would recommend atleast 4 dishes to try to be satisfied for dinner. For a drink, I had the yuzu gin and tonic which was tasty and not overly sweet or fake tasting. However, the service was standard and the server could have been a little more attentive. In addition, when pouring the waters she spilled it onto my silverware and table. I didn't mind but something to consider because if it was wine, it could have stained something or my clothes. Not sure why this isn't a one Michelin star but It should be considered!

This is my go to restaurant for business and personal outings. Food is spectacular, service is great, and they are attentive to allergies and food sensitivities...makes eating out fun again. Thank you!

Total five star experience. Everything in this restaurant is beautiful, including the food. All of the dishes were so simple but the tastes were so complex and perfectly seasoned. I hiiiiighly recommend it for a special lunch or brunch. Can't wait to come back for dinner!

Was a bit underwhelmed by ABCV. I've heard good things and that the roasted cauliflower was the star of the show. Knowing this I made sure to order the cauliflower and I also got the mushroom walnut bolognese. The cauliflower to start was good but not great or excellent has it has been claimed to be. After speaking with others at the table who had previously dined at ABCV the explained "it isn't as good tonight." Disappointing how could something change so much night to night??? The bolognese was good. Tough pasta but loved the meat like consistency of the mushrooms and walnuts.

I'm not vegan but decided to try ABC V to see why people talk so much about it and I have to say I was pleasantly surprised. The baked cauliflower and the avocado hummus were outstanding! The pastas are great as well. The space itself is really noisy though and we could barely hear each other which is why I'm giving 4 stars.

Wow! It was our first time here and I am beyond flabbergasted by the ambiance and level of service we experienced. Our server, Sydney, truly elevated our experience with her knowledge and pizzazz. Thank you, Sydney! Is tomorrow too soon to come back?

Absolutely outstanding and innovative food and even non-alcoholic drinks for those of us who stay sober. But the decibel level is so great that it's painful to eat there. Conversation is not possible. Cruel to the servers who are damaging their eardrums. I cannot fathom why anyone would run a restaurant who's point is to do no harm to animals, but harm the people who eat there. I would never go back.

Fantastic food as the cauliflower is a must have. However, the service was slow and parts of our order never came even asking multiple times. So, expect subpar service for an excellent dining experience.

This was a very wonderful experience especially since I have been trying to get to ABCV restaurant for a while now. Started out with a cocktail thai julius which is a lemongrass infused tequila, cointreau, sea buckthorn, thai basil, galangal, whipped coconut. It was absolutely refreshing for a beautiful summer night. My honey opted for the pomegranate kombucha which he liked very much
For dinner we started with the avocado lettuce cups, toasted cumin, serrano and lime, pepitas. Really tasty with some amazing flavors. Then we ordered the saison battered maitaike and oyster mushrooms, black sesame, honey, za'atar, scallions. Right amount of crunch and tenderness. The pandan coconut sticky rice, lemongrass grilled fairy tale eggplant, peanut, thai basil was a great choice. This transported me to Bali. Reminded me of what I used to eat for breakfast. It could have done with a little less salt. The mushroom walnut bolognese, carrot paccheri, celery, mint leaf was so good. These dishes were great because they are served as a way to share. 
Now I do not usually order dessert but I am glad my honey suggested looking at the dessert menu. We ordered the chocolate cake. This was truly an amazing way to end the night. The cake had the right amount of everything. It was perfectly moist with not too much sugar. ABCV come take this W(Winner). Thanks for a really wonderful experience. Definitely recommend this place to all Vegans out there and even for those who just want a break from animal protein. The food was so good I didn't even get into the interior which is so beautiful. Can't wait to try out the breakfast and brunch options. The wait staff definitely know their stuff. They are accommodating and attentive.
Best vegan restaurant in New York, without a doubt. The whole experience is a delight. I keep going back and it's amazing every time.
Great vibe and delicious vegan food. Very accommodating with my food allergies. I always  love coming here when I'm in NYC.

Nope... not a cool place. 
A noisy environment, extremely small, overpriced portions, crummy service. 
I get what this place is trying to be and totally appreciate it, I even understand that this is the reason why many patrons are so generous with their five-star ratings, but everything has its limits. 
You can be environmentally friendly, source food locally and help the community, this is all quite commendable and should be celebrated. However, this place is still a restaurant, and with that comes responsibility, patrons should still be able to expect reasonably good service, and good value for what they are ordering. 
I am not holding my breath for ABCV to turn things around, after all, you have to wait quite a bit for a table, the place is always packed and people love this place.
It is apparent that this may be the classic case of ... it's me, not you.
Absolutely fun atmosphere !! Great, creative menu with absolutely delicious selections.  Desserts were fabulous as well  loved it !

So this was my first stab at a completely vegan restaurant in New York City and I am SO glad we picked this place last night. It's a bit pricey which is to be expected but the menu is full of creative options, and everything we had was full of flavor. We started with the sweet corn dumplings which were piping hot and just spicy enough, the avocado lettuce cups, the roasted cauliflower, and finished off with the vegan chocolate cake - one of the best slices of cake I have had in a very long time. Not to mention the white interior is gorgeous, and our waiter Masad was fantastic.

I had to take a star off for service at the door. Having a reservation for a table of two I find it very gauche that they would make me stand and wait when they don't really have a place in the front to stand and so little bar space. My friend arrived fashionably late like she does and we still had to wait 15 minutes because our 8:30 table wasn't ready until 8:50.

The food is great but the portion is small and expensive.  You can try it and not bad.  It is worthy to try.  The environment is great to sit and enjoy the dinner time. But have to order more food. Not enough.

I had wanted to come here forever and managed to make my first visit a lovely lunch with a friend for their birthday! 

We ordered quite a few plates to share and each dish was as delicious as it was beautiful. If you are vegan in NYC you definitely have to visit, but if you're not, it's even more important to give it a try. 

I am definitely one to go and support any tiny cafe or food truck that is selling tasty vegan food, but to really elevate the experience and to be able to celebrate with a fine dining menu that doesn't contain animal products.... that is a really powerful thing. 

Kudos to this wonderful place, and a special thank you for the happy birthday candle added onto dessert

Hey guys, am upset with this restaurant visited on 14 th sept 6:30 pm sat. I went for my hubby's birthday eve, I had called and reserved the table for 2 a week ago! And see wat happens. 1) I had asked them to give a less louder table, but they didn't. We reached before time and asked them we can wait but they made us sit in the location which was super noisy. 2) I had asked them to have candles around the desert we order and disappointment they didn't . It was easy if they would have told me that they can't I would have got it . 3) I ordered two items for the main course, Second one was salty, while we were eating the server asked us if everything was fine! I told them it's very salty ! He says that lemme find out from the kitchen and he never came back to us. Our desert was served and we went out of the restaurant ! I didn't wanna create mess on my husbands birthday eve. But this is wat I don't expect !!!  So I won't return back with this experience. Overall the taste is ok and portions are small. I have been to so many vegan places and they are much better than this.  So abcV where is ur hospitality, quality control, feedback review and solutions !!

Amazing. Who knew veggies could taste so good!

Must haves: roasted cauliflower, chicken of the woods, and dosa with eggplant. 

Makes me want to try to make more vegetarian dishes at home. We left stuffed and very satisfied! We were recommended 4-6 dishes between the two of us, but honestly we would've been full with the whole roasted cauliflower + 2 other dishes. So so good.

Everything was delicious! I came here for a business breakfast. Loved the atmosphere and I had a lovely almond latte. I also had a coconut yogurt dish which was incredibly good. I'm not vegan, but there are plenty of healthy options. The decor is really wonderful and a nice place to be in.

The food was exceptional.  We had the roasted beets, the chicken of the woods, the casarecce, the applewood smoked butter beans, and the eggplant dosa.  The cocktails were fun. 

Our server was helpful in navigating the menu and answered all of our questions.  There are a few steps of service that should have received more attention such as clearing plates and filling empty water glasses.  We were also seated without being offered a drink menu. That being said, these points were not deal breakers but they would have made the night more enjoyable and are usually present at this price point. 

All in all, a good experience.

I'm not a Vegan but this place is phenomenal.  We had butternut squash, mushrooms, hummus....yummmm!!  The ambience is beautiful although the waitress was a little pushy with upsale.  I look forward to returning!

ABCV was a pleasant surprise. This was my first time going to a all vegetarian restaurant and it did not disappoint. Starting with the service, the experience was excellent. Our waitress was bubbly, kind, and knowledgeable. The food was very flavorful as well. My favorite item has to have been the eggplant dosa dish. It was so authentic but at the same time unique. I probably could have done without the walnut bolognese-the texture was a little strange with chunks of walnut in the sauce. The cocktails were fantastic and so unique. The menu also included non alcoholic drinks that were fun and unique such as a rose water soda. Would go back and recommend to vegetarians and non vegetarians!

Came here with a group of friends and we were seated immediately with great service. Phyllicia is such a great waitress-- she was so sweet and explained everything on the menu to us! She and the other waitresses were really attentive. The cocktails are great and we loved the food!

One of the best restaurants ever. Dishes are unique but the chef does not try to pose the vegetables as meat based dishes (ex: you won't find beet infused tofu that tastes like salmon here) which is something I appreciate. Veggies are beautiful the way they are and they don't have to be transformed into hotdogs, burgers or shnitzels to be appreciated. Everything tastes fresh and light. Avocado wraps, crepe and the bean hummus are my favorites. Their non alcoholic drinks are quite memorable too. Oh and the service was splendid. Had the sweetest waitress (had a lot of beauty marks on her face)

Updating with some more dishes:

Banana pancakes: were only ok 

Coconut sticky rice with veggie slaw: holy cow, this is up there with my favorite dish of the avocado lettuce cups. Warm and hearty and lemongrassy and creamy and soft rice underneath citrusy and spicy and fresh assorted vegetables with mint and lemongrass and nuts and shaved coconut and toasted garlic - truly a wow dish

Wow! Did not think vegetarian dishes can be this good! 

My friend and I went for brunch and had the pancake salad and tofu cauliflower with a protein smoothie and the green juice. Everything tasted fantastic. The pancake smelt really good, puffy, warm on a savory/salty side, go perfectly with the yogurt, and salad/avocado. I added a poached egg on the tofu dish - the flavor of the dish is incredible, just right amount of savory but not too strong, with fresh handmade tofu and fresh veggies. It was very appetizing, same as the drinks. Will definitely come back to try other dishes on the menu!

Found hard plastic in my beet carpaccio (seen at the back - probably came off a clamshell packaging or some sort). My mouth bled from this - Saturday the 5th of october. Manager came afterwards to say sorry and to offer other dishes that would be on the house, but we were already full at that point. They took the beet carpaccio off the check, of course. But no remarks on how this happened/ what would be done to prevent this in the future. Please be careful, could be very very dangerous if swallowed.

Food and bar seating service was great otherwise.

I live in the neighborhood and have frequented abc's family of restaurants for years now. Unfortunately, the service at abcV has become extremely poor. A few weeks ago I went for brunch. It was busy and I put my name on the list. Her estimate was 15 minutes, but I understand that things can take more time. After about 30 minutes of waiting, I noticed an empty table outside and the host said we could have it as soon as it was set. I then proceeded to wait an additional THIRTY MINUTES for them to get the table set. I don't know if it was incompetence or whether they were intentionally trying to make me wait but it was absolutely unacceptable.

I sent an email to customer service at Jean Georges restaurant group to tell them about my experience and NEVER heard back. Extremely disappointing.

ABCV is a venture from acclaimed chef of Jean-Georges, with a vegetarian/healthy leaning. My friend and I had previously made reservations here for a brunch, but they kept us waiting when we came in even though we were on time for our reservation, and didn't offer an apology. 
Ambience is very pretty, clean, and modern. It looked like it was 
The menu is entirely plant-based, with lots of interesting options. My friend went with the dosa, and I went with the sweet potato. The dosa was not bad, and my friend ate it in entirety, though remarked that it wasn't amazing. 
The sweet potato tasted like it had been very simply and plainly roasted, with a heap of salad dumped on top. I had to keep reaching for the salt to make it appeal more to my tastebuds.
The servers here all have an annoying, new age way of calling customers "friends", ie. "Friends, are we ready to order?" I found the whole thing very unusual. 
Overall, not a great experience here.
Great service and delicious pancakes. Dark inside for brunch and very small portions. The pancakes were not very filling and did not have much fruit on top. Would go back to try more options though

this place has a special place in my heart since my boyfriend and I spent our anniversary here  and it means so much that I can spend high quality food with high quality people! We ordered the eggplant dosa, mushrooms, rice, and ofc the head of cauliflower!! With a side of wine & their elixirs! These dishes were made to perfection, elevated the flavors of vegetables, and was worth every penny!

Perfect brunch spot - hip, white, clean and innovative.  Great drinks and healthy innovative dishes from bowls to benedict. The wild mushroom and poached eggs were light and hearty in an earthy farm to table way.  Egg sambal cheddar dosas and mimosas anyone?

A friend took me here for a birthday dinner. I am a steak and bacon type of gal and I have to say I really enjoyed the food and cocktails here. The ambiance is nice and the staff were warm, friendly and very accommodating to my friend's special diet and allergies. I felt great when I left this place - none of the heaviness I feel after indulging myself with a rare steak or mushroom cream sauce laden sweetbread. The eggplant dosa was yummy. I would definitely come back to try their other offerings. Thumbs up to the cocktail

Like this place for its creativity and interior design. 

I loved the green hummus, and the beet root dish. The black sesame mushroom with honey was also good. 

Cauliflower is overhyped- it's only seasoned at the top and I feel like this could be made at home easily. It is also really expensive. 

Don't order the matcha green-brûlée. It is very bitter.

I found this restaurant exquisite.  The staff was exceptional.  Zach the maître d was attentive.  The food was out of this world. We were a party of 7 and everyone of us was extremely happy with our food. We had many shared foods as well- those fingerling potatoes were to die for.  The ambiance was industrial chic.  Very comfortable. Amazing food.

I LOVE the food - I hate the restaurant!

Seriously.  I've had two outrageously good meals at ABCV (although I, for one, think the cauliflower is way, way over-rated) but at the end of the day I simply won't go back.  The reason?  It's like eating in a freakin' high school cafeteria: everyone is seated at long communal tables, there's nothing but hard surfaces in all three dimensions and the result is simply the most deafening environment I've ever experienced.  The server and I were screaming at each other just to place the order.  I had to shout at my dinner companion - I probably heard more conversation from the two strangers seated at my right and at my left than from my companion!  By the end of the meal I couldn't get out fast enough.  Oh, the food was great - the maitake mushrooms, the smoked butter beans, the unbelievable wontons, all of it were fabulous - but without headphones I'd never go back.

At first I was hesitant to join my friends at ABCV, as I like my meat and fish. I was completely wrong. Their food is exquisite and the taste combinations are phenomenal. The menu is a bit on the pricier side but even that has not stopped me from going back several times. really worth a visit.

ABCV is one of my favourite restaurants. Very consistent, and the service is always really friendly. The vibe is very cute, I would say good for a date, except that I find it a little noisy at times.

This time, we had the crisp radishes, which were incredible. The wok seared turnips were also good with a kick at the end (but not too spicy). The best dish in my opinion was the applewood smoked butter beans, which had a delicious creamy sauce. The potato truffle, the special for the night, was good but I probably wouldn't have gotten it again (it was $60 and I didn't think it was very special). Finally, we also had the dosa with yogurt, avocado, and sprouts. They gave a generous portion of yogurt and avocado (greatly appreciated). Overall, 5 dishes was just the right amount of food for the two of us.

I think the food was definitely above average and ambiance was nice. I reserve 5 stars for meals that really wow me, which this came close to but not quite. I would give 4.5 stars if I could!

Definitely worth it to check out, especially if you're vegan or vegetarian.

This is a 5 star worthy restaurant even considering it's a vegetarian/vegan-only one. Came with a group of 5 for a bday celebration. 

Interior and decor is really nice. Trendy, boho-chic vibe. 

Food is, for the most part, excellent. 
The menu changes seasonally so some of these items may not be available still.

Top items:
- Beluga Lentils with chili oil and black vinegar, yams, broccoli stems, cilantro. I wouldn't normally order this because how good can lentils be? Well I was so wrong. Incredible flavor in this dish. Just trust me on this.
- Dosa with smoky eggplant, tomato chutney, coconut yogurt, cilantro. The flavor of the eggplant combined with the tomato was really intense. It also just melted in my mouth. Get this dish. 

Other notable items:
- Half or Whole Roasted Cauliflower with turmeric-tahini and pistachios. If you don't like cauliflower, you probably won't like this dish. It's just doused in oil and roasted. But it's really pretty and acts as a good centerpiece for the table. For all you insta-h**s out there.
- Mushroom walnut bolognese with carrot paccheri, celery, mint leaf. Recommend for the meat lovers who were dragged to this restaurant.
- Green Chickpea Hummus with thai basil, fresh pita or crudité. Great starter dish. The hummus itself is great - tastes like vegetables (in a good way)

Drinks: I didn't order any of them, but I tried my friend's and it was just okay. She didn't even finish it. So not worth the price in my opinion.

The service was... interesting. Our server was attentive but pushy. He kept on saying we should order more food and recommended some dishes kinda forcefully. To the point where we were getting uncomfortable. We also had an outside cake delivered to the restaurant that was supposed to come out as a surprise. But they forgot about it or something and we had to ask the server to bring out the cake in front of the bday girl, which defeats the purpose. Oh well. 

I'd still make a repeat visit if I'm back in the city. It's pricey, but the food is surprisingly filling and definitely delicious.

Listen you certainly do not have to be a vegetarian or vegan to love this place. 

It's almost wizardry because the menu to me isn't super appealing but the final product is.

The recommendation from our server was 4-6 dishes for 2 people and we shared 4 + 1 dessert and that was plenty.

We tried...

1. Avocado Lettuce Cups $16 (2 to an order)
Sounds and looks super simple but it was insanely good, complex & I can understand why people order multiple of these.

2. Half Roasted Cauliflower $16
Our least favorite because I feel like I could technically make a variation of this at home 

3. Pine Nut Lemon Spaghetti $26
The most filling of dishes, creamy (without cream for you lactose intolerant peeps) and the stand out dish is the night 

4. Dosa: Smokey Eggplant $20
Basically a wrap made from rice batter, with eggplant inside with a tomato chutney, coconut yogurt and cilantro sauce. Yum

5. Dessert: Carrot Soft Serve $16
Bits of carrot cake, black sugar syrup with rum raisin & candies ginger. Outstanding & taste like a carrot cake in liquid from. Pretty large & so filling we didn't finish it shockingly.

From the decor to food to lovely service, this place is easily one of my favorite restaurants and I'll be returning to (over ABC Kitchen too:)

I'd rate abcV 4.5 stars. This is a Jean-Georges establishment. Elevated vegetarian/plant based restaurant.

The restaurant is beautiful in a trendy-modern-chic-clean kind of way. A little pretentious but beautiful nonetheless. The menu is designed to be served tapas style which is generally my favorite way to eat.
The food is very creative, flavorful, and meticulously prepared. They do a good job of actually highlighting vegetables and non meat options for what they are, instead of trying to turn them into meat substitutes. Dishes were beautifully presented, dainty, and expensive.
Our server was flawless. They also have an open kitchen. Like others have pointed out, we did have to wait a bit to be seated despite being on time for our reservation.

Also, I have to say, this was one of the more accommodating experiences I've had at a restaurant. Everything we ordered had to be vegan AND nut-free and they were able to make adjustments without any hesitation or sign of annoyance. To clarify, the menu is vegetarian not vegan, although most dishes are vegan or can be made vegan.

Now would I come back? Probably not. I was starving about an hour later. I eat meat, but not everyday so yes I am capable of feeling satisfied with a vegetarian/vegan meal. I wish there were more protein options.
I would recommend to others looking for a sophisticated, trendy, plant based dining experience.

Love this place! Got the potatoes, mushrooms with poached eggs and dosa with yogurt and avocado. Really liked the vibe of this place. Came here on a gloomy rainy day and the brightness of this place, improved my mood and day for sure. Dosa was a little hard, can use some crunch and coffee was a little cold. I hope this feedback reaches the right people, will definitely come back

A friend of mine recommended this place and I was so happy here  !  The food was amazing and the service and ambience was great. 
I had the Dosa and the lentils and both dishes were very flavorful and the portions were perfect too. 
10 stars

Not a vegetarian buy my son dragged me here. What a surprise to discover such an array of flavors from veggies. Never imagined it could taste so good. Ordered tapas style, liked everything. Service was professional, helpful, and friendly.

We had such a great dinner here- only 1 of the 4 of us is vegan, but we were all eager to try everything. Highlights were the hummus and the smoked eggplant dosa. Also fun was the spicy radish starter, the cauliflower, mushroom bolognese, the special (cacio e pepe with black truffles), and applewood smoked beans. Chocolate cake and soft serve carrot cake desserts were both great, especially the latter. Nothing was mediocre. Just amazing.

Delish tapas-style veggie treats. Having eaten at the other ABC locations, having one that caters strictly to the veggies was a no-brainer

I'd had my heart set in the cauliflower but we were advised they'd just welcomed truffle season, we diverted 

Let's just say truffle & lemon are not a good combination- both the potatoes & pasta dishes they'd loaded up with shaved truffle were completely offset by the lemon. It was a weird flavor clash that I would not repeat

Desserts were a winner & their cocktails rocked so still have to say we're fans & still looking for the cauliflower- next time!
This is a place where you treat yourself! You need to order at least 4 dishes here to get the full experience & unique amazing flavorful dishes. Everything tastes extremely fresh and clean!
A unique ambience with great tasting food and wonderful service. My favorite was the beet salad and the chocolate cake is also worth trying.

I would give this restaurant a 4 but I'm giving it 1 less star for making us wait 40 minutes even though we had a reservation. It's pretty ironic that they can cancel the reservation on you if you're 15 minutes late, but they can make you wait for 40 minutes without any explanation. 

In order to make up for the wait, they gave us 2 apps on the house, which was appreciated and very good. The first was green chickpea hummus which was one of the best dishes we had that day.  It had plenty of flavor and was very creamy. Additionally, they gave us avocado toast which was also very good. You needed to squeeze a bit of lime on top because without it, it was pretty bland. 

I got the mushroom and egg dish (substituted poached eggs with scrambled eggs) and really enjoyed it. Everything was very flavorful and the eggs were perfectly cooked. We also shared the fingerling potatoes which I would recommend. 

I did taste the coconut sticky rice dish and lentil dish and didn't really enjoy either of those, but my table liked them. 

I wouldn't rush to come back especially if the restaurant would make me wait again for 40 minutes even when having a reservation.

I went with a friend and we split 5 different plates - avocado lettuce cups, roasted cauliflower, the applewood butter smoked beans, wontons; and matcha creme brûlée for dessert. Wontons were my absolute favorite- they're fried crispy and with this creamy cilantro sauce and apples. It was all absolutely amazing. Although it's pretty expensive, it's certainly worth it. Would recommend to anyone, not just vegetarians. And I'd definitely go back to try their other dishes.

Omg!!! Every single bit was absolutely incredible I loved loved this restaurant. It also helped that it is beautiful inside. The service  is impeccable down to the runners and bussers. Felicia was our waitresses and just how she describes the food gets you excited to eat. She describes it with such passion and really enhances the entire experience. You can tell that she loves working there including the food. She offers great suggestions and really takes  care of you. You will completely feel pampered. My friend and I shared a 5 plates and we were completely stuffed. We could have had 4. The fig martini is so delicious and not very sweet which  I appreciated. We had the  Pine Nut Lemon spaghetti. Wok seared turnip rice cakes, pine nut and lemon harissa, beluga lentils, green chickpea hummus and risotto with fresh truffles. Every bite made my tastebuds tingle. There is so much more that I want to try there. They even had a small treat to celebrate my birthday. Thank you so much for
Making my birthday perfect. I will be back.

A modern take on breakfast/brunch. I love how health conscious this menu is. The ingredients are seasonal.
I enjoyed a chai tea in a cute clay mug.
Perfect for a brunch date!

I really love it here.  It's close to 5 stars, but I'm knocking it down because I often find the staff to be a bit pretentious and aloof, and I find the decor to be a little sterile.  However, those points don't stop me from coming back frequently, for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.  The food is delicious, creative, and nourishing, and there are always new additions and specials.  It's a great spot for many different occasions, and the central location helps as well.  The abc group continues to come out with hits, and I keep frequenting them!

I am obsessed with the food here. Truly amazing. Literally every dish is perfect.

The only issue is that the service is quite bad relative to the food quality. The service is actually so bad I find it funny and not even annoying. It's quite entertaining. Without fail, every time I go, the waiters seem to not want to discuss menu options beyond what's printed on the menu and servers take away dishes before I'm finished. They also clean the table as I'm still eating and seem to pop by at the most awkward moments. Giving this place five stars because of the food only.

An elevated take on vegetarian food. Definitely one of those places where you want to share with the table. 

We ordered about 7 dishes, with the two favorites being the pine nut and lemon spaghetti and the beans.

Overall giving 4 stars because, while the food is good and well crafted, it's hard to justify the price tag.

My favorite breakfast place on earth. And the most expensive. Healthy options with weird ingredients, and a variety of fresh juices and tonics. Minimalist, beautiful aesthetic of ambiance and service. Wish I could come more often.
Disappointing, especially for the price. Only go for the vibe and cute rose on table. Order the saison battered maitake and leave. Waiters were nice but food was not worth it.
Went here last night with 7 other friends. Everything we ordered was amazing & the service was also great. Really enjoyed the green hummus & the bartender in the front was super awesome.

I have been wanting to try ABCV for a while, but just now made it in. Not a vegetarian, but always looking for new and interesting ways to eat veggies and thought this was a great option. 

First off, the space is so pretty - very clean and minimal, but with those classic ABC touches - elegant dishware, pretty little wildflowers on the tables and dim lighting. We were there on a Friday night and it was crowded but not packed. 

Our waiter suggested that for the two of us we should order 4-6 dishes, but we felt like that was overkill and decided to start out with just three with a plan to order more if we needed - beets, cauliflower and the saison batter mushrooms. The beets were amazing - loved the addition of the pickle/capers and the smooth avocado in the middle. I'm a beet lover, but these were exceptional. The cauliflower I've seen all over instagram so had to try. The red harissa sauce is amazing with the tahini sauce they put on the cauliflower. Beautifully crispy. The battered mushrooms were the only thing I wasn't totally loving. They were heavier than I imagine they would be, a thicker coating of breading that was somewhat sweet/honey. The lime really lifts the dish and takes out a lot of the heaviness, but I don't think I would order it again. 

In terms of dishes, we were full after the three we had - even left a few of the mushrooms on the table. I didn't come into it starving, but 6 dishes would have been way too much. The total was around $75, which split two ways was a reasonable price for dinner. 

Our server was a little sassy with us - it started when we didn't order drinks and then only 3 dishes of food. We had to ask for an extra side of sauce twice and it definitely felt like we were being given a lower level of service because we were spending a bunch. Despite that, I'd return to ABCV again to try a few more dishes - the menu had so many good things I wanted to try!

This place had a really clean classy modern feel and we really enjoyed eating here. The meals were really tasty and we enjoyed everything we ordered a lot, however it didn't feel like it was worth the really high prices to us. I love vegetarian and vegan food so this is right up my alley but it's also hard to overpay a ton for vegetables that you know were probably not that expensive at the market.

Scammed At Xmas Dinner

I have been to ABCV multiple times and have always had a great  experience. My vegan friends from Philadelphia were excited when I told them we would be going there for Xmas Dinner since we had not be able to make a reservation with them before. What a disaster! I knew the Prix Fixe was $98 per person and thought it would be a very special and memorable meal. The service was extremely slow. Snails walk faster. The waiter refused to tell us anything about a single dish, other than we could pick 2 small plates and 1 dessert. After 2 hours we had all had our 2 small dishes and wondered why the dessert (pick one of 3) was taking 30 minutes to get. 

When I went home I looked up the lettuce leaves with avocado and pepitas on the standard dinner menu which is $16. The beluga lentils (not caviar) is $18 and throw in the standard dessert of $14 and you have a $48 dinner for $98. My former friends were stunned since they had promised to pay the bill for 6 which turned out to be nearly $1000!  We all left hungry and ripped off.

ABCv stands out from the ABC restaurants for its delicious and unique vegetable based dishes. They really take care with the dishes - beautiful presentations, interesting flavor combinations and overall delicious options. We ordered the whole cauliflower, slow roasted beets, and saison battered mushrooms. The whole cauliflower lived up to its reputation - it was the perfect consistency and tasted as if we were eating the creamiest butter. It was complimented by spicy sauces that cut the flavor as well as pomegranate seeds. The slow roasted beets were also exceptional, complimented by pickles, Dijon, and avocado purée. The flavor combination was unexpected, but surprisingly tasty. The saison bartered mushrooms were the only disappointment, I don't think we knew exactly what to expect and it seems the fried part of the dish overpowered the other flavors. The black sesame honey sauce was delicious but flavor was lost in the largely fried dish.

The restaurant has a subdued and sophisticated vibe. The attentive waiters, lovely atmosphere and delicious food make for a tasty and enjoyable dinner. I'll definitely be back to try the many other appealing dishes!

This restaurant has a beautiful ambience-- very  simplistic and elegant. It's great for a date, meeting a friend or a group of people. We ordered two entrees and a small dish to share which I thought was enough food. The portions are a good size and the food was full of flavor and texture. Drinks were a bit overpriced and I didn't find them particularly unique but the food made up for that. I would definitely come back and try other dishes as the menu changes.

ABCv elevates vegetable-based dishes really well, but it's also the loudest restaurant I've ever been to. I don't really remember if music was playing or not, but voices just carry in this space like no other. My partner and I were seated in the back section of the restaurant for our dinner, basically as far away from the much more crowded bar area as possible, but we literally needed to shout to communicate with each other. Instead of shouting, we opted to decide to communicate through facial expressions and the occasional text message as needed to facilitate answering questions like "do we want more food" and "who should pay."

If extreme noise levels don't bother you, the food is really excellent and satisfying. It's pricey, but that was to be expected. The deceptively simple carrots with nut and seed butter was among the most savory, delightful vegetable-forward dishes I've ever had, and the cauliflower lived up to the hype. We ordered a few other dishes, too, to round out the meal, and all of them were delicious.

I'm in love!!!! The avocado lettuce cups were literally to die for. The golden milk I mean wowwww it was one of the richest non dairy drinks I've ever had and is perfect on a chilly day! My friend had the egg plant dosa and described it as smokey, filling and full of flavor (I tasted a piece and I have to agree). It was a combination of creamy and crispy. While I had applewood butter beans and honestly each bite was a flavorful journey of its on. I can't wait to come back and try more food on the menu. This was one of the most refreshing, fulfilling and transformative dining experiences I've had in a while. 10/10 would recommend.

Best vegetarian-oriented restaurant in the city, by far, and one of the best overall.  Chickpea hummus is amazing.  Avocado dosa is also great, as are the carrots in nut butter.  Tofu dish I would not recommend, but their various rotating new dishes (like the recent potato one) are often revelations.  Desserts are also great.  Room is a little bright (especially compared to ABC Kitchen next door), but is still a nice space overall.  Highly recommended.

A fantastic dining experience. This place has it all. Glam, aesthetic and beyond delicious food. Youu literally cannot go wrong with *anything* you order. It will all be beyond superb. Great options for vegetarianss, vegans and meat eaters alike. Everyone will enjoy! Perfect for a date night, group or catching up with an old friend. Run, don't walk!

Came with a big party for the prefix menu, the hummus was one of my favorite.  The apps in the beginning were pretty good, and then it just went down hill from there. I enjoy the Avocado wrap, and the mushroom dish was okay.  The pasta dishes were not very good tho.

In brief: worth a one time visit  but not as a regular 

Ambiance was perfect with dusty rose and florals throughout the dIninng room. The service also felt friendly and easy, like at your favorite diner

We shared three things between two people:
The coconut yoghurt was too tart, not enough granola, overly citrusy.  It was nice as a garnish to our other mains but I'd have been pissed if it had been my main.
The dosa with Sambal and cheddar was pretty good but not as crisp as a dosa in a South Indian restaurant.  The decision to add cheese dragged down the texture of the crepe.  However flavors were good.
The mushrooms and eggs were savory and delicious, eggs poached to a perfect consistency.
Our coffee and latte were $7 each but tasted dinerish.
Bill for two people was $77.

It was a great place to check out but I wouldn''t come here again.

Extremely rude hostesses. Always a shocker given that the food is good and servers are usually well versed and friendly. I told myself I would not return after the last experience with a nasty hostess, but this time a friend chose the restaurant. I can confIdently say they lost a loyal customer to rude front staff. A shame.

This was the most predictable of the places.   We tried all the instagram-able favs and a few new items.   Nothing was disappointing...in fact everything was amazing!   Atmosphere is chic and the service was superior!  Also the drink menu both alcoholic and non is a must try.

Warning: this place is expensive. Three dishes got me to almost $90. It also gets very loud, but it has a fun vibe.

That said, if you're willing to splurge, I loved it. ABCV has kind of a confusing location and at first I walked into the sister ABC restaurant (which doesn't share the same menu). A quick walk through the restaurant gets you to ABCV.

I had three things, and they were excellent:

1. Pine nut & lemon - this was a hummus style dish, but that's an understatement. It was a very good/unique/flavorful combination.
2. Crispy delicata wontons - I loved these. By far my favorite dish. Light and flavorful. Unique from similar foods I've had.
3. Mushroom walnut bolognese - I actually made a version of this dish recently for myself so wanted to compare a restaurant version. I really liked it, but this would be better to share among two people as it started to get boring by the time I had finished.

Came here for a super belated birthday dinner and I chose this place because I really do want to be more conscious of animal consumption. 

Why torture and slaughter animals when you can eat plants?

The place is a bit cramped, so you're sitting on top of each other and once this place gets crowded, you can barely hear each other.

Our waitress was named Felicia and she had a pleasant and calming demeanor.  She recommended a couple of drinks for me, but I decided to go with the Blackcurrant & Tonic - very good and super refreshing. I would definitely add either vodka or tequila next time that I am here.
E got the cranberry punch - he liked it enough that he ordered another one.

Let me give you the run down of each dish that I tried:

Green Chickpea Hummus - very good and well balanced.

Avocado Lettuce Cups - really enjoyed this dish. The winter squash was cooked to perfection and it was super yummy.

Honeynut squash - I wanted to get the mushroom dish since Felicia recommended them, but after E loving the taste of squash, E wanted more and we ended up getting this dish instead. But this was another spread-like dish, so not exactly the same texture that E wanted. I thought this was just okay. I really wish we had the mushroom dish instead, since we just had the hummus and the hummus is still sitting at our table.

Sticky Rice - I love sticky rice and though Felicia recommended this to eat alongside with the mushroom, I still got it, just because I was curious how it would taste with the pandan infused coconut cream. I really wish this came with some mango - my favourite type of dessert!

Roasted Cauliflower - we got their well-known dish and I have to say, I was a bit disappointed. I had high hopes, since people rave about this one dish alone and it didn't meet my expectations. I felt the cauliflower itself was a bit overdone. It's too soft. Why does it have to be that soft? If they could just work on this texture, I would have loved this dish, because I am a zhug dipping fan!

Applewood smoked butter beans - who would have thought I would love beans so much. This dish was really good and especially paired with their in-house hot sauce. Delicious.

Cacio e Pepe - this was their special of the night and got this dish and my first bite was a bit salty from the vegetarian cheese, but later on, this dish tasted more balance.

Rice Pudding Ice Cream with Caramel Apple Tart - I wanted to get the passionfruit soft serve, since I have a deep obsession for passionfruit, but E is not into ice cream, so we went with this tart. I thought this was okay, since I would have preferred a tart without the caramel and the rice pudding ice cream didn't do anything for me.

Overall, my favourite dishes were the avocado cups, butter beans, hummus and the cacio e pepe.

I definitely would come back to try the mushroom and the beets.

Awful service. 

We sit down at our table for two birthdays and everything starts off great. Then the waiter comes over and asks for what we would like to drink. We say "please, start with the ladies first, " and the waiter has the nerve to tell us that he prefers to go in order--showing us that he's already irritated. 
This is just one example of a constant attitude we received from the waiter. I will not be eating here again if they continue to hire people like this. It's not worth the headache for over-priced lettuce.

The food was delicious but outrageously priced: count $25 on average for a plate, and you'll need 6 to feed 2 people. 
The staff was lovely too. 
I wouldn't go back and wouldn't recommend it simply due to the prices applied... But then again, it's the flatiron district.

Most of the dishes we ordered were good, but the fettuccini was very disappointing. It was loaded with black pepper and way too much truffle. It probably had the same amount if not more truffle than pasta and the taste was not good. Then when we got the check it was even more disappointing as it was a special they tell you table side and turned out to be $45. NOT WORTH. ugh it just changed the taste of the rest of the meal. Had to eat something else to get the taste out of our mouths. Just have to put it out there so others can avoid it.

My favorite vegetarian restaurant, hands down. Everything and I mean, EVERYTHING, is perfect about Abcv. Two words to describe the place is - fine balance. 

It is the fine balance when it comes to the ambience, the service and food. 

The atmosphere is so clean, so chic, and so warm. I love how easy, functional and elegant this place is without overdoing it.

The service is the same as the atmosphere. The servers are knowledgeable about the menu, have great suggestions and positively helpful. Nothing is too much or too little, it's just right. 

The food is absolutely delicious, simple and the flavors of the ingredients shine. I love their turmeric elixir (drink) and their lettuce wraps. You must get these 2 menu items if you don't get anything else! You must! There is something for everyone and all will be great choices. 

Abcv is a very instagram-able restaurant with great food. Often times those two don't go hand in hand but Abcv is the best mix of the two. 

Go on, try this restaurant and you won't be disappointed. Guaranteed.

Trendy plant-based restaurant with a fair amount of vegan options. Lots of natural, whole foods and essentially no processed ingredients in their dishes. Servings are pretty small, so would recommend ordering several dishes to share among a group of people.

2 words: beluga lentils.

Never knew belugas could taste so good. Also love the sticky coconut rice. Juices were pricey and mehhh. But those belugas... mMmm

Everything we tried here was fantastic so it's hard to recommend dishes. I've no idea where they get phenominally tasty strawberries in February. It's expensive (around $100 a head with one drink and a tip) and well worth it.

Would be nicer if they waited for us to finish dessert before bringing the check. Other than that the service was great too.

Was not a vegetarian the first time I came here at my friend Joey Repice recommendation. I left a fan and with a whole new attitude about vegeterian food. I have come back several times and have not been disappointed. The chick pea hummus is a great way to start the meal followed by the whole cauliflower. The sides and sauces bring out the best in the dishes. The Ragu Bolognese is one of the best pasta dishes I have ever had and no meat in the sauce whatsoever.  

I will keep coming back.... as well as now being meatless. 

I would recommend this to anyone who believes they could not be a vegetarian. 

Made a believer out of me.

ABC versions never disappoint. The refreshing combination of food ingredients resulting in a dish which comes as a surprise if your imagination is limited to the description on the menu is the speciality of ABC and ABCV is no different. Amazing food!

Imagine a very plausible scene where the Indian food purists of the world  protest outside a restaurant incessantly chanting "Down with the Frenchman. He's ruining our food." For the NYC/London Desi crowd they mostly avoid this place citing the lamentable -- "Fake", "Wannabe", "Confused". 

That type of rubbish gets me fired up since I had nothing but the most elevated experience here last week. Jean-Georges is an astounding chef along with being smart enough to understand where he may need a local resident expert to fill in the gaps. Since abcV dishes up a mean dosa, he definitely assembled some superstars in the kitchen! For dosas especially it's all about the lentil batter fermentation. And wow was it spot on! I ordered sweet potato dosa and even those sweet potatoes had been given the authentic masala treatment without overpowering the dosa pancake itself. Then those chutneys...! Even the lettuce cups I was recommended to start with were out of this world!

This review is for a visit from a while ago. The service was very poor. They made me wait 30 min for a table even though I had a reservation and the restaurant was half empty. The hostess did not acknowledge me even as I stood in front of her. The food was hit or miss, and overall salty. ABC Kitchen and ABC Cocina have much better service and vegetarian food; it's a shame this ABC location is managed so poorly.
Consistently amazing every time! Highly recommend checking out their outdoor dinning with the hybrid menu from both ABC restaurants.

Brought two non-vegetarians here and they're still talking about how incredible the food was two days later.  Everything we had was delicious. I can't wait to come back and have everything I had again and also try more. Wonderful restaurant period - but also one of the best vegetarian restaurants I've been to in my life.

I was so excited to try this restaurant when I moved here from Philly because Jean-Georges just opened up an amazing restaurant in Philly recently. We initially made reservations at ABCV, but were a little confused when we got there because we didn't realize they combined this with ABC, so the menu was not all vegetarian. I'm assuming they combined the restaurants because of Covid. They still had many veggie options, so it was a pleasant experience. To start we got the snap pea hummus which came with veggies and a small pita bread. The cauliflower was so good! I'm sometimes hesitant of ordering a whole head of cauliflower because the inside is sometimes undercooked but this one was thoroughly cooked and the flavors of the sauces were in each bite! My main entree was the vegan walnut bolognese pasta. I've never tried real bolognese so I can't make that comparison, but the pasta here was packed with flavors I've never had before! The pasta was also cooked al dente. We ended with a strawberry shortcake dessert, which was a little dry and I would try a different dessert next time.

Due to COVID, ABCV is combined with its sibling restaurants ABCcocina & ABCkitchen. The menu is interesting and quite varied. 
For cocktails we tried to peach milk punch & ginger margarita. Both were absolutely amazing. 10/10. Probably the best part of the meal. The actual "meal" had its middling highs & lows. 
The $20 guac was underwhelming. The tortilla chips were the best part of it. 
The sweet corn empanadas were my personal favorite part of the meal. The flavor, texture--perfect. The lime sauce served on the side was unforgettable. 
The truffle pizza was pretty good. I enjoyed it, but I wasn't wowed. The truffle flavor was definitely present there though, which you don't get often. Dough was cooked perfectly too. 
The roast cauliflower was... interesting. My boyfriend loved it but I just wasn't impressed. The texture was undercooked, the flavors were off, and the tomato "sauce" on the side was offensively strong for me. But he thought it was amazing and complex, so that may be a personal opinion. 
We didn't feel compelled to stay for dessert. Overall it was kind of a let down. I got a peak at the inside when I used their restroom and it was stunning. I think eating inside would have enhanced the experience.

I am a big fan of the tranquil, bordering-on-sterile (in a good way!) ambiance of this restaurant. I get the sense this decor is meant to embody the purity of vegetarianism, which is a little tacky as a concept, but all that's to say I found the environs pleasant.

For drinks, I had the fig vodka cocktail, which was delightful - deeply infused with the sweetness of figs, as I had hoped.

We shared 7 small plates in the total, with my personal favorites being the amazing harissa turmeric cauliflower - the best whole cauliflower dish I've had anywhere to date. The veggie burger and fries were also fantastic, and I loved the deeply smoky flavor of the kimchi bokeumbop.

None of the dishes were bad, but the hummus was mediocre, and I found the shakarkand chaat-esque smoked yam with yogurt and sev to lack sufficient spice. The mushroom bolognese rigatoni was also good, but nothing I'd dream of having again.

Was underwhelming. Those 2 words sum up the experience. The drink list is limited recommend adding few cocktails. They were out of the burger I wanted to try. Out of the 5 dishes we ordered I barely remember one. I think the dosa, they should leave to South Indian restaurants. I recommend going to adyar Anand bhavan or sarvana to taste real one.
Great indoor ambiance and comfortable spacing to adhere to social distancing. Has small servings, meant for sharing.

What a cute spot to go to for date night! Came on a Friday night, inside was a quarter capacity at 9pm, they have ample outdoor seating with 6 feet distancing. Originally made a rsvp for their sister spot abc Kitchen but due to unforseen circumstances had to be accommodated to this one, which wasn't a problem at all! At the front, they take down your information for contact tracing and then have you step up to this scanner for your temperature. Very high tech! 

Ambience was very romantic, candles and dim lit area. Really sets the mood! 

Our server was super sweet and had awesome hair! Too bad she had to leave before our meal was done. Very personable and friendly! 

We ordered the mushroom Walnut Bolognese, Applewood smoked butter beans, whole roasted cauliflower and green chickpea hummus that came with pita bread. Everything was phenomenal, perfect texture, temperature and not too salty and im normally a carnivore so this was trying something different and also because my friend is a vegan but it felt so refreshing and not heavy at all! Presentation was impeccable, everything came out around the same time didn't even get to finish taking photos before the next dish was out! 

Wrote in the notes when making rsvp that it was a celebration of birthdays so towards the end of the me the waiter brought out a coconut sherbet? With a candle on it and with the happy birthday writing on the plate. Super cute and adorable! Would definitely come back again and to try out their other sister locations!!

Not to be confused with ABC Cocina -- this is a full on vegan restaurant. Had reservations for 8 people (indoors, post-COVID), the ambiance is dreamy. I loved the white tables and dim lighting. It was so grown up, elegant, and lowkey. We went for a birthday so it was perfect. 

I got the lavender ghost drink, it was too strong for me. Might be best to stick with wine. 

The menu is a bit confusing. They recommended each person to get 2-3 dishes. YOU DO NOT NEED THAT MUCH. We each got one dish, maybe 2 if one was an appetizer. That was enough. I got the mushroom bolognese -- it was not flavorful. The only dish I liked was the "special" chicken of the woods. Everything else lacked salt. 

Overall, very good vibes, but little in return for your money.

Jean George has done it ! He has made an Indian Dosa Better than Indians themselves ( im south Asian and live next to Saravana bhavan/ so I know what I'm talking about here )

Best brunch I've had in a while , once the seating confusing sorted itself out - it was an explosion of flavors in a subtle but satisfying way. 

He retained authenticity of the globally inspired cuisines while being inspired and creative - and healthy ! I picked this place for its emphasis on vegan ness and anti inflammatoriness and I was not disappointed . A must go for any health conscious, open palated, foodie

5 stars for the food, everything was exquisite. -1 for the outdoor ambience, or lack of, during covid. Shockingly there are no heaters, tables simply placed in the street. The vibe is respectfully minimal but extending the indoor ambience to their new outdoor dining would go a long way in complimenting the delicious food. Many restaurants have found ways to comfortably do so.

1 out of only 2 restaurants that I've been to for indoor dining during the pandemic (the other being JG). 

really impressed with how spacious the interior was - they went beyond the 6 feet CDC guidelines. There were probably only 3 other tables inside the restaurant. 

Dosa here is amazing, my girlfriends and I ordered two of it, it was just that good. I loved everything here except the burger. One of my girlfriends is vegan and eats vegan everything and even she thought the burger patty was gross.

JG did it again with his all vegetarian restaurant where you won't miss the meat. Ambiance is minimalist and serene. The dosa's are so good and better than many at Indian restaurants. The juices are also delish!

ABCV is probably my favorite restaurant in Manhattan. The vegetables are cooked perfectly and the sauces are amazing. The food is healthy, filling, and delicious. When we go, we love to get a few different cocktails and plates for the whole table to share. The decor is beautiful and the atmosphere is vibrant yet soothing.

The place is very nice
I'd love to go again and try more of their food

All of their entrees was very interesting and beautifully designed 

I'd give Roasted Cauliflower five stars and recommend for the first timers

I can't wait to try more of their food

As a Vegan, I could sit and rave for a novel about ABCV, but I'll keep it short and sweet. 

We stopped here for a nice outdoor dining experience and I kid you not when I tell you every single bite was AMAZING. Our waiter was so kind and helpful in finding items we'd love. All the details down to the plates and cups were so aesthetic and show how much care is put into making eating here a full experience. What's great is you can order from any of their 3 menus incase someone dining with you isn't Vegan (although they should definitely eat Vegan, they'll love it). 

We ordered the squash soup which was just as good, if not better, than it looks. We then got the yam tandoori entree which had me scraping the plate. We ended with the chocolate cherry cake and it was heavenly. 

This may be one of my favorite new spots in the city and I'll definitely be back (a lot!)

Overall I would say it was a okay spot for brunch. I would highly recommend the dosa and the chocolate croissant. We also wanted to try the chia pudding, but it was sold out...and we went at 11:30 (FYI, the place opens at 11). Not sure if they just didn't make enough since it's not a popular dish or it's too popular of a dish that it sold out in 30 minutes. Probably won't be back for brunch, but might come try dinner one night.

Amazing Vegan/plant-base restaurant! Everything on the menu was on point and you forget you're eating vegan food ha! I really enjoyed the atmosphere and of course the food. What I do like about eating vegan food is that you don't feel gross hah! 

Things I ordered: 
- Green Chickpea Hummus: thai basil, fresh pita or crudité
- Slow Roasted Eight Ball Squash: coconut, cashews, flowers, warming spices
- Whole Roasted Cauliflower with turmeric-tahini and pistachios
- Bolognese pasta

I would definitely come back and try other items on the menu!

Strictly Vegan. DON'T COME IF YOU LIKE MEAT!!!
Great ambiance and service. Nice looking cocktails. The pasta dish came out cold twice. The third time it came out ok. Still very hungry afterward.

What can I eat? That is the dilemma you will face. 

If you like mushrooms, pasta or yams then you're set. If you remember the old ABCV menu that boasted a robust set options of healthy and organic dishes, then you're at the wrong place. Yes it's Jean Georges, and has a nice ambiance but let's get to the nitty gritty.

The menu is EXTREMELY LIMITED, consists of mostly mushroom, pasta and potato dishes. If you want any modifications to something on the menu, keep dreaming. If you're on the keto diet you're out of luck. If you order the pasta be prepared to have it get served cold multiple times before you actually get a hot one. Make sure you check the bill because odds are it won't be right!

Being fair, you must commend top notch service and delicious cocktails. The ginger julep is an A+! However, I'll be damned if you think you're going to find a meal that can satisfy a group of 4 or more.

Disclaimer: I am not vegan.

I have actually never been to a strictly vegan/vegetarian only place before so I wanted to give abcV a try.

I ordered the following during dinner hours:
- Smoky tandoori white yam ($23)
- Whole roasted cauliflower ($27)
- Mushroom walnut bolognese ($24)
- Flagrant chili peppercorn broth ($27)

I was not a big fan of the food that they served. The menu was very, very limited as there were only a few options to choose from. I actually thought the tandoori white yam was delicious. The flavors that the sauce gave the yams were on point. The crispy noodles that topped it really gave the dish the added texture that it needed.
