The roasted cauliflower is the most hyped menu item from this place. But I still cannot imagine why people would pay $27 for a smaller cauliflower. The parts of it that were charred did not taste good at all. The bolognese dish was very mediocre and tasted too bland and earthy for my liking. The broth dish with ramen actually smelled super delicious and was actually good but would be better if they toned down a bit on the chili oil.

The portion sizes are way too small for the prices that they are charging. I definitely would not be coming back here because of the limited menu items,  tiny portion sizes, and sky-high prices for mediocre food.

As a disclaimer, I'm not vegan nor have I tried many vegan restaurants. However, I do love trying out vegetarian and vegan meals so I was excited to try this place out especially after watching Worth It. 

We ordered 4 dishes in total: the fragrant chili peppercorn broth ramen, smoky tandoori white yam, whole roasted cauliflower, and mushroom walnut bolognese which came out to around 120 dollars. 

The food was flavorful but was not worth the price for the portions they give. If you have to order 4 dishes for 2 people that don't eat much in the first place, there's an issue. The cauliflower always seems to be the highlight but paying 27 dollars for a small cauliflower is a bit much. 

What increased my rating from a 1 star to a 2 star was that the service was great, they really tried to accommodate us and make our dinner special

Very good ambience for a date or a formal dinner. It took a while to get seated even though we had a reservation, probably because of the rain. The food menu was somewhat small - the taste was good and different, and the portion sizes are small and balanced. The ramen could have been more flavorful though. Overall a good experience.

I came here with my 2 friends for brunch on a Saturday, and was not very impressed, unfortunately. 

I was so excited to try this place, but I found a lot of the food to be pretty salty and not impressive, especially my sandwich and the mushroom entree dishes, and my dosa.

I also thought the menu was a bit light, and limited, some of the items I had heard about were not on the menu. 

Out of the several dishes my party ordered, I only enjoyed the green hummus, which was very good with the fresh vegetables and pita they serve. 

My sandwich was so salty and I was done with it after 2 bites and made my boyfriend eat it to avoid food waste, and even he did not enjoy it. And the small side salad that came with the sandwich was definitely bad tasting, bland, tasteless, and odd.

The waitstaff was only okay, and not very attentive, and kept taking our plates away, even after we asked them to leave them. 
Will likely not be returning honestly. Under impressed overall.

Ambiance was casual, but still dark and kind of romantic. The food was great. A great date night place if you are looking for plant based options. The staff also seems to be diverse which I like and the cocktails were really delicious.

Really a very overrated place. I loved the food but the Dosa is not as good as a South Indian Dosa we would get in other restaurants. The place looks nice but not exceptional. It's a one time visit for me. I don't think I would be going back.

When I use to go here it was amazing from the food to the atmosphere. I recently dined here and was extremely disappointed. The once amazing food wasn't even tasty. Please go back to how you once were abcV.

the food had very average flavor. furthermore there was just so much oil. like just because this is a vegetarian restaurant, you don't need oil to make dishes taste good. DO NOT ORDER THE RAMEN! but the service was Michelin tier at least

This place was almost like a dream. The service was incredible. The plates were so pretty. The food was absolutely delicious. I was so surprised by the Green Hummus, the vegetables were so fresh and delicious. 
Oh and there are boss women in the kitchen, yes yes yessss. I would go back again. Really enjoyed our time there.

Not at all what I expected. With the ratings I was expecting the best vegan food in the city but I would be curious to meet the people that give this restaurant a good review to understand why. This was the most overpriced food I've had in the city. We spent $40 for 1 piece of asparagus cut up into 6 pieces after the sever recommended it. The only saving grace was the drinks were delicious but they did not make up for the experience.

We had such a great experience here! Arnold was so helpful and friendly, and gave amazing recommendations. We felt so supported and welcomed, and absolutely loved having Arnold as our server! The food and ambience were exquisite. Will definitely be returning!

Food was excellent! Very nice staff too!
It was a little expensive though, but quality was the best in the city!

Amazing meal. The hummus and cauliflower are two delicious dishes that will surprise your pallet in every bite.
The restaurant is super nice and the service was very accommodating.
I also came for brunch and the poached eggs with mushrooms are delicious (we did have to add salt as it was not salted at all when it was served but after salting properly it was delicious)

I had a great birthday meal here and have had a nice experience every single time I've come. The menu is always quite creative, the cocktails are great, and the service is good. I plan to come back here a lot.

Our waitress was excellent, the beet dish and the avocado lettuce leaf were great.

The main / only issue is with this "mushroom" dish, which was actually a roasted celery heart. For every single other dish, the key ingredient was emphasized - for this one, the ingredient emphasized was the most expensive ingredient (chanterelle, of which there was one, chopped up), whereas the actual dish was roasted celery root.

The restaurant and staff are mostly great, but please rectify this aberration and I will rectify my review.

Delightful and memorable veggie food, but wow, the prices are steep! The variation in prices across the menu (approx. $15-$30 per item) also does not really reflect differences in portion size. Mostly everything is sort of "tapas" size, meaning just a handful of bites (even for the more expensive dishes), although there is the occasional surprise, such as the fragrant basmati, which was entree-sized. This was probably my favorite dish, and not just because of the size - I can't stop thinking about that lemony tang and those toasty peanuts! The sourdough blue corn focaccia was interesting and good: one very generous slab of focaccia served with sunflower nori butter (!!) and tomato. The California dates were tasty but probably not worth getting again: four date halves, stuffed with a coconut yogurt spread, fresh mint, and pistachio. (Maybe this would have been better as a dessert?) The shallot labneh was excellent. The wood roasted beets were very good: a few thick slabs of beet topped with amazing coriander chutney and delicious crispy curry leaves. For drinks, the cantaloupe martini was delicious, and so was the apricot milk punch.

We came here for brunch and are so pleased with our visit. The restaurant vibe is so nice and all the workers here are very friendly. Our food was amazing- highly recommend the soft scrambled eggs they were delicious. We definitely will be coming here again on our next trip to New York!

For vegans, vegetarians, and plant-based peeps this place is like the kids say - lit!  For a good night out with upscale dining - go here. Awesome drinks, apps, food, desserts, and coffee. 

Get the Mezcal Maracuya! Fernet Vallet, and a blackberry fernet on the after dinner drink menu! That's cool. 

Saison eggplant was very different and exceptional. Whole roasted cauliflower was so good - exceeded expectations.  Only miss was a special succotash with shredded Australian truffle. Truffle did not taste so good and I typically love truffle. 

Highly recommend. Will be back.

Went for lunch today with a friend. I had wanted to try this restaurant out for over a year. It was awful! Way way too much sodium and very poor use of spice. The hummus was terrible, as were the raw vegetables that accompanied. Just lackluster...the hummus so bad we sent it back. The dosa was too thick and doughy, the filling extremely sparse. The chop salad was full of potential, but the almost childish use of ingredients made each bite an unpleasant adventure--would the next bite be shockingly spicy? Too salty? Loaded with a strange burning crunchy raw thing or spearmint or cilantro....nothing worked. Everything was horribly salty. We informed our  waiter that we did not want anything too spicy/flaming hot, and he proceeded to take our order without telling us that everything we ordered was a spice bomb! When we expressed to him how we felt about the food, he tried to sell us dessert. At no point did anyone on this waitstaff ask us if we had everything we needed...once. That was it. Wish it was better. I'm still embarrassed that I recommended!

I really like the vibe of this place, the design and the feel are kool and welcoming and very much in line w ABC esthetic. The servers were really nice and the place ran like a well oiled machine. The dishes were good but after 3 plates we both left a bit hungry, the portions were really quite small, perhaps that's the way food should be and we r so used to enormous American sized portions lol
Fantastic. Everything was delicious (get the corn fritters). The service was lacking, but I blame it on the pandemic. We cannot wait to go back!
had an amazing meal here. right now i have a dilemma. go back here or to regular abc kitchen!

Ordered blue corn pancakes which were sweet with a hint of. Pt e and were absolutely delicious.. can't wait to go back just to have them again.. also tried the avocado toast with had a layer of spicy sauce that added a very good kick.. would recommend the two..

This place is good! Not impressed with some of the dishes but enjoyed our time overall. A bit expensive...

I came here with my girlfriend as we heard the hype, saw the YouTube Worth It video and had to see what was up. 

Ambiance (5/5): I personally loved the ambiance. The exterior of the building is open and inviting and you can see what's happening inside. It's also on a busy, happening street with other restaurants. The interior has a super clean layout and design and is well kept and was packed.

Food (3/5): The food was okay. I didn't have strong feelings about it tbh. We ordered a few dishes (each pretty expensive for the small portion you get. The Labne and Cauliflower were great, and would recommend those. The corn soup was also good. However, I don't recommend the bolognese. Didn't really taste like anything and was our least favorite dish. Did I mention how expensive it is for such little food?? 

I had one drink from the bar which was a non-alcoholic Soba drink of some sort which was AWESOME. Had a great earthy flavor, which was addictive and wasn't too sweet.

Service (4/5): Again, was okay but not great. They are very busy, and the host was really unaccommodating to our request to get seated 5 minutes earlier when we arrived which was a bit off-putting. Propitiously, this led us to the bar where I had one of the BEST drinks - the Soba, which I can't recommend enough. 

Glad I tried it once, but not sure I would go again

abcV is the epitome of semi formal fine dining. Great food, gorgeous environment, and amazing service. What I love about this restaurant is that all of their dishes are meant to be shared with the table, which I believe is so important after not seeing our friends and family for so long, that we share these intimate and joyful experiences together.

However, their portion size was quite small, and while that allowed us to try more dishes from the menu, I believe it would be more fulfilling if it was larger (especially for a larger group of 7 people). Furthermore, some of the vegetables presented on the dishes were unaltered - which is fine - but i didn't feel like a stick of raw radish dipped into hummus needs to be glorified the way it was. Hummus was good though.

Their water tasted supernatural. A choice of sparkling and still water was offered - I tried both, and both soothed my senses.

A reservation should be booked beforehand especially when coming with a larger group.

Went here for brunch with a friend. It is a vegan/vegetarian sister restaurant of the ABC restaurants, located right next to the ABC furniture store. All the food we ordered was tasty, and packed with flavor. The wait staff was very kind and knowledgable about the menu and had recommendations to give if you are unsure of what to order. The beautiful soft decor and light fixtures created a calm yet fun and whimsical vibe to dine in with friends. Overall a delicious and fun experience.

We have been wanting to come here since long! Finally made it on a special occasion. The cocktails were great. Loved the smoky and charred flavor in Beluga lentils - would highly recommend this dish. I couldn't imagined lentil could be made this way. The Fragrant chili peppercorn broth was amazing too - so flavorful! For dessert we ordered chocolate ganache cake which was great! Just keep in mind portion size is really small here!

The ambience here is the best part, everything is white and it feels fancy. The menu is different and has a wide variety of options but nothing really stuck out when picking. We asked the waiter for recommendations and they turned out to be delicious. This is your typical NYC semi-fine dining though - not much quantity and it's expensive.

Regrettably wish I could leave a more favorable review and equally higher "star rating"; however, this restaurant continues to take their loyal Vegan and Vegetarian customers for granted. The main course portions are extremely tiny and served in small appetizer plates. If you go, just make a reservation on Curry Hill for real and better priced vegetarian food as a lot of the culinary influences are Indian based.

Good: service was attentive and professional. However, they did bring my pita bread after we finished dinner.

Space: industrial chic; feels high end.

Recommend: Roasted Cauliflower and Basmati Rice as main courses. However, these are toddler portions so eat before you come to enjoy the space and the  company you're with :)

Good service, good drinks. 

While the food was decent too, but remember you're coming here for the ambiance and experience and fresh produce and such and not as much for bombastic flavours. 

Dosa - alright and home style. Lack of uniform crispiness or more to than usual colours after being cooked on the griddle was a bit disappointing to look at. Could be heartier and more filling with some spiced soup or lentils instead of just Greek yogurt. 

Basmati - a take on lemon rice, done well but 
did I miss any crunchy accompaniment with it? 

Green chickpea hummus - nice and refreshing. 

Pita - soft, easy to eat. 

Apple kohlrabi salad - skippable. 

Burger - decent, could've done with more flavours. Or maybe I only got a bite too small to tell as we shared. 

Cauliflower - looked amazing. Tasted good. 

We tried a lot of the cocktails and except for the arrack one, all were very good. The table favourites were the mezcal one with coconut and the concord grape margarita.

Came here after going to SUGARFISH. We only got drinks and the wine was one of the reds recommended by the waitress but it wasn't anything spectacular. It's a cute date night ambiance but we just sat at a high top table and it felt like it was in the way of a lot of foot traffic.

Not sure I'd come back for food here but we were able to be seated quickly as a walk in on a Thursday night which was a positive.

This places was recommended from a non vegan / vegetarian so I thought it must be great. I decided to splurge and go.
I am party of one, so I couldn't reserve a sit (not online and they won't answer the phone). But luckily there was a place available on the spot.
The waiter was very eager and nice. I decided to go big with the 75$ special which was good but definitely not worth the price. 
As soon as I finished the waiter brought the check, he said I can stay for a while due to the rain but I felt not welcomed there anymore.

I have been wanting to try ABVC for years now. Maybe my expectations were high, but it did not deliver on multiple fronts. 

DRINKS
Tried 3 drinks and they all tasted like concoctions I would make in college aka not that special. On paper they seemed intricate and a fun blend of flavors, but then when we tried them, they were all just eh. One even tasted like meds. Would stick to wine or standard cocktails like a G&T where you can't go wrong. 

FOOD
I feel like I had a similar experience with the food. On the menu the mixture of ingredients seemed like they would deliver a nice punch of flavors but everything was just bland. We thought with every new dish that hey this might be the one that's going to be a little better and every bite was just flat. Also felt like everything was under-seasoned. Here's what we got (all recommended by the waitress)

Coconut Sticky Rice
Salad with apples 
Squash purée app - pita served with was just sad, looked store bought  
Taproot (fried)

Drinks
Spicy martini - zero spice tasted like meds 
Gin with red pepper - zero red pepper taste

This is one of those...I never write a review but the experience was so bleh that I am taking the time to write a negative one.

Waiter was nice and knowledgeable 

Focaccia was okay, but sacrilegious and was country bread at best

Don't order the Japanese cauliflower

The special was a bucatini served luke warm, it was okay

The wontons were the best thing we ordered, but at a world class restaurant they would have been a good starter and not the most impressive thing on the table.

Save yourself the time from this blase over priced experience with sub par service. 

Thinking back...the decor almost perfectly summarizes the dining experience. Undefined. Unresolved. Underwhelming.

I'm typically a big meat eater but this place really opened my eyes to how delicious vegetarian / vegan food can be. In addition to great food, the service was top notch, great creative cocktails and a perfectly designed environment that balanced lighting, colors and music perfectly.

Super good but maybe not worth the price... 

So given this is an upscale, higher priced spot, I'm a bit more critical. 

The aesthetic was beautiful. Clean, white and very open. We sat at the counter with a kitchen view so could see food being prepared: I love places that do this and it was so much fun to watch at the counter. I was a bit disappointed by the wait staff. They were not very attentive, didn't check up really. Nitpicking maybe, but for the type of place I just expected top tier service. 

For lunch we got the honeynut squash, egg/cheese dosa, farro bowl, steamed veg, cherry cake, and hazelnut mochi.

My partner and I saw the crock pot that the squash dip was prepared in and made plots for how to steal it because it was that good. The pita to dip ratio was wayyy off. They also serve a hummus dip that comes with pita AND crudité but the squash dip only comes with the pita so we ended up ordering a second pita because there was more than half of the dip left (and trust me, we would scoop a lot of dip on our pita).

I'm fully plant based so didn't try the dosa personally, but my partner said the dosa itself was very well made and the cheese/egg made it very filling. 

The farro bowl was so yummy, with many flavor and texture combinations to keep you interested throughout the whole bowl. 

The steamed veg was quite a disappointment. Incredibly overcooked (the broccolini would fall off a fork it was so mushy) so the broth it came it just seemed counterintuitive. The broth itself also added no flavor, tasted just like lemon juice. If I'm paying $17 for 5 broccolini stems and 2 bok Choi leaves, I just expect perfection, especially at a vegetable focused restaurant. 

Dessert was the comeback we needed. The chocolate cherry cake was very cherry forward and not too intensely of chocolate. The mochi dish was so unique and wonderful. Lots of great textures between the soft mochi, cold ice cream, and crunchy hazelnuts. Another flavor and texture explosion. 

Overall definitely beautiful to the eye, but given the price point fell short a couple places.

I came here once three years ago, and was looking forward to coming back ... but I forgot just how much I loved this spot!  I was a little nervous bringing my carnivorous husband this time, but he didn't miss the meat this time around which I view as a testament to the flavorful preparations and thoughtful menu by the restaurant.

Drinks were excellent - subtle flavors, not too strong and light enough to not overpower the food.

Service was superb - our server was incredibly knowledgeable about the menu and recommendations when prompted.  I asked for pairwise comparisons in every section of the menu, and she was able to describe in delectable detail what to expect with each dish.  She was incredibly engaging and pleasant - just a delight.

Food was all excellent with a range of flavors and textures.  We had the squash dip with the pita which was warm and perfect for fall.  The full head of cauliflower is a specialty and would highly recommend - we initially thought we would pass as we make a whole cauliflower dish at home, but I'm really glad that we tried this one for new inspiration.  

Decor is nearly all white (with some light pink accents) which makes it fit well for a nice dinner in jeans or a formal dinner all dressed up.

The food took over an hour to arrive. The restaurant was not full and we watched another table get salad and hot dosa and dessert  and then lukewarm pancakes and not warm pear entree arrived. We won't be back.

We had a delightful dinner here with family! The restaurant was full even though it was a Monday night. The restaurant was beautifully decorated and the staff was polite and friendly. My favorite dishes were the California dates, the Walnut Bread, the most delicious Roasted Whole Cauliflower, the Katsu, and the Labneh. The Mushroom Bolognese was also good. The Cherry Chocolate cake was delightful! I could go vegan if I could eat like this!

We got a table for 4 and ordered 1 of the bottles of wine, I think it was a Sangiovese. The wine was ok, but could hardly blame the restaurant for it. But over the next 30 minutes, we started to realize the service wasn't that great either. It just one of those places that seem to do all the right things but still get everything wrong. For instance, they filled our water glasses constantly but didn't bring our wine for the longest time. Eventually, we ordered the focaccia bread and that was really good!
For entrees We got the dosa, beluga lentils, carrot entree and the rigatoni one. They were all just ok, quite underwhelming to by honest. The carrot based entree probably being the best of these. Another thing was that our entrees came slowly one at a time and we couldn't really have eaten it together at all. The dosa came without the yogurt or avocado and upon notifying the servers, they send our server and she went to check in to let us know that it was indeed a mistake and that they'll bring a new dosa (the old one was pretty cold at this point) and not charge us for it.

For dessert, we got the Yuzu tart. That was the final nail in the coffin -  it looked so sickly and sad, really. The Yuzu flavor carried it but the tart was terrible and custard was not smooth and creamy and overall super disappointing. 

I was honestly looking forward to this experience but left disappointed, underwhelmed, slightly hungry and very upset. Would not recommend this place.

My husband and I ate at abcV for dinner while enjoying a Christmas weekend in the city. At nearly $30 a dish, which are meant to be shared, it put it into the special occation dinner range for our wallet. We ordered three and shared them. It was enough food that we were full but not overly so by the end. 

We started with the Whole Roasted Cauliflower with turmeric tahini, za'atar, date molasses pomegranate, red zhug, fresh herbs, pistachio  at $29. I was skeptical because everyone now has a whole roast cauliflower, but it was truly amazing. You could tell the cauliflower was first branded and had flavor throughout even before the herb tahini top or red zhag sauce. 

We then followed it with the Saison Battered Maitake with calamansi turmeric honey, black tahini togarashi, scallion at $28. It was by far the best mushroom dish I've had. Mind blowing in crunch and the sauce was a perfect mix of sweet and acidity to cut the fried batter. 

We finished with the Wild Matsutake Kabocha Wontons with aromatic peppercorn broth citrus, tender market greens at $35. It was the only letdown of the evening. Though the filling of the wonton was delicious the broth wasn't to our taste. Would recommend skipping this dish.

The most disgusting and tasteless food I ate in my life. Don't waste your time and don't waste your money. For the first time in my life, I had to spit out food because it tasted so terrible here. Not to mention that they should be ashamed of themselves for charging an arm and two legs for what is on the menu.

Amazing vegetarian food with a surprisingly eclectic menu! Loved the ambience and the food!

Food: you have to do this restaurant family style so you can try many different items. We ordered the Labneh, whole cauliflower, rice, and dosa! I enjoyed everything! The Labneh was an amazing dip that I could just eat alone! It was so flavorful and rich! The caulflower is one of the signature dishes and I would highly recommend ordering! It will not disappoint! The rice was my least favorite. The dosa was good but pretty plane

Drinks: good wine selection

Ambience: it is a crowded spot! I went on a Tuesday night and it was very happening! But it is a beautiful restaurant with a view into the chefs making food

Service: a bit awkward service tbh! Felt a bit rushed! 

Price: expensive - but the flavors and quality are worth it!

The restaurant's atmosphere was romantic. Low lighting, soft. I went on a Thursday night and there were no actual tables available so we sat at a high top. 

Everything on the menu can be made vegan. We ordered based on the waiter's recommendations so I don't recall what was ordered exactly other than mushroom Bolognese and some giant cauliflower. The appetizers were small plates but the entrées were a little larger. 

I would go back. It's right by union square holiday market. Street parking was available.

For the last three years, this has been, and still is, one of mine and my boyfriend's (not vegetarian) favorite restaurants in nyc. It's our go to treat yourself spot. They really take vegetables to a new level.

A+ for atmosphere. It's modern and cozy and feels very special and romantic. Great place to impress your date. 

At this point, I've tried the majority of threats on the menu. Here are some of my favorite dishes:

-roasted whole cauliflower head- never disappoints. My boyfriend hated cauliflower before he tried this and now he's been reformed!

-mushroom walnut bolognese- the sauce is so savory and flavorful. The pasta is perfectly al dente. We usually can't resist ordering this. A decent portion too. 

-honeynut squash dip- this was a favorite of my party. The squash is basically whipped and topped with a delicious yogurt sauce.

-saison battered mistake-this was very delicious. Basically a giant thickly bartered tempura mushroom. 

All in all, really special food and ambiance. Check it out!

After making reservations over 2 weeks in advance, we celebrated our anniversary here and were given a very nice comfortable corner seating at this extremely comfortable, low lighting, romantic kind of setting restaurant. 

Welcomed by a friendly team, we were seated right away and placed our order for cocktails which included a very flavorful Bell Pepper Martini ($17), Smoky Fig Sour ($18), and Rose of Sharon ($18). Smoky fig sour is a definite must try for whisky lovers and Rose of Sharon was the least fun to drink! Cocktails overall lacked the spirit punch, but were enjoyable.

Erin, who helped us during our visit was friendly and explained to us that it was a tasting menu and 2 to 3 dishes per person on an average would be ideal. We took that suggestion and ordered a few things which included Shallot Labneh ($20), Saison Battered Maitake ($28), Norwich Meadows Badger Flame Beets ($21), Dosa ($21), Whole Roasted Cauliflower ($29), and Mushroom Walnut Bolognese ($26).

Personally, I am not a big fan of tasting menus, and the pricing at abcV is definitely on an expensive end. The things we ordered were based off on other Yelp reviews, and food overall was just okay. We love bold flavors, and the only dishes that really impressed us were the Shallot Labneh and Saison Battered Maitake.

A different take on Dosa, which was served with cold sprouts, avocado, and yogurt confirmed that Dosa is a dish best served in its classic form with (or without) potato masala subji and the traditional sambar and chutneys, and was one of our least favorite dishes of the evening. The mushroom walnut bolognese was good too, but our pasta was slightly thicker (and chewer) than we like it to be.

Portion sizes to prices are slightly off. Veggie food presented in different styles/cuisines including Middle Eastern, Indian, and Italian though were quite interesting.

Noise level was low, easy to have conversations, and a very friendly team definitely adds a star!

So good! My favorite vegan place in the city. The staff is amazing and KNOW THEIR STUFF. The crispy mitake was amazing and a MUST. Our waitress suggested that we keep the sauce for the cauliflower and she was not wrong. I came with my boyfriend and we were both STUFFED after. I love love loved this meal and can't wait to be back again
Excellent restaurant overall.  We went with our Vegan son and enjoyed everything.  Highly recommended.

Superb!  Food was absolutely delicious. We shared a squash dish with warming spices and tahini served with warm home made pita. 
I had a basmati rice with peanut, micro-greens and delicious spices and friend had mushroom (vegan) bolognaise. Perfect size dishes. Cooked to perfection. We ate outside under heat lamp. Service was excellent. 
Covid protocols in place.

Great ambiance and loved the decorations. We ordered cocktails to start. I got the Mezcal Drink and it was good but not my favorite cocktail I've ever had. It's a must to get the cauliflower and the Maitake and the mushroom Bolognese.  I could have done without the squash purée and the dates. They didn't have much flavor.
The food is excellent, truly spectacular and exciting flavors. The service is great, and I like the atmosphere. It is quite pricey, though.

My bf and I came for date night. We loved the ambiance and the decor. Very simple romantic and clean. We had the maitake, wontons and the cauliflower. The maitake was amazing!! The cauliflower was also really good. We loved all the different flavors!! The wontons were definitely different but not terrible. I also had the pineapple upside down cake and gurllllaaaaa, it was so good I had to order a second. If I didn't grab the last piece, I would've ordered a third . Our back waitress was Tatiana! (Hope I spelt her name correctly). She was amazingggg. Loved her vibe so much. She recommended great drinks for us. I don't remember our Sake name, but it was something with fox lol. So yummy. Our waitress was Janina, she was so knowledgeable of every thing which is a plus and on top of everything. Both were absolutely great and worked well together. Lastly, the manager, Paden, also great energy, loved speaking with him and just super nice. The three of them are what makes new restaurant experiences amazing. Can't wait to be back (need that pineapple upside down asap already). Wish I took pics, but I was smashing everything. Thanks guys!!!

Against my better instincts, I'm a fan of ABC Kitchen. I don't particularly care for Jean-George's empire (though Nougatine is nice) and have always found the food/drinks to be good but overpriced, but the stunning decor and beautiful ambience of ABCK always brought me back. 

I wasn't expecting much from ABCV besides a blander, whiter (literally--have you seen the decor?) version of ABCK, but was pleasantly surprised by how nice everything was.

- Shallot Labneh: I spent a week in Jordan last November, but tried not to compare the real deal from the motherland with this labneh. On its own, it's still incredibly tasty and I loved the addition of black sesame seeds, both for taste and aesthetics.

- Saison Battered Maitake: Mushrooms any way are usually a hit for me, but mushrooms in this marvel of a black sauce are in the upper echelon. This one's a win for shroom lovers.

- Smoky Woodear & Potato Wontons: On a cold winter night, this is the hearty, soupy dish you want. 

- Celery Root Katsu: Surprisingly tasty if you're a celery fan, and the shredded shiso topping was just divine. I wish more restaurants would incorporate shiso (green and red) into their greens.

Drink-wise, get the Smoky Fig Sour if you want the best (drunk) bang for your buck, the Bergamot Reviver for something light and refreshing, and the Mezcal Maracuyá for an in-between. And if you want to warm up, the best cocktail of the night (IMO) was the deliciously spiced Saffron Golden Mylk Hot Toddy. Cinnamon, cloves and cardamom, oh my!

Minus a major star for service slowing down tremendously halfway through our meal. From 6-7pm, things were great. After 7pm, the place filled up completely, and like so many restaurants I've recently visited, they couldn't keep up with demand. Sigh.

I really don't understand the hype...the taste is just okay but the portion is so small! After 4 dishes, we went to Thai Villa for another dinner. The space is crumped and loud...it is not comfortable.

Came here for Valentine's Day weekend and had window seats. We didn't get the set menu but ordered 4 dishes to share with my boyfriend. Everything was delicious but we especially loved the mushroom dishes. We wanted the smoky woodear and potato wontons too but they had sold out so we just have to make another trip back. For dessert we were eyeing the tasting menu desserts and they let us order both even though we didn't order the tasting menu. We were so satisfied and full afterwards. They brought us some golden mylks on the house since it was Valentine's Day, which was a sweet gesture.

Wow I was so blown away with the aesthetics and food. My friend invited me here for brunch over the weekend and it was my first time eating here. Im not vegan so I was really impressed with the flavors. The portions were a little small more medium but all the food is best for sharing. But the portions were really good for me since I haven't been eating a lot lately. The mushroom with poached egg was amazing. So many flavors in the mushrooms! Plus I love mushrooms but I was surprised because of how they were able to make something simple so tasty. And of course I loved the almond pancakes! The almond butter on the side was the best part. The bananas go perfect with them too. I really appreciate the large size cup for the latte. It was a really good amount and I LOVE lattes so I really really appreciated that. The aesthetics of the restaurant are so beautiful, peaceful, bright and nice. Lovely vibes with the beautiful antique ish looking silverware. I'm a fan!
Food was exquisite! The carrots the brussel sprouts. Plenty of options to choose from, and all of them are just super tasty! A vegetarian favorite for me!

Enjoyed lunch at ABCv, and it's amazing they could seat our group of 7 at a round table! Great for a group.

Bests:
Avocado lettuce cups
Dosa - tumeric sambal, cheddar, egg, dill, mint - my favorite!
Wood roasted rainbow carrots w/ nut butter - this was delicious

Really good:
Dosa - Yogurt, avocado, sprouts
Beluga lentils sauteed in black vinegar and aromatic chili oil
Whole roasted cauliflower - loved this one!!
Market vegetable chop salad
Hemp seed burger

Wouldn't order again:
Savory grilled tartine - the weak link of the meal
Overhyped restaurant and We didn't like the food there . Prices are too high but the food taste quality and quantity was not that good

The most condescending hostess  ever in NYC, possibly globally. We had a reservation and were on time and she still was the rudest person I've ever experienced. We actually left before getting seated because of her. Wow, why does this lovely restaurant keep her as their front of staff...

My sister and I visited for brunch on a Sunday at 1:30pm, and nearly every table was taken. Make sure to book a reservation a few days in advance! We also had 3 different servers as the first two got too busy and couldn't help us anymore. They were all very kind and helpful though despite the work demands. The brunch menu has limited vegan options compared to their dinner menu, but our server explained that poached/fried eggs could be substituted for avocado. We got the avocado lettuce wraps ($19 for only 2?!), seared mushrooms ($20, veganized with avocado substitute instead of egg), and the hemp/quinoa burger ($27). We had wanted to try the avocado tartine, but they were out of that. The wraps and mushrooms were our favorite. The wraps had a perfect blend of spices and textures and were sturdy to eat by hand. The mushrooms were simpler in flavor (salt, pepper, and dill), but were cooked to just the right softness. The burger itself had good flavor, but the patty was too soft and mushy for my liking. The beets on the side were also sour and atrocious to eat--better left as a colorful plate "decoration". Overall, definitely not worth the $27. 
We still had an appetite after the 3 dishes and were craving vegan croissants, but after experiencing the small portion sizes, we decided to get the pastries elsewhere. I've heard more positive things about abcV's vegan dinner options, so I hope to try that someday!
Food is good but not for the price they charge. I'm happy we tried them but not blown away.

The thing I love most about eating vegan is the creativity behind different dishes. It is an art form in itself and it introduces a whole new taste pallet. I went here for my anniversary, and the evening was magical. So many amazing dishes to chose from and so many fun new things I had never tried before. The employees are all very kind and professional and the vibe inside is very modern and cozy. Definitely more of a once in a while kind of place for me because it is on the pricier side but overall just spectacular.

My friend was visiting from Paris and asked if I wanted to join her at ABCV for dinner. Being new to the city, I don't turn down dinner invitations, so I accepted immediately. I then looked it up and realized it was high-end (Jean-Georges) vegan, so I tempered my expectations, knowing it would be an expensive and perhaps not satisfying dinner. I was going for the company after all, so I was less concerned with what the restaurant would be like.

I was pleasantly surprised by how satisfying all of the dishes were and the fact that I left not just full, but with leftovers for another meal. I honestly didn't even notice that the meal didn't have any meat. As mushroom lovers, we ordered the saison battered maitake, the shiitake mushrooms and the mushroom walnut bolognese in addition to the whole roasted cauliflower and the slaw. My favorite dishes were the bolognese and the slaw (which definitely surprised me). The leftovers even held up well for another meal. Pricey but not crazy given that the portions are actually more generous than you would think. I'd come back!

Pea hummus & Salad was amazing!! The mushroom bolognese and roasted cauliflower was not great, which the waitress recommended. wish I ordered other items as everything looks really appetizing 8 j. I wanted to try everything. Great ingredients in their non alcoholic drinks. Overall ambiance was very chic and pleasant.

All of the food is excellent. Small portions so just be prepared going in that you'll want to order a few dishes, so it ends up being a pricey meal, but definitely worth it. We had the fried maitake, the walnut bolognese and the yam bread with tomato. All of it was incredibly well prepared and interesting flavors. We sat at the chefs counter and watched the preparation - there was one beautiful beet dish that looked amazing and I want to try next time! The chairs at the chefs counter are like bar stools with a back - a bit narrow and not super comfortable. Very interesting cocktail menu and comprehensive list of non alcoholic mixed drinks (juices, extractions, shakes, etc)

Came here for brunch, wouldn't come again...

Mediocre food (we got the lettuce wraps, dosa, and avocado toast.)

My friends didn't like their drinks.

Portions were tiny -- we were all still hungry after the meal.

The most disappointing part is that my friend asked for hot sauce (a totally normal brunch request ammiright?!) and they charged us $7 for it. $7 for a side of hot sauce!!

If you're going to charge for a side of hot sauce when that's not standard practice anywhere else, you should tell the customer when they're ordering it. Nobody assumes they'll be charged for hot sauce at brunch -- and on top of that to charge $7?! That's as much as my drink cost! Eek. Very unpleasant experience.

I would have liked to give this a 5 star review due the the food, however the hostess (s) were beyond rude, condescending, and bad the evening horrible. The Hostess sat us at a high top near the door were we were getting hit by the door and incoming foot traffic. When I asked to move tables they didn't even look and said nothing was available. We went at 7pm on a Friday night, early for nyc standards, and the restaurant was empty. When I mentioned there were many open tables near the back they refused to seat us. Felt like we were at a fast food restaurant due to the amount of people near the door. Then the hostess sat someone immediately after us who did not have a reservation.
Delicious food. Super friendly service and environment feels cozy and intimate. Will return any time I'm in NYC.

Great food nice flavor full. Pricy though. Good place for special occasions. 
Can repeat for special occasions

This place is very upscale in both its ambience, food presentation, and taste. That being said, this restaurant may not be for everyone, as the dishes you can order are more "appetizer" sized than actual entrée size; there is no entree-sized dish, not to my knowledge (like vegan tapas). The server advised to order 4-5 dishes for a party of 2, and the average dish is between $20-30. 

This is a good place to try with friends/explore different cuisines if you're not a vegetarian (like myself). The only issue I had was the lack of a normal-portion-size meal, but that isn't the point or intention of the restaurant. All around good experience; I'd go again if I had vegan/vegetarian friends visiting.

Super delicious meal. My mom and one of my best friends and I had an amazing dinner here. We ordered the morelles with sticky rice, the shishito peppers, the eggplant, corn wontons, ginger tofu, and the whole roasted cauliflower. My personal favorites were the corn wontons and the eggplant. We also ordered a couple of delicious drinks. I don't remember the name of mine but it was like I was drinking a smoky corn flavored (don't knock it until you try it!) margarita. My friend ordered the honeydew daiquiri which was a great choice as well. Definitely recommend coming here for dinner or drinks. Well worth the price!

Back again for my third dinner... only thing we reordered was the whole roasted cauliflower, which was just as amazing as before. The price on Yelp says $27, but it is 29 just fyi. Worth it? Absolutely. We also tried a new fried eggplant appetizer, the grilled maitake and fennel, the summer squash, and the truffle pasta special. 

The summer squash was the a little underwhelming in terms of textures, but the sweet salty olive plus the tomato, and fresh grilled squash in a pool of olive oil was delightful to eat with pita (not included). 

The Saigon eggplant was super crispy and fresh in a napa cabbage boat, with a lemony avocado dressing and fresh Thai basil. Super strong lemon and basil flavor but delicious and perfect for the summer. 

I absolutely loved the mushroom dish, and it was even appreciated by a mushroom hater (don't get me wrong, they're not trying to disguise the mushroom-- it was just delicious). But five mushrooms is nothing for $21 or however much the dish was (a lot). Still, it was my favorite dish next to the cauliflower in terms of flavor. 

The truffle pasta was $69. This was definitely not worth it, but it was still yummy. A little plain in flavor- mostly just a creamy truffle tomato sauce. Not much textural variety (the breadcrumbs on top for "crunch" we're barely noticeable) and no real pop of flavor to wow you. Great truffle quality and quantity of course, but I definitely would not order or recommend ordering unless you can afford to regularly eat $100 dinners. 

All in all an amazing experience as usual, and I'm sure I'll be back!

Food is very average but expensive. Has a very eccentric vibe. 
Dessert was really good.
Corn dumplings, carrots and California dates are recommendations.

I've been a vegetarian for the past 20 years. I've been to numerous restaurants in different countries. The quality and quantity of the food here isn't worth it. It is okay at best. The cost is beyond ridiculous for the portion sizes and quality.

The food here is definetly surpriningly good especially since I am not vegan and usually wont get full. The hummus was soo delicous!! The cauliflower was also epic. Also loved the vibe and the service.

The food here is very good. Between two of us, we ordered 5 food items and 1 dessert. I also had a ginger tonic which I enjoyed. The standout food item was the dates - very small portion, but absolutely delicious. The pasta was also very good - cooked perfectly al dente. 

My only complaint: this was a hot August night, and it was a little bit too warm in the restaurant, and the water was room temperature which didn't help.
Interesting food. light and refreshing for the most part but everything tastes a little off to me. I wouldn't really recommend- you can get much better food for less money
Very very good. The kumquat salad is incredible. They carry Saratoga Sparking Water, which is my favorite.

I paid $27 for a seasonal "salad" that literally just consisted of half a mango and half a tomato. It was sprinkled with salt and black pepper and maybe one serrano pepper. THAT'S ITTTTTTT!!!!!This was one of their specials and not on the menu so I didn't know the pricing beforehand and while I fully expected some kind of markup because of the way this restaurant is generally,  $27?! Fuhgetabout it!! 

They said the mangoes are flown in from California when they presented the specials. Like so what? California sure as hell is not known for its mangoes so this pricing makes so sense. Presentation wasn't great either and I've had much better seasoned mangoes from the Mexican ladies who sell them on the street or on the subway. 

The only reason I am giving them one extra star is because the service was at least decent. I really hope the ridiculous prices for the tiny amount of basic food you get is going towards paying their wait staff premium wages because that would be the only thing that could remotely justify the sheer stupidity of the half mango I was just served. Overall, total rip-off.

abcV is certainly a lovely dining experience; something to be enjoyed on a special occasion! The prices are certainly steep but the dishes on their menu are rather novel fusion concepts drawing from Indian /Mediterranean/ Oriental cultures. We started with the honeynut squash/tahini dip and mint hummus which were both fairly good! It was odd they left one plate of pita for a table of five individuals....We were informed everything is eaten pretty much family style. Next we had the roasted rainbow carrots which was sooooo well seasoned and flavored, perhaps my favorite. After that we had the spinach spaghetti which wasn't my favorite but not bad. Roasted cauliflower was so well cooked it sliced easily and yet had a lovely bit to it. The seared tofu was also quite creamy and delicious in the ginger chili reduction. The beluga lentils was most comforting as it has many indian spices added, so the taste was quite familiar. My pomegranate mezcalita cocktail had a nice hickory smoky aroma, subtle fruity taste, and not too sweet which I appreciated. After ~8 -9 dishes for 5 people we were fairly full surprisingly, we had the cocao nib creme brulee as dessert which came with a complimentary dish of ice cream as we were celebrating a birthday. 

Service was prompt and friendly, management was lovely as well accommodating. Restaurant ambiance ok, nothing noteworthy. I certainly would recommend it to anyone vegetarian/vegan as the menu offers a variety of choices and offers something very novel. Considering the creativity, fresh ingredients and presentation, probably makes it pricey but ultimately they are ALL veggie dishes portions could be a little bigger in my humble opinion.

Had the famed cauliflower, lettuce cups, and mint hummus. The lettuce cups were the star of the show-- wow! Such an amazing combination of flavors. Rhe hummus came with some of the most flavorful, fresh carrots i have ever tasted. The cauliflower was very good but perhaps a bit overrated.  As for the price point, I am not yet convinced that the average $20+ price point for each of these selections are justified.  But judging from the packed house, there are plenty of folks who believe so! Worth experiencing once, to see what a celebrity chef's rendering of vegetables actually tastes like.

Food was wonderful - perfectly prepared, flavorful vegan dishes & thoughtful, inviting presentation. Less one star for seating us at a tiny high table adjacent to the main walkway for diners & staff when we had specifically requested an "out of the way" table for dinner due to COVID risk concerns (request w/ rese ~1wk in advance). The high table could only hold one (shared) dish at a time and seemed more appropriate for cocktails/drinks, with no elbow room between the wall and the busy aisle. Despite that the food was delightful & I'll return but only when the weather allows for outdoor seating.

I can sum up my opinions in one word: RIPOFF!  Easily the most overpriced restaurant in New York. 

When one decides to go out to dinner to a new place, you look online to see if the pricing is in line with the occasion. It was actually my birthday and my guest was my vegan son.  He and I have loved Vongerichten's French cooking for years (before he was vegan), so going to abcv seemed like a good idea based on the prices.

Nowhere online or on the menu do they say that everything is small plates.  I consider that deceptive.  We only found out when our waitress came with the menus and suggested 5-6 dishes for a party of two. My son did quick math and wanted to leave but I said we'd still enjoy the food, which we didn't for the most part.

The grilled oakwood shiitake mushrooms very totally over-salted.  The roasted butternut squash had too much heat for an autumnal vegetable.  The other dishes were just mediocre and tasted as if Vongerichten had nothing to do with their origins. The one standout was a tiny scoop of sweet potato ice cream.

I'm willing to pay big money for fine dining but this was far from it.  $150 before tip for veggies and an inexpensive glass of wine?!?  Insane. I'm not the only one who felt that way.  A couple was seated next to us, read the menu and got the news that everything was small plates. They got up and left.

The service is mediocre at best.  The hostess coped a real attitude when we arrived and instantly made us feel unwelcome. The noise level is very high because every surface is reflective. 

Again, I find it deceptive and a bit of an intentional ripoff for abcv  not inform you that it's a tapas place until well after you are seated. I've been going out for Manhattan fine dining since I was a teen and NEVER EVER got ripped off so badly.

Caveat emptor.

Came here for my birthday this year and had an incredible meal! As a vegetarian, I was pleasantly surprised that the whole establishment specialized in curating a 100% vegetarian experience! Here's what I got:
Cocktails - got the oishii drop and one more gin based one, they are both good not great
Whole roasted cauliflower with turmeric tahini & zaatar - the head of the cauliflower is fantastic and very well spiced! I did find that as you got to the root of the vegetable it got more bland but this is where the dipping sauce comes into play! 
Sweet corn wontons with spicy tomato broth - this was the star and a must! So so so flavorful and well balanced, just an explosion in your mouth. 110% recommend this. 
Red pepper hummus with caramelized pistachios - this was good as well, lots of depth while being pretty simple
Mushroom walnut bolognese - perfectly Al dente pasta and flavorful sauce! 
Chocolate Layer Cake - soooooo good! I'm not a big cherry person but this was just so rich and yummy! 10/10 recommend if you're a chocolate person like me :)

Overall I had a fantastic meal and will definitely be back for more!

let's start with the service; the minute we walked in we were greeted by the sweetest kindest person, Nijat Nijat is sooo pleasant and kind and helpful. Our server was Janina. We have never experienced a server quite like her. Her attention to details and her knowledge of the product is second to none. Janina is remarkable at what she does.
Khalid and Luz are also sooooo helpful and kind and soooo sweet and good at what they do. 

Now the food; it's next level. It's memorable and a treat. Every bite of our spinach pasta  was savored. We had a date appetizer that was as flavorful and unique as they come. Their soft serve  desert is like nothing else we've tasted. 
The executive chef is is special and ABC is beyond fortunate to have him. 
Last but not least is the manager; Erin. We had an issue with our table and she is soooo nice and accommodating. Erin is also fantastic at her job. The perfect disposition for what she does. 

ABC, I don't say this lightly when I say Nijat, Khalid, Luz, Janina and Erin are exceptional and your fortunate to have all on your side. 

And your restaurant is one of the BEST experiences my girlfriend and I have had the pleasure of enjoying. 

We're blessed to have you in the city.

I had been to ABCv once before but I think that the restaurant has significantly improved over the past year.

The entrees and starters were all delicious with many complex flavors and textures.

My favorite dish was the tofu which was extremely soft and silky, it just melted away as you cut into it.

The restaurant is vegetarian but pretty much everything can be made vegan, they are also able to make almost all dishes gluten free.

Service was on the slower side, drinks came out after starters. Be prepared to spend a small fortune here.

Spacious restaurant, small bar at the front with pricey cocktails which are good but once they get packed take forever to arrive after ordering. Friendly service and they explain each dish well as they arrive. Food was good, tapas style for sharing so for 5 of us we got about 10-12 dishes. Each dish comes out one at a time and not all at the same time. I was very full leaving but then got really awful heartburn for hours after. Not sure what happened but our practically vegan dinner did not sit well at all. Each of us had about 3 drinks with dinner and we also got 3 desserts to share and it was almost $800 with tax and tip. So be ready to spend!!!

Everything we ordered --
Green apple and sage collins: tastes like a very fresh pressed green juice
Oishii drop: a very yummy strawberry cocktail with a salt rim (had two of these)

Dosa for the table: really good and all the chutneys were on point
Smoky inari: a tasty two biter. We all liked this one
Crunchy saison battered black maitaki: also tasty
Dosa light and fresh: different style dosa, also tasty but the other one was better
Grilled oak wood shiitake
Whole roasted cauliflower: large cauliflower, nicely seasoned and roasted
Warm crimini carpaccio
Spinach spaghetti x2: very Al denté and filling
Mushroom walnut bolognese x2: liked this one and very similar texture and flavor to a meat bolognese. 
Creamy seared tofu

Chocolate cherry layer cake: very moist
Chocolate crème brulee: more like a custard or pudding and didn't have the sugar crust, very chocolatey
White sweet potato soft serve: my fave, really good
Plum sorbet: fresh and great palate cleanser and way to end the meal
Food lacked flavor and service was very inattentive. Definitely very overpriced for the overall experience
Vegan restaurant by Jean Georges. Food was pretty unique. Ambiance of the restaurant was clean and nice. Service was alright.

This is the second time I've eaten here and the experience was much better this time. I still feel like the tables are too close. I could barely fit between the tables without bumping into the table and couple seated next to us. The food came out very fast. We got all our food in 30 min we were done. Great and efficient but hardly a nice romantic dining experience. The waiter recommended we get 5 dishes as they're all meant to be shared bites. And they were really bites. We were hungry when we left. The pasta was definitely undercooked. I'm use to eating al dente pasta, but this was under. The spring onion in the mushroom dish were almost impossible to cut. I had to eat the whole thing at once. The salad was the best dish. The dressing was amazing. We also got a butternut squash purée which was delicious but my husband referred to it as our baby food course. Our server was really nice. Very great. Knowledgable and friendly. He checked on us many times. I still think it's odd to have the bathroom in the kitchen. 
The food flavors were all wonderful, I love the concept and the restaurant is pretty and has a great ambiance, but it's good for a pre dinner bite. Not for dinner. At that price point, to leave hungry is sort of ridiculous.

One of my fave restaurants in the city! The entire place is vegetarian and owned by Jean Georges. The plates are meant to be shared and are very gourmet. Healthy but very tasty and creative!

The ambiance is perfect for date night or a small dinner with friends. Service is also super friendly, and cocktails are amazing. Not enough good things to say about abcV. I always enjoy going back!

Came for a dinner for 2 here and the host sat us right away at a tiny table next to the wall. I had a large bouquet of flowers but he couldn't think of where he could put them and just stared at me with no solutions. Neither the coats, nor the flowers were able to be taken care of. Newsflash..winter is here so get a coat rack and dedicate some space for peoples belongings in this capacious restaurant. We ended up putting the flowers under the table. 

We had no utensils at the table even when our first entree came. Just seems like a bit of a chaotic place. The food is overpriced. The service is mediocre at its best. But I did enjoy some dishes. 

Battered maitake was great, especially the sauce underneath. Mushroom carpaccio was well executed. And I liked both the spinach and the bolognese pastas. Hard pass on the terribly sour kimchi fried rice. And the texture of the beats appetizer was as if it came prechewed. Cake was meh. Do I want to have an experience like this again? Not really. I know much tastier places with great service and a reasonable price tag. On to the next!

The theme of this review is good but small (that's what she said).

Came here before seeing Phantom for the last time in NY, unless it reopens at some point in the future.  That has nothing to do with this review, but I am still outraged by it and upset over it and I am sharing because you, my dear yelp readers, are my therapists.  Didn't you know?  Anyway, where was I?  Oh right, food.

We are always looking for new vegan spots and a vegan fine dining - or fine-ish dining, is a rarity.  We actually almost had our wedding dinner here, but eventually chose a more convenient spot.  Anywho, two paragraphs down and still nothing remotely resembling a review.  I'm goooood.

The restaurant is very nice.  Mostly white and clean and bright.  The menu is small dishes, meant for sharing.  Not for nothing, but shouldn't dishes to share be larger than a small dish?  If entrée size is for 1 person, than shouldn't food for more than 1 person be larger, not smaller?  Maybe it's me.  Maybe I'm just fat.

We started with the honey nut squash appetizer and I got the pomegranate mezcalita.  The drink was amazing.  Pricey, but the entire menu is pricey and it is NYC.  The squash was mashed and came with warm pita bread.  It was delicious, but it was way too small for the price.

I also got the mushroom walnut Bolognese.  This, too, was very good.  I don't know if it was a standout dish, but I enjoyed it.  And again, it was too small for the price.

I guess the point is that this restaurant is a very nice place to come if you want good vegan food but also want to leave poor and hungry.

Beautiful restaurant and with a menu full of yummy treats! The cocktails were a tad strong but definitely delicious and the food was great too. Portions could have been bigger considering the price and that they're meant to be shared, but taste was great.
One of my favorite places to go by myself because when I'm in my plant base mood I honestly don't want any distractions away from my taste buds they're very delicate, my taste buds.

It's been some time since I've been to an ABC restaurant (over 5 years ago) nor a vegan spot so was delighted to hear about abcV. Located inside ABC Carpet & Home, this restaurant offers a variety of vegetarian food. The place is very spacious and clean and does get super busy quickly. 
As soon as you walk in, you'll notice the open kitchen and the bar to the right, offering delicious drinks. Everything was amazing about this place starting from decor to the service provided by Adam. 
We had the following:
- Honeynut squash
- Crunchy gem lettuce and radish
- Beluga lentil (not my favorite at all as it lacked flavor; yam def gave it a kick though)
- Mushroom walnut bolognese
- Spiced ginger cake (wasn't a fond of it as I don't like ginger but my friend seemed to enjoy it)
- Pistachio mochi
Definitely a place to visit and a perfect spot to have brunch if you happen to be in the neighborhood.

Food is good. Cocktails are good. Place is cute. Wait staff is not good.

I went for a late lunch with a my sister (we're people of the global majority) and her chwyte boyfriend. The staff was friendly enough, but they were emphatically more attentive and personable with him. We ordered a lot, I paid, tipped handsomely, but they thanked him.

Now I don't care who they thanked as much as the blatant implicit bias. It was wild. Apparently Jean Georges restaurants have a preference for palm-colored folx, but just tolerate everyone else. For 2022, that's pathetic.

I don't have alabaster friends, so I  have no reason to return--not that abcv would even care.

I came here on a Saturday evening. I'm always happy to support a vegetarian spot, and this is worth the support. I went with a big group and we all got appetizers, entrees, and dessert - everything was excellent. The waitress was also very attentive. It is expensive, but it is worth it for a special occasion.

The cauliflower looks an alien brain from Mars Attacks.
The salad, a Marina Dunbar painted palette
The dosa, more like Ethiopian injera with unique sauces to dip into.

We had 1.5 dishes per person, 6 or 7 total, not a runt amongst them. But you might need a snack, or a vegan slider after, as its more tasting than stuffing.

Bring your daddy warbucks wallet and just empty it onto the table.

kudos to A, our excellent server, recommended us well, and also described and endless truffle selection that eve. didn't try, though. woulda had to sell the car.

Food was very good, but the service was pretty bad.  Before our drinks arrived, the food arrived. It was within minutes of ordering. The cauliflower was terrific, but slightly warmer than room temperature.  It obviously had been sitting under a heating lamp. Twenty minutes later our second entre arrived.  In between there was a bread plate with a chickpea side. The waitress hardly ever looked at our table. Waiters were removing food when it was obvious that we were not finished. If they took away the cauliflower, we would have had a long wait until our next course. After the second course the woman bussing asked if we were "still picking at it?" The restaurant is very noisy. The quality of the food, however, is high. All of our dishes, including the pasta Bolognese were very good.

I've been coming to abcV since it opened, and while I used to love it, it's gone downhill recently. In recent years, I'd give it a five star rating; based on my recent experience, I'd give it a one star rating; hence the average of a three star rating.

Last night, I ordered six dishes and only one was good (the dosa with chutneys). The charred white yam with tandoori masala, yogurt and tamarind was inedible - the flavors were so off I almost spit it out (and Indian cuisine is my favorite cuisine). The special entree -  kimchi rice - was okay but too tangy to eat more than a few bites. The spinach spaghetti tasted literally like the water from boiled spinach - the other flavors of preserved garlic and lemon and saffron were barely detectable. The black sesame ice cream didn't have the texture of ice cream and the flavor combo was weird to eat more than one bite (again, black sesame is one of my favorite flavors, so not liking this was a surprise to me). 

And I'm not some meat and potatoes kind of person who can't appreciate vegan food. I've been vegan for seven years and love the possibilities that plants  provide. But at this $$$ price point, one good dish out of six is lousy. 

I'm hoping it was just an off day in the kitchen and I will venture back in the spring when their menu has changed. Hopefully things will be back to normal!

Only got one thing for takeout but it was sooooooooo good.

green chickpea hummus- 5/5. Tastes different from regular hummus for sure, has a really unique taste and I love it. The veggies it came with were super fresh too

Maybe one of the best restaurant experiences I have had in the city. Exceptional service down to the waitstaff being very knowledgeable about the menu and specials including being very detailed about food allergies. The ambiance and vibe of this spot are incredible. We sat at a table very near the kitchen and were able to see the Cauliflower heads being cooked and plated. The kitchen window was a very unique aesthetic design element to the spot that we really enjoyed. 

The food was beyond my expectations. This is my third experience at a Jean-Georges restaurant and by far my favorite. The flavors in each of the dishes were incredible and each dish had elements of being the standout. Our favorite items were the Cauliflower Head and Walnut Bolognese. For a vegetarian restaurant, I was very happy the ideas for the dishes were clearly very thought through.

Definitely get the Hot Saffron Toddy, one of the best drinks I have ever had. Must-visit spot if you enjoy a unique dining experience, I will definitely be back.
We had a wonderful evening here. The food was amazing and the service was wonderful. I am not a vegan and it doesn't matter. It is simply delicious. The wait staff was so attentive.
Most amazing place for vegan food. It is a must try when in New York City. I personally love their burger and roasted cauliflower

The food was very very good and I would recommend it to anyone. We got lost to where the entrance was. A rude custodian by the name of George acted very creepy towards me by holding the door open.but other then that its been great

Undoubtedly the best vegan restaurant I've been to EVER. It always amazes me even more that all the dishes are raw vegan and so flavorful. They all have such elegant flavor profiles and divine presentation. The drinks are amazing! The service is amazing! Because I've gone a few times and have tried nearly everything on the menu I can't recommend a specific thing because EVERYTHING IS GOOD. Everyone is very kind and friendly the atmosphere is welcoming. I will share a few images but trust me when I say you'll enjoy anything you order here! The only thing I'm sad about is one of my favorite dishes they usually have was out of season for the current menu so I missed out on getting it again. Technically the seasonal menu just makes the experience more adventurous and surprising! Excited to visit again and see what they have in store

Janina was spectacular, incredible menu knowledge and very inclusive. They created an eating experience for me and my fiancé that left nothing to be desired. Janina is what should be desired in a server, never felt rushed, always felt like they're knowledgeable on EVERY item. Made this dinner ideal.

Janina 10/10.

I really wanted to like this restaurant more, but I left feeling kind of disappointed in my experience. Anytime I go to a city like NYC, I get excited about the abundance of vegan and vegetarian options. I had heard such good things about this place and decided to give it a shot. My sister and I had a reservation for 2 but last minute, a friend was joining us, so we had to cancel it. Unfortunately, on a Saturday night at 7 pm, they said the wait to dine inside would be quite long and the only seating they had was outside. After turning the heater on, which honestly did not help in the near freezing weather, and sitting in front of a view of trash bags on the street, we asked if we could wait for a table inside. After telling us no twice and us considering leaving to find somewhere else to eat, they eventually said that we could wait and they would have a table ready in 30 minutes. The wait ended up being closer to an hour and 15 min and every group was seated before us. The restaurant seems to be designed for pairs, which was why it must have been so difficult to get a table. We were seated at one corner of a table of 6 and a different couple was seated next to us. We honestly did not mind sharing our space at all! Due to the long wait, they brought us a complimentary honeynut squash with pita as an appetizer. It was a pleasant surprise! The squash was a good mix of sweet and savory and the mint made it taste really fresh. The pita portions were very small though. To start off, we got the crisp radicchio salad. I really loved the mesh of textures and flavors. The spiced avocado paired well with the fresh fruit, but the dressing was heavy on the garlic and ended up overtaking the entire salad. For entrees, we got the spinach spaghetti and the custardy tofu. The spinach spaghetti was bland, but the lemon upped the flavor as did the umami/tang from the gran kinara cheese. The custardy tofu was a very unique dish for me. It melted in your mouth. The broth was a little more sour than I was expecting, but it paired well with the coconut rice as suggested by the waiter. We were also given a scoop of delicious sorbet with a candle even though it was none of our birthdays! Overall, the service during the meal was good, the ambiance was nice, and the food is interesting/unique, but I don't think the experience was really memorable. Rate 3 stars for food and prices but add a star for the 2 complimentary dishes.

After sharing two appetizers, two entrees, and a dessert with my companion, I left ABCV underwhelmed--and a little hungry. The physical space is trendy, intimate, and comfortable, and our affable server was very knowledge about the menu; that is when we could find him. We dined on a busy Wednesday evening and waited too long for everything, including ordering.

With one or two exceptions the food was bland, skimpily portioned, and disappointing. We paid about $35 for a special pasta with morels that turned out to be something one might toss together when cleaning out a pantry. The only item I thought was notable was the set of avocado and lettuce wraps. Finally, the cocktails were tasty, but skimpy like the food. And we enjoyed our $92 bottle of Sauvignon Blanc--one of the less expensive wines on the menu.

Overall, not a terrible meal; the ambience is cool and the staff were friendly. I just found the food boring, paltry, and overpriced.

ABCV was way more popping than i thought. There were plenty of reservations available a week in advance but the restaurant was full on a Wednesday night.

The restaurant is pretty cool, a bit like an art studio vibes. It is a bit loud and some tables are closer together than others. 

Food/drinks:
-Cocktails were both good and really balanced. I got a mezcal maracuya(?) and loved it
-Dosa was great as well. Whatever mango/passion fruit dip that was was AMAZING
-the Beets made in a tartare style was decent. Needs to be mixed together to get all the flavors intended
-whole cauliflower was good, but I think it needs more tahini and topping. It's only covered at the top and there needs to be more topping/sauce for the middle/base that isn't exposed
-bolognese - definitely our favorite. It's great stuff!

Visited ABCV on Valentine's Day for a date night and I got to say, this vegan restaurant by renowned chefs, Jean Georges & Neal Harden, lives up to all the hype. I am not a big fan of vegan/plant based food but was completely blown away by the dishes we tried here, a total culinary experience: 
1. California dates with whipped coconut yogurt and tahini, pistachio, mint and lemon- an absolute delightful dish with unique ingredients, I could never imagine went so well with dates.
2. Dosa with sambal, mint and pear chutney. The pear chutney was my favorite and the dosa good too! Was so glad to see Indian dishes on the menu which didn't disappoint.
3. Mushroom walnut bolognese- this pasta was soul food. So comforting and rich. It came with mushroom sauce and every bite had the crunch from the walnuts. Thanks to our sever for her top recommendation!
4. Whole roasted cauliflower with turmeric tahini, za'atar, pomegranate, red zhug, fresh herbs & pistachio- the sauces in this dish were excellent! If I could, I'd ask for a side of each! Highly recommend!

We came here with a big group so we sampled several of their dishes. Definitely recommend and it's a bigger plus that it is vegan. 

Some of the highlights:
Dosa, figs, basmati rice, little gem lettuces

Personally, the desserts were the gems of the night and I loved the chocolate cake and the hazelnut mochi. The mezcal passionfruit cocktail was also delicious. 

Service was polite and prompt-- they definitely keep the courses/dishes going with no lag time in between. This is also the place that holds you to your reservation time and gives you warnings leading up to the end of your time!

We had a lovely meal of about 8 dishes for 4 people. The waiters were friendly and knowledgeable and maintained a good pace, bringing dishes one or two at a time. Some of our favorites were the dosa with chutneys, the radicchio salad with citrus and avocado, and the roasted shitake mushrooms. The beluga lentils were very tasty but quite acidic - we paired them with a side of sticky rice. The cocktails and nonalcoholic drinks were creative and well balanced. Overall, it was a very tasty and pleasant meal - but at this price, with plates of this size, I expect dishes to pack a bigger punch.

Worst meal I had in New York!  The dosa was awful (egg tasted weird) and dry (mine was the non yogurt), my companion ordered the other dosa with yogurt and avocado she didn't like it either.  She is not picky nor ever complains oh she did to me.  I don't like confrontation so we didn't say anything, I took two bites and that's was it.  My companion tried to eat it only was able to eat 1/4 of it.  How in the world can they be famous serving this junk!  We both were sick that night and the next day.  Stay away from this place !!!

Exceptional. The special pasta today was a bit meh while the asparagus was a standout as were the other dishes (we had a lot of the menu). Drinks were ok, they didn't have the one white wine I ordered but it's ok. Have the salads, the cauliflower, the silken tofu, I could keep going....
Great specials! Cozy atmosphere, great for a date night out or just a close family gathering. Would come back :)

We had a reservation, they kept telling us to wait 5-10more minutes. We were seated 45mins after the said reservation time. This didn't make any sense, because it's not like they had a line of people waiting to be seated, everyone waiting had a reservation, which makes me think they overbooked. 

And from the way the front desk/manager/servers were behaving it seemed this wasn't a one off scenario, like this happens to them quiet often. So they are used to it, and just following a robotic protocol - apologizing, giving us an appetizer for the "inconvenience" etc. None of which felt genuine. 

Food was good, or at the very least creative, which is why I am giving the two stars. But overall extremely disappointed by this place. We'll not be going back.

Best dining experience in NYC. Staff is welcoming, professional and well versed in what is being offered. Food presentation is perfection. Fabulous cocktails, extensive wine menu. Food & beverages outrageously delicious. Try at least one of their signature cocktails. Do your best to leave room for dessert. Perfection.

Great service, good food, okay cocktail. We ordered the roasted potatoes, avocado cup, mushroom burger and the dosa. Everything was fantastic. The cocktail I ordered was the rhubarb margarita, it didn't really taste like anything :(

They get points for creativity with the food but the service was atrocious. It took us literally an entire hour to get any food and even then, it was just a small thing of bread. Needless to say, we were starving. Drinks also took forever - both the first and second (like 20-30 min). 

For food, I was impressed I left fairly full given the lack of meat and was also impressed by the creativity of the dishes but sadly, none were particularly good to me. The best was the whole roasted cauliflower and the texture of the dosa (warning the chutneys are spicy), but everything else was blah, including the mushroom bolognese that people seem to rave about and the homemade tofu. 

Given the terrible service, lackluster food, and high prices, sadly would not recommend.
very different type of food, amazing flavors, meticulous plating! the restaurant decor is very clean and elevated, was a bit expensive but that's what you'd expect
Love this restaurant. Excellent vegan options -- and good wine by the glass list. Loving dining outside and people watching. Great location in union square.

Delicious food overshadowed by bad service.

First entree came out 10 minutes before our starters. Server was swapped at the beginning of the service. Second entree came out 30 minutes after the starters and 40 minutes after the first entree.
